On appeal the said judgment was reversed by the learned Additional District Judge, on a finding that the court of first instance erred in law in shifting the onus upon the defendant to prove that the plaintiff was not the grand-son of Gour Majhi and allowed the appeal on a finding that the plaintiff was never the grand-son of Gour Majhi, but was the grand-son of ptoly Majhi, brother of Gour Majhi and thus had no interest and was not a co-sharer in the partible land and as such he could claim 8 annas share thereof on partition. In that view of the matter, the impugned judgment and decree of the learned Munsif were set aside and the original title suit bearing No. 171 of 1969 was dismissed. As against that the plaintiff has preferred this appeal to this court. 

 5. In the instant suit there was no dispute that Gour Majhi was the original owner of property in question. There was also no dispute that there existed a person called Nagar Mondal the father of the plaintiff. The issue was whether the said Nagar Mondal was the other son of Gour Majhi and thus a brother of defendant No. 1 or a son of Keroly Majhi, brother of Gour Majhi and thus a cousin of defendant No. 1. The court of first instance in view of the pleadings of the parties framed Issue No. 3 thus: 

 6. It was framed so by the court as it was the duty of the plaintiff to prove that he  was a co sharer of the property in question in order to be entitled to ask for partition. To prove that co-sharer-ship of the property the plaintiff has also to prove that he was the co-owner and that he was a co-owner because he was an heir of the original owner. The law is that the person who pleads in the affirmative of the issues is to prove the same. In the instant case the affirmative of the issue was whether the plaintiff was the grand-son of Gour Majhi and thus a co-sharer of, the partible land. There is, therefore, no error caused by the court of appeal below in coming to the view that the onus was upon the plaintiff to prove by admissible evidence that he was the grand-son of Gour Majhi and thus a co-sharer of think property left by Gour Mjahi, which was illegally shifted upon the defendant by the court of first instance. A finding of fact arrived at by wrongly shifting the onus is erroneous and cannot stand the scrutiny of law. Only on this ground the finding of fact of the court of first instance is liable to be set aside.

parties:
Bashir Ahmed (Md) --------- Plaintiff-Appellant
VS
Nasima Akter and others Defendant ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Mannan, J: This appeal is directed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-1-2015 (decree signed on 5-2-2015), passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 88 of 2007, dismissing the suit. 

 2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this appeal, in brief, are that, one Mst. Harunnessa filed Title Suit No.88 of 2007, before the Court of the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur, seeking cancellation of deed No. 14863, dated 7-7-2004, and deed No.26390, dated 23-11-2005, as mentioned in the schedule to the plaint. 

 RS Khatian Nos. 56, 559, 206, appertaining to SA plot No.1573, corresponding to RS plot Nos. 2998, 2999, 3010, 3015, SA plot No.1540, corresponding to RS plot No.2995, in the Mouja of Dokhin Salna, Police Station Gazipur Sadar, District-Gazipur, belonged to the father and husband of the plaintiff's. After the death of her father and her husband she has inherited the entire disputed land and she was blessed by 1(one) son namely, Md. Bashir Ahmed and 2 (two) daughters namely, Nasima Akter (defendant No.1) and Samima Akter (defendant No.2). She had been possessing the suit land peacefully, but on 1-2-2007, she came to know that, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had taken executed and registered the disputed deeds, but she never went to the Sub Registrar's Office, nor had gifted the disputed 'land to the defendant Nos.1 and 2 and she did not at all deliver the possession of the said property to the defendants. The defendants collusively and fraudulently created and registered the impugned deeds and in spite of these two deeds, she was possessing the suit land with the knowledge of the defendants. On 1-2-2007, the defendants claimed the title in the suit land, on the basis of the said two disputed deeds and had denied her title in the suit land. Hence, the plaintiff filed the instant original Title Suit No.88 of 2007, seeking declaration for cancellation of the impugned 2(two) Hebanama deeds. 

 6. The defendant No.2 had contested in the suit by filing written statement, denying all material allegations narrated in the plaint contending intor alin that, the plaintiff was living under the care nursing of her 2 daughters (defendant Nos. 1 and 2) the plaintiff, being satisfied by their nursing and scare, she had voluntarily gifted the suit property to the defendant Nos.1 and 2, vide the alleged 2 Hebanama (deed of gift) and that she voluntarily went to the office of the Sub Registrar and executed and registered the Hebanama deeds and had delivered the possession of the suit land to the defendants and that, the defendants were possessing the suit land by erecting house and paying rent. The plaintiff had no right and title in the suit land. She had filed this case being influenced by her son Md. Bashir Ahmed. She prayed for dismissal the suit. 

 In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree dated 29-1-2015 (decree signed on 5-2-2015), passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 88 of 2007, is hereby set aside and the deed No.14863, dated 7-7-2004 and the deed No.26390, dated 23-11-2005 are hereby declared void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The judgment and decree of the lower Court shall be stand modified.

parties:
Memorandum of appeal from original decree and Md. Hasen Ali Matbar and others --------- Defendants Nos.1-6 & 8 appellants
Vs.
Md. Mohsin Ali and others -------- Plaintiffs-Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Mansur Alam, J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 28.03.2005 (decree signed on 04.04.2005) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 83 of 2004 decreeing the suit. 

 a) a decree for declaration of right, title and joint possession over the suit land; 

 The plaintiff-respondent filed this suit impleading the defendant-appellant Nos.1-8 alleging that his father died leaving behind his four sons namely Hasan, Mohsin (plaintiff), Akbar, Azgor and Roushon. Three daughters namely, Jamila, Aleba, Afia and wife Earun. These heirs had been possessing the suit land jointly. These defendant-appellants on 07.10.1998 claimed the suit land measuring .37 decimal disclosing that Amiruddin transferred the same to these defendant-appellants by way of the alleged wasiatnama deed. Thereafter plaintiff-respondent got the certified copy of the wasiatnama deed on 26.10.1998 and came to know the details of the deed. Father of the plaintiff-respondents did not execute the alleged wasiatnama deed and the suit land was never transferred to these defendant-appellants. This plaintiff-respondent jointly have been possessing the suit land measuring .37 decimal. The father of the plaintiff was never paralyzed or suffered from arthritis. He was also able to put his signature. He was found to do salish darbar in his locality. The defendant-appellants created this wasiatnama deed by way of forge practice. The plaintiff-respondent thus prayed for declaration of right, title and joint possession over the suit land since his right and title was clouded by the alleged deed. Also the plaintiff-appellant prayed for further declaration to the effect that the alleged wasiatnama deed is illegal, not acted upon and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff-respondents. 

 4. whether the plaintiffs has right, title and joint possession over the suit land ? 

 6. whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree, as prayed for ? 

 The learned trial Judge upon hearing the parties and on considering the evidence and materials on record by his judgment dated 28.03.2005 decreed the suit mainly on the ground that the plaintiff-respondent by adducing evidence became able to prove his right, title and joint possession over the suit land and also held that the alleged wasiatnama deed is illegal, not acted upon and not binding upon the plaintiff-respondent. 

 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.03.2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 83 of 2004, the defendant-appellant preferred this First Appeal. 

 Mr.Md. Khalilur Rahman the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellants in the course of argument takes us through the impugned judgment, plaint of the suit, written statements, deposition of the witnesses and other materials on record and then submits that the trial Court below without applying its judicial mind into the facts of the case and law bearing on the subject most illegally decreed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff-respondent have been able to prove his right, title and joint possession over the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court erroneously held the view that the impugned ‘wasiatnama’ is illegal, not acted upon and not binding upon the plaintiff-respondent. The learned Advocate in this context submits that the trial Court did not appreciate the evidences adduced by the defendants before the Court, the impugned deed though is a registered deed but it may not be rescined merely on basis of oral evidence of the plaintiff-respondent, defendant-appellant proved well that the father of both the plaintiff-respondent and that of the defendant-appellant Amiruddin was paralyzed and was suffering from arthritis, hence he could not sign of his own hand on the impugned deed, that the defendant-appellant submits that a medical certificate Exhibited as ‘Ga’ where it transpires that Amiruddin was suffering from cardio vascular accident with right sided hemiplegia with high blood pressure, that the learned trial Court did not consider the aspect that the relationship between Amiruddin and the plaintiff-respondent was not ever well, which caused execute the wasiatnama deed leaving plaintiff Hossain Ali aside. 

 The learned Advocate for the defendant-appellant further submits that under the provision of Muslim Law an wasiatnama in favour of the future heir/heirs if objected to by any heir shall not be binding upon him, an wasiatnama shall not be invalid or void in the eye of law, the trial Court failed to consider that one transferee of wasiatnama is a granddaughter namely Rojina Begum of late Amiruddin Matbar. This Rojina will get her portion of land cited in wasiatnama. Learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellant lastly submits that the plaintiff-respondent Mohsin Ali did not consent to that wasiatnama and the alleged deed might not be binding upon him, one transferee of the alleged wasiatnama is granddaughter of Amiruddin. So, she would not be left out of/ her share she is entitled, in this background the wasiatnama as a whole shall not be invalid or void in the eye of law. The learned Advocate for the defendant-appellant referred a case reported in 73 DLR(AD) at page 28 that a legal heirs would not be in any way deprived by rescinding the wasiatnama. But the legal heirs Rojina would get her portion if the alleged wasiatnama exists. As we found that the impugned wasiatnama is not executed by its transferor and the defendant-appellant is failed to prove its execution beyond any doubt. So, the defendant-appellant will not be entitled to get any relief in connection with the share of the legal heirs of Rojina. This legal heirs Rojina and other heirs of late Amiruddin have sufficient relief to inherit the property of Amiruddin as a co-sharer. So, on consideration of the above the cited decision is not applicable in this appeal. The learned Advocate for the appellant lastly prays for allowing this appeal. 

 Having heard the learned Advocates from both the sides and having gone through the materials on record including the impugned judgment of the trial Court. The only question that calls for our consideration in this appeal is whether trial Court below was justified in arriving at the findings that the defendant-appellant have been able to prove their wasiatnama to have been executed duly by its transferor Amiruddin, whether the alleged wasiatnama is liable to be set aside. Similarly the other question that calls for our consideration is whether learned trial Court rightly concluded that the impugned wasiatnama deed dated 18.01.1990 is forged, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff-respondent and whether learned trial Court rightly declared that plaintiff has right title and joint possession over the suit land. 

 The P.W.1 Mohsin Ali stated that Amiruddin Matbor was never paralyzed patient, he used to adjudicate in his locality, he can put his signature, he has been possessing the suit land with others. In his cross examination his testimony could not be shaken by the defendant-appellant. The P.W.2 Md. Abdus Sattar corroborated the evidence of Pw1 Mohsin Ali with regards to the claim of Amiruddin by the defendant-appellant. The Pw2 supported the version of the plaintiff-respondent’s case that the plaintiff-respondent has been possessing the suit land with other party and the relationship of Amiruddin with plaintiff Mohsin Ali was good. To cross by the defendant-appellant he reaffirmed that he met Amiruddin 5 days prior to his death at his rice machine. Both the witnesses on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent denied the suggestions of the defendant-appellant that Amiruddin could not put his signature or he executed the impugned deed by using his thumb impression or the plaintiff-respondent has no right title and possession over the suit land or defendant nos.1-6 had been possessing the suit land. 

 On careful perusal of the evidences and materials on record, we find that the plaintiff-respondent brought the original Title Suit No. 83 of 2004, for a prayer of declaration of title over the suit land and for a further declaration that impugned wasiatnama is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. It is admitted by both the parties that the suit land was belonged to Amiruddin, father of plaintiff-respondent and of defendant-appellant. The defendant-appellant claims that the suit land measuring .37 decimal has been transferred to them by way of impugned wasiatnama. So the defendant-appellant is to prove their claim. But on close perusal it appears that there was no any cogent ground to transfer the same to the defendant-appellant. The defendant-appellant though raises that the relationship between Amiruddin and plaintiff Hossain Ali was ill, but they could not adduce any tangible/substantive documentary evidence in this aspect. So, the contention of the defendant-appellant to the effect that Amiruddin transferred the suit land by way of impugned wasiatnama on account of his bitter relationship with Hossain Ali is not at all proved. 

 The learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellant argued that there is a transferee namely Rojina Begum, granddaughter of late Amiruddin is entitled to get her share in wasiatnama. He further submits that plaintiff Mohsin Ali did not consent to the execution of wasiatnama. So, in this background, under the provision of Mustim Law the impugned wasiatnama might not be binding upon him to the extent of his portion, but in no way, granddaughter Rojina Begum be deprived of her share. In this background learned Advocate for the appellant argues that the alleged wasiatnama, therefore be sustained for the interest of Rojina Begum. He further argues that learned trial Court on misconception of the provision of Muslim Law found that a Muslim cannot transfer more than 1/3 of his total property by way of wasiatnama and the defendant-appellant have not taken any steps to seek probate for the deed before any competent Court. Learned Advocate for the defendant-appellants argues in this context that for the reason of transferring more than 1/3 of the total property, the wasiatnama will not be illegal and probate for the Muslim is not necessary. Learned Advocate refers the relevant section of Muslim Law regarding this contention. But these questions will come up only where the execution of the impugned deed is proved. But from the above evidences and from the observation of the learned trial Court, the defendant-appellant have been failed to prove the execution of the impugned wasiatnama. So the subsequent matter, for example, the right of grand daughter of late Amiruddin, or the right of the consented party to the impugned deed or the consequences of the person who is not party to the impugned deed are not required to be determined here. 

 On meticulously perusal of the entire evidence both oral and documentary, it appears that learned trial Court rightly observed that plaintiff-respondent has been able to prove his right title and joint possession over the suit land by adducing sufficient evidences. The plaintiff-respondents right, title and joint possession has not been hampered by producing the impugned wasiatnama as the defendant-appellant has failed to prove its execution beyond any doubt. Therefore, we are constrained to hold that the impugned judgment of the trial Court below is not liable to be interference. The learned trial judge correctly and properly evaluate the evidence on record as to right, title and joint possession of the plaintiffs-respondent in the suit land and rightly concluded that the defendant-appellant by adducing evidence could not prove the execution of the impugned wasiatnama. 

 The impugned judgment and decree dated 28.03.2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 83 of 2004 decreeing the suit is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Asma Khatun and others -------- Appellants
vs
Md Abdul Karim and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts, for disposal of this appeal, in short, are that respondent No. 1 herein as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.166 of 1977 in the third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka (which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.22 of 2003) for specific performance of contract stating that the suit land measuring an area of 7 katha 9 chhataks of plot No.163A, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka was leased out to Abdus Sattar Bepari, predecessor of the defendant Nos.1 to 12 for 99 'years by the Government at a consideration of Taka 48,301 for construction of building. Out of the said amount, Abdus Sattar Bepari paid Taka 10,640 only and unpaid premium was Taka 37,661 which was to be paid by installments as per terms and conditions set forth in the allotment letter. Abdus Sattar Bepari, in total, paid Taka 19,908 by different installments till 21-1-1971 but he could not make any construction as per terms of the allotment letter due to his financial constraint. He was, therefore, looking for an efficient contractor to finance and supervise the construction. The plaintiff was a first class contractor and had intimacy with Md Ariff, one of the sons of Abdus Sattar Bepari. He agreed to invest in the suit land. Accordingly, a deed of agreement and irrevocable power of attorney were executed and registered on 2-2-1971 by Haji Abdus Sattar Bepari in favour of the plaintiff. Sattar Bepari received a sum of Taka 75,000 from the plaintiff as security money. The plaintiff was given possession of the suit land. Due to the war of liberation in 1971, the proposed construction work could not be done. Sattar Bepari also took loan of Taka 30,000 from the plaintiff. In this situation, Sattar Bepari, being unable to return the loan amount and unpaid portion of the lease money, decided to sell the suit land to the plaintiff at a consideration of Taka 1,08,000 with the liabilities. Accordingly, he executed an agreement for sale on 31-7-1971 in favour of the plaintiff and also executed a receipt acknowledging the payment of Taka 1,07,000 and handed over all original documents to the plaintiff. Due to his sudden death in August, 1971 Sattar Bepari could not execute and register the sale deed. He left behind defendants No.1 to 12 as his, heirs. It was stipulated in the agreement that Abdus Sattar Bepari would collect permission from the Government, income tax clearance and other required papers, and inform the plaintiff accordingly and, after payment of balance consideration by the plaintiff, he would execute and register the sale deed. After the death of Abdus Sattar Bepari, the plaintiff requested the defendants who initially assured him to execute and register the sale deed. Meanwhile, the plaintiff continued to pay installments of premium to the Government. He paid Taka 9,244 till 26-7-1973. All of a sudden, the plaintiff came to know that defendant Nos.1 to 12 are trying to sell the suit property elsewhere. Accordingly, the plaintiff served a legal notice dated 2-3-1976 upon the defendants requesting them to execute and register the. sale deed but they did not pay any heed to his request. Hence, the plaintiff filed the instant suit. 

 4. Trial Court, by its judgment and decree dated 28-5-2005, decreed the suit. Then the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.304 of 2005 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka, which was heard by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, who after hearing the parties allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and decreed the suit in part. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No.1725 of 2007 in the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which was made absolute. Thus, the appellants have preferred this appeal upon getting leave. 

 8. It was the plaint case that Hazi Abdus Sattar Bepari took lease of the suit land measuring an area of 7 kathas and 9 chhataks situated within Motijheel Commercial area being plot No.163A (South) by a lease deed dated 11-7-1962. Total lease money was fixed at Taka 48,301 to be paid to the Government. It has been admitted in the plaint that Abdus Sattar Bepari paid Taka 19,908 out of total consideration. It has further been stated in the plaint that till 21st January, 1971 he could not start any construction in the suit land and, thus, the plaintiff, being an enlisted First Class Contractor, came to an agreement with him to construct building. Accordingly, Abdus Sattar Bepari executed a Power of Attorney on 2-2-1971 in favour of the plaintiff. Estimated cost of construction of building was assessed Taka 3,54,770. He received a sum of Taka 75,000 as security money. He again took loan. of Taka 30,000 from the plaintiff and executed an agreement for sale on 31-7-1971 in favour of the plaintiff acknowledging the fact of payment of Taka 1,07,100 and handed over the original title documents to the plaintiff. It has further been stated in the plaint that Abdus Sattar Bepari died in the first part of August, 1971 (that is, within few days from the execution of the alleged agreement for sale) leaving the defendants No.1-12 as his heirs. In his evidence PW 1 has stated, “ ১৪ইং ডিসেম্বর/১৯৭১ হাজী সাহেবের তিনপূত্র মোঃ আরিফ, হাজী আলিফ ও আবদুর রউফকে পাক বাহিনী হত্যা করে।”  In paragraph 9 of the plaint, the plaintiff stated that he had paid a sum of Taka 9,244 through eleven challans till 26-7- 1973. He came to know that defendant Nos. 1 to 12 were trying to sell the scheduled land elsewhere ignoring the terms and conditions of the agreement for sale and thus, he issued legal notice. Receiving such notice, the defendant Nos.2 and 3, hiring some terrorists, tried to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land. He filed the Title Suit No. 209 of 1976 for permanent injunction and, at one stage, he got an order of status-quo. On 3-1-1977 defendants No.2 and 3 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land by force. It has further been stated in the paragraph 20 of the plaint that, on the date of execution of agreement for sale, the unpaid premium was Taka 26,393 and the plaintiff paid Taka 11,212 though in paragraph 9 he stated that till 26-7-1973 he paid Taka 9244 only. In paragraph No.23 of the paint, the plaintiff stated, That the cause of action for the suit arose first on 31-7-1971 the date of execution of the bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff by the predecessor of the defendant Nos.1-12 and thereafter with the expiry of 3(three) years on 31-7-1974 the period within which the contract was to be performed and thereafter on each date of demanded by the plaintiff to the defendant Nos.1-12 and lastly in March, 1976 when the legal notices were served upon the defendants, within plot No.163A Motijheel Commercial Area where the suit properties situated within the jurisdiction of Police Station formerly Ramna and now Motijheel and within the jurisdiction of this Court'. 

 9. In paragraph No.23, the plaintiff categorically stated that the cause of action of the suit arose at first on 31-7-1971 and, thereafter, on 31-7-1974, the period within which the contract was to be performed. Article 113 of the first schedule to the Limitation Act provides three years limitation (before amendment) from the date fixed for the performance, or if no such date is fixed, when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused. When date is fixed for performance of contract, the suit should be regulated by the first part of the Article 113 of the first schedule to the Limitation Act. In deciding the issue as to the application of first part, the Court shall take into consideration the surrounding circumstances as well. The case at hand does not fall in the first category of Article 113 of the first schedule to the Limitation Act because no date was fixed in the alleged agreement for its performance. Thus the case is .to be governed by the second part, that is, when the plaintiff has a notice that performance is refused. In paragraph 23 of the plaint, the plaintiff specifically stated that first cause of action arose on 31-7-1971 and as per first part of Article 113 of the first schedule to the Act the plaintiff was entitled to get 3 years to enforce specific performance of contract, which expired on 31-7-1974. We have found that the suit was filed on 29-7-1977. The expression "date fixed for the performance" is a crystalized notion. When a date is fixed it means that there is a definite time fixed for doing a particular act. The date fixed for the parties for performance of the agreement should be ascertained on the basis of terms and conditions of the contract. In a case, where no time for performance was fixed, the court had to find out the date, on which, the plaintiff had noticed that the performance had been refused by the defendants. For getting benefit of second part of Article 113, in paragraph 23 of the plaint, it was inter alia, stated, " …. with expiry of 3(three) years on 31-7-1974 the period within which the contract was to be performed and thereafter on each date of demand by the plaintiff to the defendants 1- 12…… " In his evidence, PW 1 said, “১-১২ নং বিবাদীগণকে আমি নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাবদ আমার বরাবরে সাফ কবলা দলিল সম্পাদনের জন্য অনুরোধ করা স্বত্ত্বেও তাহারা টাল বাহানা ক্রমে আমাকে ঘুরাইতে থাকেন।” The aforesaid portion of the pleading and evidence clearly indicate that inspite of repeated demand, the defendants did not execute the sale deed, That is, his approach to execute and register the sale deed was denied repeatedly by the defendants. It was the attempt of the plaintiff to get benefit of the second limb of Article 113 of the first schedule to the Limitation Act. In that case, it was the obligation of the plaintiff to state the definite date of refusal in the pleading which is absent in paragraph 23 of the plaint as quoted earlier. It is difficult for the Court to find the actual date to ascertain as to whether the suit was filed within three years or not or whether the plaintiff is entitled to get benefit of second limb of Article 113 of the first schedule to the Limitation Act or not. It is the spirit of law that suit was required to be filed within three years from the date fixed for the performance, in the event no date is fixed for the performance within a period of three years from the date when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused. Such specific assertion is absent in the pleading. Since the instant suit was filed on 29-7-1977 it is apparent that the same was barred by limitation. 

 12. From the amount paid as appeared from the office notes it appears to us that the same does not support the plaintiff's case as pleaded in his plaint, Moreso, the plaintiff did not comply with the terms and conditions of the alleged agreement for sale even if the same is accepted as genuine one. Non compliance of the mandatory condition itself disentitles the plaintiff from obtaining an equitable remedy for specific performance. 

 15. Specific performance of contract is an equitable and discretionary relief to be given by the competent Court exercising the same judiciously. To get relief it is imperative upon the plaintiff to prove that there was agreement for sale and consideration was settled and pursuant to the agreement a considerable amount was paid out of settled consideration, the plaintiff has already performed or was always ready and willing to perform the essential terms of agreement which were to be performed by him. The Court shall Judge the conduct of the plaintiff having regard to the entirety of the pleadings as to the evidence brought on records. The pleading and the evidence adduced by the plaintiff and the other materials on record raised a doubt about the talk of sale, payment of consideration, execution of bainanama, delivery of the possession of the disputed property and making construction in the suit land. Without taking any permission and even without making any prayer to the Government to get permission to transfer the suit land, the story of agreement for sale advanced by the plaintiff creates suspicion. Taking into account the fact that during the war of Liberation when every citizen of this country was afraid of saving his life and the fact that Haji Sattar Bepari died subsequent after alleged execution of "bainanama" and the admitted fact that his three sons were killed during the war of Liberation and having regard to the conduct of the plaintiff, we are of the view that the instant case was not fit case for exercising discretion for enforcement of contract and the plaintiff was not entitled to get any relief, the High Court Division has committed an error of law in not exercising its discretion judiciously and, thereby, erroneously made the Rule absolute.

parties:
Shamsul Haq (Md) and another ……… Plaintiffs-Respondents-Petitioners
vs
Chairman, No. 2, Chapair Union Parishad and others ……… Defendants- Appellants-Opposite-Parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015, passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No. 56 of 2015, allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008, passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 120 of 2004, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, are that, one Sharnsul Haque and Md Nazrul Islam, had filed Title Suit No. 120 of 2004, before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur, against the Chairman, No. 2, Chapair Union Parishad, Kaliakoir, Gazipur, and 44 others, seeking partition in respect of the suit property by way of allotting [5467/100] decimals of land out of 350 decimals, described in the schedule to the plaint. The pleadings of the plaintiffs need not be repeated, since these are maintained in the LCR and I have gone though the same. 

 4. It appears that, the plaintiffs has produced 6 witnesses namely, PWs 1-6 and also produced certain documents which have been marked as Exhibit 1 to 5, 5, 5(Ka), 6, 6(Ka), 7, 7(Ka), 8, 8(Ka), 9, 9(Ka). The certified copy of CS khatian No. 69 (Exhibit), 3 original title deeds (exhibit 2-4) and the certified Copy of the SA and RS khatian (Exhibit 5 and 6 series), respectively. Besides, Exhibit 7 is also an original deed No. 1767 dated 4-4-1994, Exhibit 7(Ka) to 9(Ka) are the signatures of the PWs No. 3 to 5, who are the deed writers. Having examined the order sheet of the trial court, I find that, the defendant, did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence. 

 6. Then, after expiry of 1,896 days delay, the judgment-debtor-defendant No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 56 of 2013 along with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, for condonation of delay and it appears that, the appellate court has condoned this inordinate delay and had admitted the appeal. Thereafter, by the impugned judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015 (decree signed on 14-10-2015, the appellate court has decided to remand the case to the trial court for ends of justice so that. the contesting defendant No. 1 get an opportunity to adduce evidence in support of it's claim and accordingly by the judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015, it has set-aside the judgment and decree dated 7-4-2008 of the trial court, passed in Title Suit No. 120 of 2004 and sent back the case on remand for allowing opportunity to the defendant No. 1 to adduce oral and documentary evidences. 

 8. Learned Advocate Mr Md Arshadur Rouf appeared on behalf of the petitioners. He having place the revisional application submits that, the defendant No. 1-appellant-petitioners appeared in the suit and had filed written statements and hearing of the suit continued on several dates and the plaintiffs had adduced as many as 6 witnesses and had proved all relevant documents, which were marked as Exhibit 1-9 series. He also submits that, the trial court, having considered oral and documentary evidences, was satisfied that the plaintiffs have proved the case and accordingly it had passed the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008. He next submits that, there was no error of law, nor the trial court has committed any error in passing the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008 and the same did not occasion any failure of justice. He proceeds on that, as per provision of  law, the plaintiffs has applied for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for making measurement and inspection of the suit property and as per prayer of the plaintiffs an Advocate Commissioner was appointed and he had submitted his report on 10-5-2009. But, the defendant did not file any objection against the said report of the Advocate Commissioner and the trial court had accepted the said report dated 10-5-2009 along with the field book, chitta, map etcetera filed by the Advocate Commissioner with his report, and passed the final decree on 10-11-2009. The learned Advocate further submits that, all these steps were taken by the plaintiffs and the final decree was passed in accordance with law. He proceeds on that, thereafter, the plaintiffs has filed Execution Case No. 1 of 2011 in the proper forum for warrant of delivery of possession in the suit property, as per their respective shares or saham. In the said Execution case No. I of 2011, the defendant No. 1 i.e. the Union Parishad had appeared by filing Vokalatnama and had prayed for time against warrant of delivery of possession, and their petition for time was allowed and, even after taking adjournments on 17 dates, the defendant No. 1 did not file any objection, nor it had filed any petition under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, against the ex-parte decree dated 7-4-2008 and, as such there was a delay of 1896 days and the said delay was condoned by the appellate court, as if it were routine, and it had allowed the appeal only on the ground that, the defendant No. 1-appellant could not adduce any oral and documentary evidence before the trial court, hence, for ends of justice, it should be given an opportunity to adduce oral and documentary evidence before the trial court and sent back the suit on remand, accordingly. The learned Advocate further submits that, the judgment and order of the appellate court is contrary to the provisions of law in as much as a case could not be sent back on remand to give any opportunity to either of the parties to improve its case. He also submits that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court was contrary to the decision reported in 1 MLR (AD) 1996 page 430 = 49 DLR (AD) 77: Feroz Alam and others vs Zobaida Nahar @ Zharna and others, which he read out. Besides, he proceeds on that, the appellate court has not at all record any circumstance that had prevented the defendant-appellant from adducing the oral and documentary evidence before the trial court in support of their case, inspite of filing written statement and he had asserted the fact that, the defendant-judgment-debtor had took time on 17 dates for filing written objection against the warrant to deliver possession, as recorded in the order dated 15-10-2014, whereby the execution case has been finally disposed of, vide the certified copy, annexed to the application for revision. He also submits that, the plea that the previous Chairman of the defendant No. 1 did not inform about Title Suit No. 120 of 2004 is a lame excuse and is totally false, unprecedented and unreasonable in as much as an Union Parishad is a local authority and has its permanent establishment to manage it's affairs. Therefore, the plea that the earlier Union Parishad Chairman was busy in his election, hence, he could not take any step in the suit or in the execution case are all simply absurd and not cogent grounds in as much as an election is a matter of personal interest of that Chairman candidate and it has nothing to do with the business of the Union Parishad. He further submits that, considering the matter in its totality and in view of the law laid down by the Appellate Division, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute. 

 15. Besides, the appellate court has not at all recorded any circumstance, to justify its order of remand, that bad prevented the defendant-appellant from adducing its oral and documentary evidence before the trial court in support of their case inspite of filing written statement. It is axiomatic that, the plea that the previous Chairman of the defendant No. 1 did not inform about Title Suit No. 120 of 2004 is totally false, unprecedented and unreasonable in as much as an Union Parishad is a local authority and it has permanent office and establishment to look after all its affairs and cases etcetera. Besides, the candidacy of the previous Chairman is matter of his personal interest and not of the public interest. 

 The impugned judgment and decree dated 8-10-2015, passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No. 56 of 2015, is hereby set-aside.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.42 of 2018
parties:
Golam Mursid Shahabuddin being dead his heirs: Ishrat Jahan Lipi and others ------ Petitioners
-Vs-
Abdul Hague and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the present respondent as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.22 of 2003 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Noakhali, for declaration that respondent No.2, Fulmati Khatun, wife of Sam Miah as the benamder of the land described in the schedule of the plaint. 

 6. In the said suit, respondent No.1, Golam Mursid Sahabuddin, added himself as the defendant by the order of the Court contending that the suit is false, fabricated and collusive and that there is no cause of action for filing the suit. Respondent No.1 contended that the present petitioner transferred 59.5 decimals land by way of Hiba deed in favour of Fulmati Khatun and said Fulmati Khatun transferred the land in favour of different persons by executing different deeds. Therefore, the plaintiff did not have any right and title upon the suit land. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, plaintiff as an appellant preferred Title Appeal NO.217 of 2006 in the Court of District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali, which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali and he allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trail Court. 

 11. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in considering that in the civil revision, no process was served on contesting defendant No.1, Golam Mursid Sahabuddin and process was fraudulently suppressed on him and Golam Mursid Sahabuddin died on 19.11.2011 leaving behind the present petitioners, but heirs of defendant No.1 was not fraudulently substituted and the judgment and order of the High Court Division was obtained against the dead person by practicing fraud and as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not well founded as original Title Suit No.22 of 2003 was filed for simple declaration that the suit deed was benami deed and defendant No.1 was Benamder of the plaintiff, but the suit for declaration as filed was not maintainable without prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and thus, the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, but learned Judge of the Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to consider these legal aspects to the case and thus, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in reversing the judgment of appellate Court below without controverting the findings of the appellate Court below and as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law as it misread section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure and decision cited by it. Defendant No.2, GM Sahabuddin filed the appeal against adverse remarks passed by trial Court against his title in case land and as he was aggrieved by some remarks against him, he had the right as per law to file appeal contrary to the finding of the High Court Division and as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division erred in law as it failed to consider that adverse remark against defendant No.2 passed by trial Court was unwarranted and not based on facts and law and the appellate Court below rightly and legally interfered and modified the judgment of the trial Court and allowed the appeal. 

 14. It is admitted by the parties that the suit land originally belongs to the plaintiff-respondent who acquired such proper-ty from his paternal-aunt by way of Hiba deed. 

 15. The plaintiff-respondent has come with an allegation before the trial Court that he executed Hiba-bil-ewaz deed being No.5563 of 1965 in favour of sister, Fulmati Khatun with a view to avoid the claim of dowry and maintenance by his first wife, Mrs. Feroza Khatun. It has been further alleged that in fact, defendant No.1, Fulmati Khatun (sister of the plain-tiff) his benamder (name lender) and she has got no right, title and interest in the suit in the land and as such, the plaintiff-respondent filed this suit for seeking a declaration to the effect that the Hiba-bil-ewaz deed in dispute dated 08.07.1965 is the benami deed and the plaintiff-respondent is the real owner of the land in dispute. 

 16. On the other hand, the present petitioner (added defendant), Golam Mursid Sahabuddin, added himself as the defendant by the order of the Court, claimed that the suit is false, fabricated and collusive and there is no cause of action for filing the suit The present opposite party No.1, also contended that the present peti-tioner transferred 59.5 decimals land by way of Hiba deed in favour of Fulmati Khatun and the said Fulmati Khatun transferred the land in favour of different persons by executing different deeds, therefore, the plaintiff did not have any right and title upon the suit land. 

 18. The plaintiff-respondent with a view to prove be fact of benamder has filed a certified copy of money execution case being No.08 of 1965 which has been marked has Ext.2 by the trial Court. It has been revealed from such Ext.2 that Feroza Khatun filed the original case against the plaintiff-respondent, Abdul Haqu'e, before the year 1965 and from such original money decree, this money execution had been instituted by Feroza Khatun for realization of money from the plaintiff-respondent. In this respect, it is the positive case of the present plaintiff-respondent that aforesaid Feroza Khatun was his first wife who sought for dowry and maintenance from him and on the event of denial, she filed this money suit claiming such dowry and maintenance from him. It has been further alleged that with a view to avoid the claim of his first wife, the plaintiff-respondent finding no other alter-native executed the Hiba-bil-ewaz dated 08.07.1965 in dispute in favour of his sister (defendant No.1). From Ext.2 certified copy of money execution case, it appears that money execution case being No.08 of 1965 was started in the same year when-ever the Hiba-bil-ewaz deed had been executed. Thus, it appears that the plea of executing such benami deed appears to be true. Over and above, the name lander, Eulmati Khatun (defendant No.1) appeared before the Court and filed a solenama admitting the fact that she is the benamder of the plaintiff in respect of such Hiba-bill-ewaz. In this respect, the trial Court in his judgment asserted in the following verbatim: - “১নং বিবাদী মোকদ্দমায় বাদীপক্ষের সাথে একটি আপোষনামা দিয়ে বাদীর দাবী স্বীকার করেছে।”
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Syurja Kumar Bepari and others -------- Petitioners 
vs 
Basudev others Biswas and ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 49 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-3-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Faridpur in Title Appeal No. 207 of 2006 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 15-8-2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Alfadanga, Faridpur, in Title Suit No. 133 of 2004 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The petitioner No. 1 and the predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 2-6 of the instant Civil Revisional application, as plaintiffs, filed original Title Suit No. 103 of 1985 for a decree of partition of the suit land in respect of RS Khatian No. 1063 and declaration of title about 4 annas share of the schedule land. Subsequently, the plaintiff-petitioners have amended their plaint with a further declaration that they have reversionary right in the suit land and the two sale deeds described in schedule `Kha' to the plaint are illegal, concocted, void, without consideration and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners, in short, are that the property described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint belonged to Ram Joy Bepari, Madhab Bepari, Tara Chand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari who were full brothers and all of them died before CS operation. Ram Joy died leaving behind his only son named Pitambar Bepari in 4 annas share, Madhab Bepari died leaving behind his only son named, Avoy Charan Bepari in 4 annas share, Tara Chand Bepari died leaving behind his two sons named Sadhu Bepari and Gostha Bepari in 4 annas share. Guru Charan Bepari died issueless leaving behind his only widow named Muktakeshi Bewa in 4 annas share as recorded their names in the CS Khewbat (Khatian) No. 15/1 of Mouza-Char Sultanpur. Thereafter, Avoy Charan Bepari died before RS operation leaving behind his only son named Sonatan Bepari, as such, his name was recorded in RS khatian operation in 4 annas, Sadhu Bepari died before RS operation leaving behind his only widow named Madhu Bala Dasya, her name was recorded in RS khatian in 4 annas, Pitambar Bepari died before RS operation leaving behind Jangli, Sarat Chandra, Prannath, Ghonesh Chandra, Nepal Chandra and Raghu Nath Bepari as his heirs, their names were recorded in RS khatian as per their shares. Muktakeshi died before Sonatan Bepari and Gostha Bepari and then Gostha Bepari died leaving behind his only widow Promoda Sundari and then Promoda Sundari also died on 27th Agrahayan, 1391 BS and before that, said Madhu Bala died leaving behind only Sonatan Bepari as her husband's brother's son as legal heir and lastly, Sonatan Bepari died leaving behind his two sons the original plaintiffs of this suit and in the way aforesaid the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing total 8 annas share in the suit land. 

 4. The property in question were sold in auction for arrear rents and one Manik Sarder purchased the land in auction. Said Manik Sardar Settled the same to Gostha Bepari who executed and registered a kabuliyat on 11-1-1945 in favour of Manik Sarder in respect of the suit land and then Gostha Bepari erected dwelling houses on a part of the suit land and possessing rest of the same by cultivating various crops: One Ganga Charan Biswas filed Title Suit No. 43 of 1995 in the Sadar Munsif Court, Faridpur against Gostha Bepari and others for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession. During pendency of that suit Gostha Bepari died leaving behind his only widow named Promoda Sundari who was substituted as his only legal heir. Promoda Sundari also contested the suit and it was ultimately dismissed. She acquired 1.92 acres of land as her life-estate. Promada Sundari lived with the help of the plaintiffs and with the income of the suit land and there was no legal necessity to sell the property and also she had no right to transfer the same. On her death, the plaintiffs have acquired the same as their reversionary right. The plaintiffs applied fire to the mouth of deceased Promoda Sundari (corpse) at the time of cremation and after 11 days they have performed her "Sraddha" ceremony. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the claim of the plaintiffs are false, baseless; the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit land; the plaintiffs are not reversioners and therefore, they are not entitled to file the present suit in that capacity; the defendants are bonafide purchasers for value without notice. Promoda Sundari sold the suit land in the year 1981 and 1984 for her legal necessity and to forfeit the loan of her husband, to offer food to the manes and also other obsequies of her deceased husband. The plaintiffs are not entitled to get relief as prayed for and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 2006 before the District Judge, Faridpur, Eventually, the said appeal was transferred to the court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Faridpur for hearing and disposal who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-3-2008 disallowed the appeal and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this juncture, the petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

 10. He further submits that in the earlier two judgments passed by the trial court rightly held that the petitioners are reversioners of the owner of the property Gostha Bepari and rightly held that the alienation of the property by Promoda Sundari was not for any legal necessity and the defendants in suit utterly failed to prove that the property was sold to them for any legal necessity. But for the third time the trial court wrongly held that the plaintiffs could not prove that they are reversioners of original owner by any evidence and the property was sold by Promoda Sundari for legal necessity. The appellate court though disallowed the appeal on the ground that the alienation of the property was for legal necessity of Promoda Sundari, but rightly held and found that the petitioners could able to prove that they are reversioners of original owner, Gostha Bepari. 

 12. Mr Abdul Bari with Mr Khandaker Aminul Hague, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 49 submit that the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their original plaint was replaced by subsequent amendment of plaint for several times starting from 1997-2004 and by bringing amendment of plaint introducing new facts basically destroyed the basic averments and statements of the plaintiffs made in the original plaint, as such, the trial court rightly observed and held that the plaintiffs on different times by bringing the facts inconsistent with each other could not establish their claim of reversionary right in the property and failed to prove that they are revisioners of original owner, Gostha Bepari. He further submits that the property in question admittedly, left by Gostha Bepari and acquired .by Promoda Sundari as her life interest and during her life time she transferred the property for legal necessity as stated in the recital of the deed and stated by the witnesses adduced on behalf of the defendants. It is also argued that the plaintiffs could not substantiate their claim that they took care of Promoda Sundari and maintained her expenses till her death or they incurred any costs for funeral of Gostha Bepari or his subsequent religious ceremony on their part, as such, Promoda Sundari for her maintenance and after the death of Gostha Bepari, for performing his various religious formalities transferred the property to the defendants. But the appellate court while disallowing the appeal though rightly held that the property was alienated by Promoda Sundari for her legal necessity but wrongly held that the plaintiffs could able to prove that they are reversioners of Gostha Bepari. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catena of cases Mst. Rahima Khatun vs Sree Monoranjon Saha reported in 13 MLR (HCD) 334, Matilal Sarcar vs Brajabashi Biswas reported in 12 DLR 142, Upendra Nath Mukherjee vs Gurupada Haider reported in AIR 1930 (Calcutta) 508, Golaka Chandra Nayak vs Gobinda Nayak reported in AIR 1996 (Orissa) 189, Mst. Sheo Kuer vs Nathuni Prasad Singh reported in AIR 1976 (Supreme Court) 709, Banga Chandra Dhur Biswas vs Jagat Kishore Acharja Chowdhury and others reported in XXI CWN 225 and Smt. Pramila Debbarma vs Smt. Gitasree Debbarma (Chakraborty) reported in AIR 1997 (Gauhati) 78. 

 14. From perusal of record, it appears that the suit was decreed by the trial court at the first instance by the judgment and decree dated 9-11-1992. The defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 324 of 1992 before the District Judge and the said appeal was heard and disposed of by the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Faridpur who by the judgment and decree dated 7-4-1997 allowed the appeal and sent back the suit on remand to the trial court observing that the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their plaint is not sufficient, giving an opportunity to cure the defect in that regard. After receipt of the record by the trial court, the plaintiffs amended their plaint on 12-11-1997 by introducing some facts and again amended the plaint on 28-6-1998 incorporating some facts and adding an additional prayer in suit. Thereafter, the trial court framed eight issues for retrial of the same and again decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 29-7-1998 on the findings that the plaintiffs are reversioners and Promoda Sundari transferred the property to the defendants without any legal necessity and also held that the suit property being agriculture land Promoda Sundari acquired no title. 

 15. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendants further preferred Title Appeal No. 239 of 1998. The said appeal was heard by Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, who allowed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 20-10-2003 and again sent back the suit on remand to the trial court with some observations made in the judgment. The appellate court again observed that fact of reversioner has not been properly substantiated by evidence and the trial court failed to observe that the property was sold by Promoda Sundari for legal necessity has to be gathered from attending circumstances. After arrival of the record, the case was transferred to the court of Assistant Judge, Alfadanga for disposal where it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 133 of 2014. Before the trial court the plaintiffs again amended their plaint by filing applications on 17-4-2004, 24-8-2005 and 11-5-2005 giving genealogy afresh with certain corrections. The learned Assistant Judge recorded evidence of the parties on recall and by the judgment and decree dated 15-8-2006 dismissed the suit on the findings and observations that the plaintiffs could not able to prove that Ram Joy and three others were full brothers as no PWs have witnessed them and nothing has come from the plaintiffs side to establish that they were full brothers and sons of a single person and secondly, held that the property was alienated by Promoda Sundari for her legal necessity and also held that admittedly, the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the property. 

 16. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court, present petitioners preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 2006 before the District Judge, Faridpur which was also disallowed on 30-3-2008. 

 20. From perusal of Exhibit-1, CS Khatian No. 15/1, it appears that in the title Column of khatian, name of Petambor Bepari son of late Ram Joy Bepari, Avoy Charan Bepari son of late Madhab Bepari, Sadhu Bepari and Gostha Bepari son of late Tarachand Bepari, Muktakeshi Bewa wife of late Guru Charan Bepari have been recorded. From the said recording, it cannot be construed that Ram Joy Bepari, Madhab Bepari, Tarachand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari were full brothers in the absence of any other evidences like their father's name or any other documents before CS record. Both the parties unequivocally admitted that the property in question was acquired by Gostha Bepari from the owner Manikial Bepari in the year 1945. Though the said facts were stated in the original plaint but subsequently, by way of amendment, the plaintiffs brought the fact on record that Gostha Bepari died leaving widow Promoda Sundari, SA khatian solely recorded in the name of Promoda Sundari for 1.92 acres. BS draft khatian recorded in the name of Ashananda Roy son of Pari Mohan Roy, the defendant No. 2 in suit measuring 1.20 acres who purchased the same from Promoda Sundari. Thereafter, Promoda Sundari again by a registered deed dated 25-6-1984 transferred 23 sataks of land to Sree Basudev Biswas and Sree Joydeb Biswas opposite party Nos. 1 and 49. 

 21. I have gone through the evidences of PWs PW 1 claims that the deed if there be any produced by the defendants are forged and false and in cross he stated that Deed No. 440 dated 26-5-1984 executed by Promoda Sundari for 23 sataks is valid and deed dated 22-8-1981 is invalid deed and by the said deed the defendant No. 2 did not acquire any title in the property and they purchased the property from Promoda Sundari without her legal necessity. He stated that his father died 30 years ago when the plaintiffs were minors and their father did not take any care of Promoda Sundari. They used to live in the house of their maternal uncle, 2-3 miles away from the suit property and they could not produce any document showing payment of rents for the property after or before the death of Promoda Sundari. He stated that he filed the suit for recovery of possession of 1.92 acres, but the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 purchased by two sale deeds only 1.53 sataks. Nowhere in the plaint or evidences the plaintiffs could state about the remaining land and he admitted that in original plaint they stated that Pitambar is one of the brother of Guru Charan, Avoy Charan and Ram Joy but subsequently, they claimed that Pitambar is son of Ram Joy and nephew of other three brothers. He also stated that Pitambar died leaving 3 sons Koilash, Jangli and another whose name is not known to him and he does not know Koilash died leaving whom and also stated that he did not see any of the heirs of Pitambar and does not know when they died. 

 23. From the evidences and prayers made in the plaint by the plaintiff, it is clearly established that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property. But 1.53 acres of land under the possession of defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 and in evidence, it has come out that out of the remaining land 14 sataks of land covered by plot No. 1866 is in the possession of Surandra Nath Mondal son of Akkhoy Kumar Mondal who has not been made party in the suit. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that they are in possession of the land other than the purchased land of defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 and could not justify why suit for recovery of possession has been filed against the defendant Nos. 1, .2 and 49 who purchased only 1.53 sataks of land out of 1.92 sataks. The trial court highlighted all those anomalies in the plaint, subsequent amendments, evidences both oral and documentary and found that the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their original plaint as well as by subsequent amendment after 17 years contradicts each other and no clear picture has been given about acquisition of title in the property as reversioner of Gostha Bepari and the trial court also found that in the absence of clear genealogy of acquisition of property by the plaintiffs as reversioners the plaintiffs claim cannot sustain in law. 

 26. The said recital of the deed have not been reverted in any manner by the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners by any evidence either oral or documentary that Promoda Sundari before alienation of the property earlier transferred any other property or she has other source of income or she took help from any relative other than the plaintiffs or the plaintiffs used to maintain her till her death. It is true that the fact of legal necessity has to be proved by the purchaser. The power of a Hindu female to alienate property are wider in respect of acts which conduced to the spiritual benefit of her deceased husband. The widow is entitled to sell the property even the whole of it if the income of the property is not sufficient to cover the expenses for such acts. In the present case the recital of the deed indicates legal necessity in different way; such as, spiritual benefits of her deceased husband, payment of debts and maintenance of the widow. In the absence of any other reliable evidences it can be easily inferred that the property was alienated by the widow of Gostha Bepari for legal necessity. The defendants, as purchaser of the property had obligations to prove legal necessity but in the instant case the plaintiffs in one hand could not establish and prove by any evidence that Promoda Sundari had no legal necessity to transfer the property in question and on the other hands the recital of the deed discloses some legal necessity which has to be construed liberally. The recital is clear evidence of the representation and if the circumstances are such as to justify a reasonable belief that an enquiry would have confirmed its truth, then when proof of actual enquiry has become impossible, the recital coupled with such circumstances would be sufficient evidence to support the deed. To hold otherwise would result in deciding that a title becomes weaker as it grows older, so that a transaction perfectly honest and legitimate when it took place would ultimately incapable of justification merely owning to the passage of time. Both the courts below concurrently observed and held that the widow of Gostha Bepari, Promoda Sundari had no other alternative for her livelihood. Being a widow it was necessary for her survival to alienate the property left by her husband.

parties:
Chairman, Khulna Development Authority, KDA Building, Jessore Road, Khulna Sadar, Khulna ----------- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner
VS 
Kalimata Bigraha and another ---------- Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 293 of 1993 upholding the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1993 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna Sadar, Khulna in Title Suit No. 53 of 1987 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts give rise to the issuance of Rule in a nutshell are as follows: The present-opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the Original Title Suit being No. 53 of 1987 for a decree of perpetual injunction restraining the defendant, Khulna Development Authority (here in after KDA) from entering into the suit property forcefully and demolishing the "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" situated in the suit land contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to mouja Baniakhamar under Police Station Sonadanga of District Khulna within KDA Mazid Saroni in Plot No. A-45 measuring an area of 6.000 square feets is being used as "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" managed by a committee, on behalf of the Hindu community to perform their religious functions. In the suit property "Sree Sree Kali Mata Bigraha" has been established in hundred years back by the people of Hindu community, who were performing puja and other religious functions from the very beginning. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that for the purpose of puja and other religious functions an executive committee was formed in which the plaintiff No. 2 is Secretary. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that, as a place of worship, the Hindu community is regularly performing their religious programmers peacefully in the suit premises for more than hundred years and at this stage, KDA wanted to acquire the suit property illegally and tried to demolish the "Mondir" situated within the suit premises. In the suit premises besides the deity Kali, the other deities like "Durga" and others are standing and there is a boundary wall of the premises, but the defendant out of ill motive, giving threatening to the devotees, trying to dismantle the "Mondir" forcefully in the name of acquisition of the property for their so-called development work and as a result, finding no other alternative; the plaintiffs instituted the original suit for permanent injunction. 

 3. On the other hand, the case of the contesting defendant No. 01, KDA in short is thus, that the suit property has been acquired by KDA and the KDA gave compensation to the original owners of the property. The further case of the defendant-petitioner is such that, after acquisition of the property they have taken vacant possession of the land-in-dispute, which is a commercial Plot being No. A-45 measuring 6 (six)-kathas of land and has been leased out in favour of one Sheikh Ashraf Ali. The other Plot No. A-46 measuring the same quantum of land has been leased out in favour of one Kamruzzaman and the lease-holders are possessing the property. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1993 and 7-6-1993 respectively. 

 5. Being aggrieved the defendant preferred a Title Appeal being No. 293 of 1993 in the court of learned District Judge, Khulna which was transmitted to the 1st Court of the learned the then Subordinate judge, Khulna for hearing and disposal and the learned Appellate Court hearing the appeal disallowed the same affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 and 1-10-1995 respectively. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that, the learned trial court as well as the learned Appellate Court committed illegality and irregularity during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff No. 2 applied for allotment of the suit land to them as it was acquired by KDA and thereby the plaintiffs are stopped from filing the suit against the defendant. The learned Advocate also submits that the suit is barred by Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 but the learned trial court as well as the learned Appellate Court failed to appreciate the law and without realizing the facts and circumstances of the case erroneously decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal in favour of the plaintiffs and, as such, the Rule is liable to be made absolute. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that, neither the trial court nor the appellate court committed any illegality or infirmity in deciding the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs have acquired valid, right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by way of adverse possession for more than hundred years, which is being used as "Puja Mondir". The learned Advocate also submits that inasmuch as the suit premises is a place of worship of the Hindu community at the locality, there was no scope for requisition of that property by KDA and the land-in-dispute can not be vested to the Government by any proceedings. The learned Advocate submits that the people of the locality from the ancient time are performing their religious functions in the suit premises, which is commonly known as "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" and in the suit premises there is a Kali deity and other deities & these are being used for various religious activities of the Hindu community. The learned Advocate argued that the property is out and out such a property which is being used for religious functions including "puja" and other related affairs of the Hindu community. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned trial court at the time of disposal of the original suit rightly after proper assessment of evidence in its true perspective arrived at a conclusive decision as to the nature and character of the suit property and accordingly, decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and subsequently, the Appellate Court also at the time of disposal of the appeal on proper appreciation of law, evidence and factual aspects of the case decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the respondent therein, and there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

 10. In order to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocates, on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 passed in Title Appeal No. 293 of 1993 along with the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court dated 31-5-1993 in Title Suit No. 53 of 1987 including all other relevant papers and the evidences adduced from the sides of the respective parties, it transpires that the plaintiffs to the original suit in order to obtain a decree of perpitual injunction restraining the defendant, KDA from entering into the schedule property forcefully and dismantling the standing "Kali Mondir" of the suit property filed the original suit and going through the plaint, I find that it is the specific contention/case of the plaintiffs that "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" represented by the secretary, Shib Bari Sarbojanin Puja Committee, Khulna that the suit property is being possessed by the Hindu community of the locality as 'Shib Bari Kali Mondir' for years together, which is more than hundred years. It was further contended by the plaintiff-opposite parties in their pleadings that in the suit property, there is a deity "Sree Sree Kali Ma ta Bigraha" and "Durga" with other bigrahas and the Hindu community of the locality use to perform their religious activities regularly in that "Mondir" and in the year 1947 during partition the persons engaged in looking after and managing the "Mondir" left this country and in respect of the ownership of the property, due to the ignorance of the local Hindu community, no paper was obtained or record of right was prepared, but the facts remains that the local Hindu community without any disturbance or objection from any corner, use to possess the suit premises as before, for more than hundred years openly and adversely within the knowledge of all, including the defendant, petitioner, KDA. It is the positive case of the plaintiffs that the defendant-petitioner have no authority in the suit premises, but only to grab the property in the name of requisition through Additional Deputy Commissioner, Khulna sent an office memo being No. 3421 dated 10-6-1982 illegally for making a decision after consultation with the local Hindu community, but without taking decision there under, all on a sudden, on 5th Falgun of 1393 BS the defendant through their officials tried to destroy the "Shib Bari Kali Mondir" touching the religious sentiment of the Hindu community, causing serious difficulties to that community, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for permanent injunction. It was asserted by the plaintiffs that, there is an apprehension of imminent criminal breach of peace in the locality with regard to the suit premises due to the activities of the defendant KDA. 

 11. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest which was subsequently affirmed by the appellate court. 

 13. Consulting the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties it further transpires that, the defendant-petitioner during trial of the original suit submitted an official gazette marked as Exhibit-"Ka" which is not specified for specification of the suit premises and its area. Besides this, the gazette notification is with regard to an Enrollment Case No. 12086 with reference to a Waqf Estate, which is a third case. From the documentary evidences filed by the defendant, I also find that the paper which is furnished from the side of the defendant-petitioner vide Exhibit-"Gha" is a proposed plan, showing a map including the cost of a project, and it is not identical with the suit property. 

 The impugned judgment and decree dated 25-9-1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 293 of 1993 upholding the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1993 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna Sadar, Khulna in Title Suit No. 53 of 1987is hereby affirmed.

parties:
BANKIM CHANDRA BALA
VS.
ABU SAYED AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 10.03.2013 and 14.03.2013 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 214 Court, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No.10 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.11.2001 and 05.01.2002 respectively passed by the learned. Assistant Judge, Chitalmari, Bagerhat in Title Suit No.51 of 1998 decreeing the suit in part should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor of the present respondent-opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No.51 of 1998 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Chitalmari for partition, contending inter alia, that one Narayan Chandra Bala was the recorded tenant in S.A. khatian No.125, under Mouza. Khoromkhali of Chitalmari Upazila under Bagerhat District along with his other co-sharers in the suit holding in 50% share comprising an area of 2.01 acres of land. He was also a recorded tenant in 3/4 share comprising an area of 1.78 acres of land in S.A. khatian No.I99 of the same Mouza. The father of Narayan Chandra namely Bhaggya Dhar Bala during his life time obtained 0.52 acres of land in plot No.202 appertaining to C.S. khatian No.73 corresponding to S.A. khatian No.201 and 299 from a recorded tenant of the suit holding one Malek Mia and others. Thereafter, the father of the plaintiffs erected his dwelling but on 0.52 acres of land and subsequently died leaving behind his son Narayan Chandra Bala. During peaceful possession of the plaintiffs while one Darikanath Bala tried to dispossess the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs filed a civil suit which was decreed in favour of the plaintiffs up to the appellate court. In the subsequent record of right the land of plot No.202 of C.S. khatian No.73 while not recorded in the name of Narayan, he filed a suit being Title Suit No.285 of 1985 and during pendency of that suit he died leaving behind two sons Bankim Chandra Bala and Suklal Bala. Bankim Chandra in the aforesaid suit alleged that he is the sole successor of his father Narayan Chandra Bala. At the death of Suklal, Bankim Chandra did not substitute the heirs of Suklal. Subsequently, Bankim Chandra by a registered sub-kabala dated 20.06.1990 transferred 0.16 acres of land from plot No.201 and .06 acres of land from plot No. 197 of S.A. khatian No.199 and 0.10 acres of land from plot No.202 of S.A. khatian No.201/299 measuring the total land 0.12 acres in favour of the plaintiffs and delivered possession therein. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that Suklal transferred 0.25 acres of land of the suit holding in favour of one Moazzem Hossain and Moniruzzaman by a registered kabala dated .24.11.1985, who subsequently transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs by a registered transfer deed dated 15.06.1988. In this way; the plaintiffs after acquiring right, title, interest and possession in the land measuring 0.50 acres by a mutation proceedings mutated their names and opened a separate khatian being No.199/1.
