The further case of the plaintiffs is such that Suklal by a kabala dated 12.04.1997 transferred 0.26 acres of land from suit plot No.202 in favour of the plaintiffs and thereafter the plaintiffs acquired in all 0.86 acres of land in the suit holding and Civil Suit being No.59 of 1997 which was filed against the decree of Title Suit No.285 of 1985 was dismissed for default and that the defendant No.1 created a false nadabi-paira from Suklal on 16.10.1997 and that due to the difficulty of ejmali possession with the defendants the plaintiffs requested the defendants for amicable partition but they refused, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for partition in respect of 0.86 acres of land in the suit holding. 

 3.The contrary case of the defendant No.1, who contested the suit and who is the petitioner of this revisional application in short is thus that he is the sole successor in interest of the recorded tenant Narayan Chandra Bala and Suklal never executed any kabala on 12.04.1997 and also not filed Title Suit No.59 of 1997. The further case of the defendant-petitioner is such that by way of false personification the aforesaid kabala deed was obtained and the defendant by a transfer deed dated 20.06.1990 transferred 0.16 acres of land from plot No.251 and 0.06 acres of land from plot No.196 measuring 0.22 acres in all, and the plaintiffs fraudulently inserted the land which is the homestead property in the kabala and that the defendant never delivered possession to that land from suit plot No.222 and the defendant-petitioner did not take any consideration money for the aforesaid land from the plaintiffs. Against that kabala dated 20.06.1990 the defendant has filed a Title Suit No.82 of 1998. It is the case of the defendant-petitioner that the plaintiffs are possessing only 0.22 acres of land in the suit holding. 

 4. During trial of the original suit the learned trial court after framing 05(five) different issues decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiffs and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs to the extent of 0.73 acres of land in the suit holding by the judgment and decree dated 29.11.2001. 

 5. Being aggrieved the defendant-petitioner preferred a Title Appeal being No.10 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge, Bagerhat, which was transmitted to the 2nd Court of learned Joint District Judge, Bagerhat for hearing and disposal and the learned appellate court hearing the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree dated 10.03.2013 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed illegality in holding the view that the suit is liable to be decreed. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit was bad for defect of party, but neither the trial court; nor the appellate court dismissed the suit on the ground that the suit suffers from defect of party. The learned Advocate argued that, with regard to the defect of party the witness No.1 of the plaintiffs in his deposition admitted that there are some necessary parties, who are left out from the plaint. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendant-appellant-petitioner categorically alleged in his pleading that in the kabala deed dated 20.06.1990 the plaintiffs fraudulently included 0.10 acres of land which is a homestead in plot No.202 and against that fraudulent kabala deed the defendant has filed a Title Suit being No.82 of 1998 and for that, the defendant-petitioner prays for calling the volume book of the concern kabala deed for comparison. The learned Advocate during hearing of the Rule has submitted for additional evidence and lastly submits that for the reason mentioned earlier both the courts below erred-in-law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be interfered with. 

 9. In order to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocate having gone through the judgment and decree passed by the trial court as well as the Appellate Court and the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and all other relevant papers including the case records I find that, admittedly the suit land along with other property originally belonged to Narayan Chandra Bala and it transpires that Narayan Chandra died leaving behind two sons Bankim Chandra Bala and Suklal Bala who inherited the property left behind their father. 

 10. Consulting the relevant papers it also transpires that the petitioner's case is such that his full brother Suklal Bala executed a nadabipatra in his favour and Bankim Chandra by dint of this paper claimed his exclusive title and interest in the suit land and claimed him the sole successor-in-interest of Narayan Chandra Bala. The learned Appellate Court with regard to this rightly appraised the legal aspect that a nadabipatra as alleged does not create or extinguish any title and interest in favour of anybody in respect of property. It is found that from a kabala deed dated 24.12.1985 which has been marked as Exhibit-3 and the kabala deed dated 15.06.1988 (Exhibit-8) the plaintiffs have become co-sharers in the suit holding to the extent of .0.21 acres of land in plot No.201 and 199 and 0.04 acres of land in plot No.196. 

 11. Both the parties to the suit, to substantiate their respective claim have adduced witnesses and the plaintiffs have examined 05(five) witnesses and submitted their basic documents marked as exhibits. On the other hand, the defendant-petitioner has examined 03 witnesses in support of his case and submitted some documentary evidence, which are also have been marked as exhibits by the learned trial court. It is the concurrent findings and decisions of both the courts below that in the lands of S.A. khatians No. 201, 299, 199 and 125 the predecessors of the parties have got their interest and title: In the land measuring 1.78 acres the predecessor of the parties namely Narayan Chandra had 1.1866 acres of land corresponding to S.A. khatian No.199 and two sons at the demise of their father acquired .59333 acres of land. It further appears from the observation and findings of the courts below that the learned trial court under the ambit of section 73 of the Evidence Act, 1872 compared the signature of Suklal Bala and scrutinized the signature with the registered sub-kabala deed dated 24.12.1985 with the signature as it appears in kabala deed dated 12.04.1996' which has been marked as Exhibit-5 and after comparison of the signatures, conclusively held that the signatures as it appears with the deed under challenge in Title Suit No.82 of 1998 is the product of same individual and it is decided concurrently by the trial court as well as the Appellate Court that the allegation of forgery as raised from the side of the defendant-petitioner is not proved by any tangible evidence and as a result the plaintiffs to the suit obtained 0.26 acres of land in the suit plot No.202 by virtue of the kabala deed dated 12.04.1997 and the plaintiffs have succeeded to establish their plaint case by cogent evidence and that they have title and possession to the extent of 0.22 acres of land in suit plot No.197 and 201 by the purchase deed dated 20.06.1990. 

 12. Having gone through the evidence on records I find that P.W.1 Md. Amir Ali, who is the predecessor-in-interest of the present opposite parties No.1-4, testified in support of their pleading. During his deposition he testifies at a stage that the Bankim Chandra Bala without including his brother instituted Title Suit No.56 of 1997 alone, which was subsequently decreed. It was further testified that for the reason stated above, the decree was not enforceable against Suklal Bala, the brother of Bankim Chandra Bala. This witness purchased 83 decimals of land from the heirs of Suklal and Bankim. He also purchased 32 decimals of land from Bankim Chandra on 20.06.1990. P.W.1 in his deposition testifies at a stage that he requested the defendant on 15.07.1998 for amicable partition, but the defendant denied. P.W.1 in his cross-examination testified at a stage that they did not include one Kalidas, Debdas, Horish Mokter Shekh and Ashok Roy in their suit. This witness also testified that one Choitanyo and Sumanta Tarafder are not parties. 

 15. P.W.4 Montanzir Hossain is a Bank Emplyee who as per direction of the Court has brought a deed dated 15.06.1988 which was submitted in their bank for obtaining loan as mortgage and the plaintiff Amir All mortgaged that deed and obtained loan from the bank. This witness compared the photocopy of the deed with the original, which has been marked as Exhibit-8. 

 17. Vis-à-vis; the D:W.1 of the defendant, who is the defendant No.1 himself Bankim Chandra Bala in his testimony testified that he is the defendant to the suit and the total land of plot No.232 of the C.S. khatian No.73 consists of 52 decimals originally belonged to one Abdul Goni and Bhaggya Dhar was a tenant under him. This witness testified in support of his written statement. 

 18. During cross-examination the defendant Bankim Chandra conceded that Narayan Chandra died leaving behind 02 sons, he (D.W.1) and Suklal at the time of death of Narayan Chandra were in India. This witness further admitted that at the death of their father, in Title Suit No.285 of 1985, he (D.W.1) claiming himself the only heir of Narayan Chandra substituted. This witness in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiffs testified that, he cannot say as to what date Suklal went to India and he (D.W.1) will not be able to produce any lawful paper to substantiate that Suklal migrated to India. 

 22. On meticulous assessment of the evidence on records along with other materials to the original suit I find that the courts below with regard to possession of the property rightly held that, in a suit for partition constructive possession is enough and possession of one co-sharer amounts of possession of all the co-sharers of the suit holding. 

 23. Apart from this; from the testimony of the witnesses it transpires that the plaintiffs to the suit in order to succeed in their case examined their witnesses as stated above, who were thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the defendant and from the trend of their cross-examination as well as from their testimonies, no such material contradiction, omission or ambiguity is noticed by which it can be held that the plaintiff's witnesses are not competent, trustworthy or credible. The courts below concurrently in their findings arrived at a decision that the plaintiffs to the suit by sufficient tangible evidence have been successfully discharged' their onus in proving their title and interest to the extent of 0.73 acres of land in the disputed holding pursuant to their three title documents marked as Exhibits-4, 5 & 8. With regard to left out parties to the suit it was observed by the learned courts below that the plaintiffs has no claim against the recorded tenants who has been left out from the plaint of the plaintiffs and there is no chance from the side of the contesting defendant No.1 of prejudice, in absence of the persons who were not included as party to the suit. The persons in whose presence an effective and proper adjudication into the matter-in-dispute is possible, they are already on record inasmuch as they have been made party to arrive at an efficacious relief to the parties. 

 26. In our revisional jurisdiction, where glaring in consistency with the evidence on records is noticed and where it appears that there has been misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, in that case only this Court invoking its revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is entitled to exercise this jurisdiction to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the learned courts below. Otherwise, the Appellate Court being the final court of facts, the judgment and decree passed by this court is immune from interference. 

 29. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The judgment and decree dated 10.03.2013 and 14.03.2013 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No.10 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.11.2001 and 05.01.2002 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chitalmari, Bagerhat in Title Suit No.51 of 1998 is hereby 'affirmed.

parties:
Md. Rafique and Others
Vs.
Sayed Md. Abdul Quiyum being dead his heirs: Mst. Rokeya khatun and others
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.11.2014 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.19 of 2013 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.01.2013 and 20.01.2013 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka in Title Suit No.34 of 2011 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original title suit being No.34 of 2011 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka for declaration of title along with a prayer for cancellation of a deed and perpetual injunction contending inter alia, that the disputed property appertaining to Mouza Khilgaon in C.S. Plot No.10P was the property under the government as abandoned property and the government decided to settle the land in favour of private individual. Accordingly, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff Fakir Chand pursuant to his prayer for taking permanent settlement was obtained allotment of the suit properties which was in fact initially acquired by the government in L.A. Case No.47 of 1959-60 and 11 of 1960-61. The predecessor of the plaintiff Fakir Chand obtained allotment on 02.11.1961 in respect of 02(two) kathas 07(seven) chhatak land of plot No. A-627(F) and 628(P) from the office of the concerned Executive Engineer, Public Works Department (PWD) followed by an allotment latter being Memo No.8059 (RDD) dated 02.11.1961. That the possession was delivered in favour of allotment-holder on 08.11.1965. Fakir Chand under the terms and conditions of the latter of allotment for obtaining a lease deed erected a tin-shed but on the suit property in the year 1965 and used to possess that homestead as of his dwelling hut. The further case of the plaintiff is such that Fakir Chand possessed the property through his caretaker and expired before 24/25 years. At his death; his two sons the plaintiff No. l and 2 one daughter, the plaintiff No.3 and one wife the plaintiff No.4 and mother of plaintiff No. 5 and 6 Halima Khatun became the heirs. The father of the plaintiff No.5 and 6 namely Rustom Ali as caretaker of the property used to look after the property. Rustom Ali while became bed ridden due to his paralysis disease, his wife Halima Khatun along with other plaintiffs use to possess the same in ejmali. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the father of the defendants No.1-4 Altaf Hossain who was very much familiar to Rustom Ali Khan was allowed to possess the suit property without rent after the death of Altaf Hossain. The defendants No.1-4 concealed the original papers of the plaintiff. The government on 25.02.1982 executed and registered a lease deed being No.4643 in the name of Fakir Chand when Fakir Chand was already expired. The plaintiffs requested the government officials to register the lease deed in favour of them; but the office of the defendant No.7 disclosed before them that the lease deed has already been executed and registered in favour of their predecessor Fakir Chand. On 07.03.2010 the plaintiffs finding a sign board in the name of the defendant No.5 in the suit property they inquired into the matter and came to learn that the mother of the defendants No.1-4 Umme Salma Akter Khatun as am-mokter of Fakir Chand transferred the suit property on 10.09.1995 in favour of the defendants No.1-4 by a transfer deed No. 5278. The defendants No.1-4 entered into a contract with the defendant No.5 to construct a multistoried building in the suit property and according to that contract; the defendant No.5 hanged a signboard, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants in short is thus that Fakir Chand obtained the allotment of the suit property by an allotment letter No.8059 dated 02.11.1961 from the government. Possession was delivered in favour of the lease-holder on 08.11.1965. Subsequently; Fakir Chand transferred the suit property in favour of the father of the defendants No.1-4 on 10.11.1970. For execution and registration of the sale deed both Fakir Chand and Altaf Hossain entered into a deed of agreement on 12.01.1970. The consideration money was fixed at Taka 15,000/-. On the date of deed of agreement Fakir Chand after taking a sum of Taka 13,500/- from Altaf Hossain handed over possession of the property. On the same date Fakir Chand executed a power of attorney on his behalf in the name of the wife of Altaf Hossain namely Umme Salina Khatun in respect of the disputed property and it was clearly mentioned in the power of attorney that Fakir Chand entered into a deed of agreement to sale the property in favour of Altaf Hossain and his attorney is empowered to execute and register the sale deed in favour of Altaf Hossain. The further case of the defendants is such that Fakir Chand since 12.01.1970 never looked after the property and his attorney Umme Salina Akter used to manage everything on his behalf and accordingly the government of Bangladesh recognizing the attorney Salma Akter registered the lease deed No.4643 on 25.02.1982 A.D. and in the lease deed the signature of attorney Umme Salina Khatun was obtained. It was further case of the defendants that their father Altaf Hossain in the year 1981 died leaving behind his legal heirs. After the death of Altaf Hossain by amicable partition the defendants No.1-4 use to possess the suit property and accordingly the attorney Salina Khatun for want of making a registered sale deed in favour of the defendants No.1-4 filed an application to the concerned Ministry of Housing and Public Works. Accordingly, the concerned Ministry pursuant to their memo No. 6/L-95/2107/1(2) dated 08.08.1995 gave permission to the attorney Salma Khatun for transfer of the property in favour of the defendants No.1-4. Thereafter, Salina Akter Khatun transferred the suit land in favour of the defendants No.1- 4 by a registered sub-kabala No. 5278 dated 10.09.1995. The defendants No.1-4 subsequently mutated their names and paying rent regularly. During city survey the suit land has been properly recorded in the names of the defendants No.1-4 and the defendant-opposite parties No.1-4 are paying upto date gas bill, city corporation holding tax, electricity bill etc. Recently they have decided to construct a multistoried building in the suit property and for that necessity they made a contract with the defendant No.5 a developer company to contract a multistoried building therein and the developer company according to their construct have prepared to construct the same. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property on the basis of false allegations filed the suit, which is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after examining 07 witnesses from the side of the plaintiffs and 03 witnesses from the side of the defendants evaluating the documentary and oral evidence produced from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 13.01.2013. 

 5. Being aggrieved the plaintiff preferred a title appeal being No.19 of 2013 in the court of learned District Jude, Dhaka which was transmitted to the 2nd Court of learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka for hearing and disposal and the learned Additional District Judge by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.11.2014 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and dismissal decree passed by the trial court. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned trial court as well as the lower appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that admittedly after the death of Fakir Chand the lease deed in the name of Fakir Chand was executed and registered by the admitted owner of the property; government of Bangladesh and on the basis of agreement for sale before the lease deed the defendants have claimed the property from their vendor the alleged power of attorney of Fakir Chand Umme Salma Khatun, but in fact; there is no legal basis to transfer the property in favour of anybody prior to the lease deed executed and registered by the government. The learned Advocate further submits that the papers in favour of the defendants are collusive and forged having no legal basis which is totally ignored by both the courts below. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below erred in law in disbelieving the evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses without any cogent reason as to the death of Fakir Chand. The learned appellate court below during deciding the fate of the appeal failed to assess the evidence on record in its true perspective and arrived at an erroneous decision that the plaintiffs to the suit failed to discharge their onus of proof by any trust worthy evidence while the defendants to the suit in respect of their respective case successfully proved that they have acquired right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. The learned Advocate argued that the positive contention as transpired from the pleading of the plaintiffs was not considered by the courts below during passing their judgment and decree, which is an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate in support of his argument referred some decisions of this Court and our Apex Court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the basic documents of the defendants were not properly evaluated by the learned courts below in their observation and findings. Under the ambit of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure there has been material omission with regard to the materials on record and there is a misreading and non-reading of evidence as well as non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning of failure of justice, which deserve interference of this Court. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners and submits that there is no illegality or irregularity from the sides of the learned trial court as well as from the side of the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal rightly assessed the evidence on record in its true perspective and there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and both the courts below concurrently held on proper evaluation of the evidence on records that the plaintiffs to the suit have measurably failed to discharge their onus of proof and on the contrary the defendants by adducing sufficient tangible evidence from their side successfully proved their specific case as agitated within their pleading in their written statement. The learned Advocate also submits that the admitted owner of the property government' by their execution and registration of the lease deed in favour of Fakir Chand completed the process of their allotment in favour of allottee of the suit property, Fakir Chand and the entire proceedings of the allotment was ended by execution and registration of the deed of lease and the lease-holder Fakir Chand legally acquired his right to property in the suit holding and also obtained the possession therein. Both the courts below concurrently observed in their findings and decision that the documentary evidence produced from the side of the defendants makes it clear that the title of the property was properly acquired by the defendants and the series of papers goes to show that in the disputed property; the contesting defendants No.1-4 acquired their right, title, interest and possession which is admitted practically from the admission of the plaintiff ~s witnesses during their depositions before the trial Court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the witnesses of the plaintiffs in fact proved the case of the defendants as a whole; and it is not the case of the plaintiff-petitioners that the witnesses have become hostile or biased in favour of the defendants. The official witnesses produced from the side of the plaintiffs also have totally proved the case of the defendants in toto in their testimonies which are already on records and properly evaluated by the learned courts below in their observation and findings and there is nothing on record to show that the trial court as well as the appellate court committed any wrong or illegality during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred some decisions of our Apex Court and lastly concluded his submissions stating that the civil Rule having no merit is liable to be discharged. 

 10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates I have gone through the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate court in Title Appeal No.19 of 2013 and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Title Suit No.34 of 2011 along with the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties; both oral and documentary. I have also perused the connected papers including the original plaint of the plaintiffs and the written statement submitted from the side of the contesting defendants. 

 13. Having gone through the records 1 find that, both the parties to substantiate their case have adduced witnesses. P.W.1; the plaintiff No.4 Md. Solid Khan who has deposed on behalf of the plaintiffs No.1-4 and 6 as of their Attorney. This witness in his testimony testified at a stage of his examination-in-chief that on 08.09.1981 Fakir Chand who was their father died. This witness also testified at a stage of his deposition that their father for want of execution of a deed in favour of the predecessor father of the defendants No.1-4, Altaf Hossain in respect of the disputed property handed over all the original papers in favour of Altaf Hossain and after the death of Altaf Hossain the defendants did not hand over those papers to them (the plaintiffs). It was also testified by this plaintiff No.04 that their father paid all the dues in favour of the government. P.W.1 identified the lease deed No.4643 dated 25.02.1982. He further testified that on 07.03.2007 he found a sign board in the name of a developer company in the suit property. During his deposition P.W. 1 frankly conceded that the defendants applied for a plan to D.I.T. and also testified that the original lease deed, letter of allotment and original copies of chalan in respect of the disputed property lies in favour of the predecessor of the defendants, Altaf Hossain. In a reply to a question during his cross-examination from the side of the defendants, P.W.1 testified at a stage that Umme Salma filed an application to dispose of the property in favour of the defendants No.1-4 in the concerned Ministry of Housing and Public Works of the government and obtained permission from the government to dispose of the property in favour of the defendants No.1-4. It is also admitted from the side of the plaintiff No.4 that the predecessor of the defendant-opposite parties, Altaf Hossain used to reside in the suit property. As to the death of Fakir Chand P.W.1 in his cross-examination testified that on 08.09.1989 Fakir Chand died. Subsequently; the same witness, plaintiff No.4 stated that Fakir Chand in the year 1981 expired. He has conceded during his cross-examination from the side of the defendants that in the lease deed on behalf of Fakir Chand his attorney Umme Salina Akter put her signature. He has admitted in his testimony during his cross-examination that in the death certificate issued by the City Corporation; which was produced from their side, there is a recital to the effect that Fakir Chand died on 05.09.2007 and there is no paper showing their mutation, payment of rent, payment of gas bill, water bill and electricity bill in respect of the suit property and they have failed to produce any scrap of paper to that effect. P.W.1 at a stage of his cross-examination in reply to a question from the side of the defendants admits that in the deed of agreement dated 12.01.1970 being No.370 there is a signature of his grandmother Fakir Chand and in every page of this "bainanama" the name of Fakir Chand is visible. 

 19. The last witness of the plaintiffs, Momata Rani Chakroborty is an official witness, who is the Assistant Record Keeper, Sadar Record Room, Tejgaon, Dhaka. This witness proved the lease deed No.4643 from the original volume and this deed has been marked as Exhibit-6. She has also proved the general power of attorney No.371 dated 12.01.1970 from the concerned volume which was executed by Fakir Chand in favour of attorney Umme Salma. This document has been marked as Exhibit-7. This witness also proved the sub-kabala deed No.5278 dated 10.09.1995, executed by Salina Akter Khatun on behalf of Fakir Chand in favour of the defendants and this document is marked as Exhibit-8. 

 20. Vis-a-vis; the defendant's witness D.W.1 is the defendant No.1(Ka) Mst. Rokeya Khatun. This witness corroborated the case of their written statement in her deposition. She has also testified about their title documents which are on records and possession in favour of them. 

 22. The last witness of' the defendant's, D.W.3 Md. Abul Kashem Akon testified about the case of the defendants as to their right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property. All the D.W.s have been thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the plaintiffs but except some minor discrepancies no such material contradiction or omission is noticed in their testimony by which they can be disbelieved. 

 24. Going through the evidence on records and connected all other papers it is obvious to note that, the learned courts below in their observation and findings evaluated the evidence on records in its true perspective and after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law rightly and legally decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal against the plaintiffs and in favour of the defendants. I find no such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. It further appears from the impugned judgment and decree that the learned appellate court under the ambit of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure on preponderance of evidence arrived at a conclusive decision as to the right, title, interest and possession of' the parties to the suit and in the observation and findings as it appears, there is no ambiguity or illegality by which it can be held that the judgment and decree is perverse. 

 26. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 25.11.2014 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.19 of 2013 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.01.2013 and 20.01.2013 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka in Title Suit No.34 of 2011 is hereby affirmed.

full_judgment:
3. The plaintiffs case, in briefly, is that the plaintiff for want of money mortgaged the suit land to the defendant No. 1 taking Taka 375 as loan and handed over possession of the mortgaged land in favour of the defendant with the understanding that the suit land will reconvey to the plaintiff if he can pay the loan money within 8 years. Accordingly the defendant No. 1 executed a registered agreement in favour of the plaintiff on the same day. The defendant No. 1 in connivance with the defendant No. 2 abstained from retransferring the suit land and enjoying the suit land after expiry of 8 years and has been enjoying additional profit. The plaintiff is entitled to redemption and thus the plaintiff has instituted the instant suit due to the refusal of the defendant in retransferring the suit land. 

 4. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint, contending inter alia that the plaintiff never mortgaged any land to the defendant. The defendant purchased the suit land vide registered kabala dated 4-6-1966 with the consideration amounting to Taka 375. The defendant executed an agreement in favour of the plaintiff but thereafter while the plaintiff due to economic crisis sold the suit land along with other land vide registered kabala dated 17-6-1967 with total consideration of Taka 1,000 whereupon Taka 375 was deducted received cash amount of Taka 625. Due to the simplicity the defendant did not take back the agreement from the plaintiff. The plaintiff is not entitled to redemption the suit land, and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr Md. Omar Farook learned Advocate for the defendant No. 1 petitioner submits that the mortgaged deed dated 4-6-1966 and agreement of reconveyance dated 4-6-1966 (Exhibit-1) became ineffective after sale of the suit land vide kabala dated 17-7-1967 (Exhibit-Ka) and, as such, the plaintiff had no locus-standi to sue for redemption and the suit is not tenable in the eye of law. Mr Omar Farook further submits that the Appellate Court below committed error in not considering the transfer of title of the suit land by the plaintiff which resulted error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate then submits that the plaintiff in his plaint suppressed the transfer of suit land along with other land vide kabala dated 17-6-1967 (exhibit-Ka) and did not challenge the said transfer even after disclosure of the matter by the defendant in the written statement. The defendant No. 1 petitioner proved the sale deed exhibit-Ka by adducing witness DW 2 which was appreciated by the trial Court but the learned appellate Court below failed to consider the evidence of DW 2 about the proof of the said transfer and most illegally opined that the sale deed was not proved according to law as such committed error of law and then he submits that the plaintiff had no subsisting interest over the suit land after execution and registration of sale deed dated 17-6-1967 exhibit-Ka and there was no scope for reconveyance of the suit land in pursuant to mortgage deed and agreement dated 4-6-1966 exhibit-I. The learned Judge of the Court of Appeal below while disposing of the case of redemption failed to determine the issue whether the mortgage was subsisting upto its tenure or not and thus arrived at a contrary findings of fact resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and he then submits that the suit was dismissed on 13-9-1987 and the defendant No. 1 due to necessity took back the sale deed exhibit-Ka from record vide Order No. 49 dated 27-9-1987 but unfortunately the said exhibit-Ka was lost and that the defendant No. I obtained fresh certified copy of mortgage deed dated 4-6-1966 and sale deed dated 17-6-1967 and submitted those before the Appellate Court. Since the certified copy is public document and previously original was marked as exhibit before the trial Court, the appellate Court below, ought to have believe those as valid documents or in the alternative the appellate Court below being a final Court of fact ought to prove its genuineness by calling the volume of the Sub-Registrar Office but without arriving any conclusive proof disbelieving those documents and disbelieving the defendant's case committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The defendant No. 1 after purchase the suit land along with other land vide kabala dated 17-6-1967 transferred the suit land to Ambia Khatun vide kabala dated 17-4-1983 and while dispute arise between the defendant No.1 petitioner and Ambia Khatun, the defendant No. 1 instituted Other Suit No. 145 of 1995 against Ambia Khatun for declaration of title and for permanent injunction which is still pending and during its pendency any proceeding by the trial Court against the same is bad in law. 

 9. Mr Md Shamsul Haque, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties submits that the original deed dated 17-6-1967 was never produced before the Court or any other Authority for mutation, preparation of record-of-rights, payment of revenue etc. and there was no explanation in the written statement as to the where about of the original deed and evidences as regards the missing of the original deed have been apparently untrustworthy. No GD was lodged as regards the missing of the original title deed, even the certified copy of the said deed was taken back without any explanation and was submitted after a long time before this Court only after the police went to the suit-land for execution of the decree of Appellate Court below. The custody of the registered agreement for reconveyance dated 4-6-1966 in original in the hands of the plaintiff-opposite parties herein speaks against the execution of the deed dated 17-6-1967. When the agreement in original was filed in Court by the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 could not legally satisfy the Court why the agreement in original was not handed over to the defendant No. 1 before registration of the deed dated 17-6-1967. The plaintiff's suit was for redemption of 15 decimal land but the defendants claimed 20 decimal on the strength of the deed dated 17-6-1967 which was straight way denied by the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 did not prove his possession over the additional 5 decimal of land, no mutation, no record of rights, no payment of revenue of the defendant No. 1 was produced before the Court though the defendant No. 1 claimed that he purchased the said 15 + 05 = 20 decimal of land on 17-6-1967, so it is the conclusive circumstantial proof that the said deed dated 17-6-1967 being a forged deed was never produced by the defendant No. 1 and was never acted upon. Whereas the plaintiff has upto date record of right and up to date payment of revenue as regards the said additional 5 decimal of land, being his paternal property, is the conclusive proof of possession and title of the plaintiff-opposite parties. Mr Haque then submits that the so-called deed dated 17-6-1967 is ex facie a vague one as it does not mention specifically the value of the additional 5 decimals of land and the value of the right of reconveyance while both the instrument required separate stamp and registration cost specifically. Mr Haque further submits that the defendant in depositions and cross-examinations and also at paragraph No. 5 of his/their application for stay of the execution case filed before this Court on 1st day of July, 1998 clearly stated that he has transferred the suit-land to one Ambia Khatun on 17-4-1983 and 11-5-1983 and the plaintiff-opposite parties instituted the suit for redemption on 3-6-1983 and why the defendant No. 1 petitioners is/are fighting the legal battle without impleading said Ambia Khatun and why said Ambia Khatun is not coming for stay of the execution case ? Such contradictory claim and conduct of the defendant petitioners overwhelmingly proves his/their fraud and forgery and thus the plaintiff opposite parties has /have been deprived of the benefit of the suit-land for more than 4 decades. Mr Shamsul Haque then submits that as per section 6(h) of the Transfer of Property Act there can be no transfer to any disqualified transferee. The transferee of the alleged deed dated 17-6-1967 was already a transferee as regards 15 decimals of the suit land as per the registered deed dated 4-6-1966 and therefore he was a disqualified transferee in a deed dated 17-6-1967 where the said 15 decimals of land was in the schedule of both the deeds dated 4-6-1966 and 17-6-1967. The registration of the subsequent deed amounts to cancellation of the earlier deed which is not permitted in law and the sub-registrar was without lawful authority in registering the subsequent deed dated 17-6-1967 and similarly as per section 7 of the Transfer of Property Act only person entitled to transferable property is competent to transfer the said transferable property. While a validly registered deed dated 4-6-1966 was in force and was admitted by the parties, the transferor of the said deed dated 4-6-1966 was already a transferor in respect of 15 decimals of land and he could not be a valid transferor in the deed dated 17-6-1967 where in the schedule the said 15 decimals of land was included. The subsequent deed could not be registered and law cannot be changed by consent of the parties. The subsequent deed in the instant case was simply void, which even does not require a declaration that the said deed is void. Such a deed whenever is produced for any practical purpose would not be accepted and liable to be impounded by any lawful authority and as per section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act an ostensible owner can transfer any property. Now as per the deed dated 4-6-1966 the defendant was ostensible owner and the defendant could sell the suit land, then how a person entitled to sell could buy the same suit land from a person who is already a transferor and at the later time he had no title no interest in the suit land. Until his right to reconveyance was specifically enforced and the suit land was transferred back to him by a registered deed, he had no right, title and interest on 17-6-1967 over the suit land and he could not execute the subsequent deed as regards the 15 decimal of land. Mr Haque then submits that as per section 4 of the Stamp Act, 1899 additional stamp is required for additional instrument. Obviously the alleged deed dated 17-6-1967 had additional instrument, however no consideration was specified for the additional instrument, namely the right of reconveyance, and, as such, no separate stamp was used and no registration cost was paid and it was also not clear what was the consideration for the additional 5 decimals of land. As per section 14 there can be no second instrument on same stamp paper and section 15 of the said Act provides that such deed is deemed as unstamped which is liable to be impounded whenever it is produced, and sections 27, 33, 35, 43, 57, 61(4), 62, taken together the said deed was liable to be impounded, not admissible in evidence and the person in possessesion of such a deed is liable for criminal action as per the Stamp Act and then submits that as per Schedule 1(55) of the Stamp Act, 1999 the right of reconveyance could be released or renounced as per law upon payment of specified stamp duty but the defendant No. 1 had arranger for registration of a forged deed dated 17-6-1967 which was if registered at all was registered illegally and that is an invalid document which can never be acted upon and has been acted upon in the last about 50 years and as per the Registration Act once sale deed is registered, the same cannot be cancelled by consent or by subsequent deed (AIR 2011 Mad 66 FB), and a sale deed once registered can be avoided only by a subsequent registered document transfer (27 CWN 8 PC) and then submits that as per section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with the decisions reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 66 DLR (AD) 162, 20 BLC (AD) 4 the plaintiff-opposite party is entitled to recover possession of the 15 decimal of the suit land. Mr Haque then submits the plaintiffs case stands proved by admission of the defendant No. 1 and the defendant's case being denied by the plaintiff, the Evidence Act provides onus upon the defendant to prove his case, because in the absence of any evidence in this case the plaintiff is entitled to the decree in his favour inasmuch as the plaintiffs case has been admitted by the defendant and the plaintiff acquired title by operation of law and the Appellate Court below findings as regards burden of proof is in accordance with law and the trial Court erred in law as regards onus of proof and thus the Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his contentions he has referred to the case of Emmanuele Grech vs Antonio Grech, reported in 6 DLR 599 case of Haji Waziullah vs Additional Deputy Commissioner, reported in 41 DLR 96, case of Amirun Nessa vs Golam Kashem reported in 42 DLR 499, case of Abdul Hamid vs Dr Sadeque Ali reported in 27 DLR 511, case of Abdul Quddus vs Anjuman Khatoon reported in 36 DLR 313, case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR 239, case of Shaukat Ali vs Shamsum Bibi reported in 27 DLR 59. Mr Haque lastly submits that in the instant case the transaction i.e. the usufructuary mortgage began on 4-6-1966 and after 7 years on 4-6-1974 the term of usufructuary mortgage (খায় খালাসী বন্ধক) expired. So the transaction was alive when the President Order No. 88 of 1972 was promulgated. So the President Order No. 88 of 1972 and the provision of Section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 are applicable on this transaction as it was alive up to 1974. So the President Order No. 88 of 1972 and provision of section 95A, the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 should apply in this case and the Rule in the instant civil revision is liable to be discharged for end of justice with exemplary cost as the defendant deprived the plaintiff opposite party herein for a period of more then 4 decades. The defendant failed to prove his case by adducing oral and documentary evidence and the learned trial Court was unable to realize the legal issues involved in the suit as such committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice but the Appellate Court below rightly passed the judgment and decree on the basis of evidence and considering the legal issues. 

 11. The plaintiff for want of money mortgaged he suit land to the defendant No. 1 taking Taka 375 as loan and handed over possession of the mortgaged and in favour of the defendant with the understanding that the suit land will reconvey to the plaintiff if he can pay the loan money within 8 years. Accordingly, the defendant No. 1 executed a registered agreement in favour of the plaintiff on the same day. The defendant No. 1 in connivance with the defendant No. 2 abstained from retransferring the suit land and enjoying the suit land after expiry of 8 years and hence the suit. The defendant No. 1 congested the suit and claimed that he purchased the suit land vide registered kabala dated 4-6-1966 and executed an agreement in favour of the plaintiff and subsequently the plaintiff due to economic crisis sold the suit land to him (defendant) along with other land vide registered kabala dated 17-6-1967. The said original deed 17-6-1967 was never produced before the Court and there was no explanation in this regard and on the other hand, the registered agreement for reconveyance dated 4-6-1966 in original in the hands of the plaintiff which speaks against the execution of the aforesaid deed dated 17-6-1967 and the defendant failed to prove that the said deed dated 17-7-.1967 was executed by the plaintiff. On the basis of the said deed dated 17-56-1967 the defendant claimed 20 decimal land but failed to prove his possession over the entire land and no mutation, no record of right and no payment of revenue of entire 20 decimal land was produced before the Court which indicates that the said deed was never acted upon. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on, record I find no substance in the Rule.
