 11. In support of the pleadings of the parties both the parties have adduced evidence to substantiate their contention. In addition to that, the defendant-appellants during pendency of the original suit submitted an additional written statement stating that at the demise of Omar Ali Chowkidar his only sister the plaintiff Rupban Bibi became his legal heir and thus Rupban Bibi became the owner of the disputed property. The plaintiff Rupban Bibi very often felt ill due to her old age and the defendant No. 1 Most. Monowara Begum used to look after her. It was further mentioned in the said additional written statement that being pleased with the defendant No. 1 the plaintiff decided to transfer the suit land in favour of Monowara Begum and finally she made an oral gift in favour of the defendant No. 1 in respect of the disputed land including homestead. 

 31. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 13-10-2011 and 14-11-2011 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Madaripur, in Title Suit No. 131 of 2010 in decreeing the suit is hereby upheld and confirmed.

parties:
Yeamin Nobi (Md) and others ------ Appellants 
Vs.
Moklesur Rahman and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The appellants' case, in-short, is that the land measuring 0.58 acre in plot No. 724 appertaining to CS Khatian No.509 under holding No.8 of Kushtia Pourashava originally belonged to Nil Moni Roy Chowdhury and others, who exchanged the same with the two brothers named Yamin Nobi alias Yeas in Nobi and Rexaun Nobi. The said two brothers after getting the disputed land under exchange deed in equal share started living thereon and later on conflict arose which resulted in various civil and criminal cases amongst them. The predecessor of the respondents, Md Rejan Nabi as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.174 of 1976 in the Court of the then Sub- ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Kushtia for partition against his brother Yeamin Nobi (predecessor of the present appellants) and got Preliminary decree on contest vide judgment and decree dated 12-4-1980. The defendant No.1, thereafter, as appellant preferred First Appeal No.7 of 1981 before this Court and during pendency of the said appeal the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 sold his 50% undivided share of land on 14-2-1982, 16-2-1982, 15-7-1982 and 17-7-1982 by 6 Kabalas (Exhibit Nos. 'Cha' and 'Chha' series) without serving any notice upon the predecessor of the present appellants and hence, Md Yeamin Nobi, the predecessor of the present appellants filed Miscellaneous (preemption) Case No.43 of 1989 under section 4 of the Partition Act for pre-empting the case land. 

 5. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record factually found that the land under preemption was divided land and the petitioner did not mention the schedule of the land under pre-emption in the original preemption petition and the pre-emption case was barred by limitation according to the provision under Article 180 of Limitation Act as the case was filed after long lapse of 6/7 years, that is, beyond the stipulated period of 3 years and thus, the learned Subordinate Judge dismisses the pre-emption case by the impugned judgment and order dated 17-5-1998. 

 7. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant in the course of his argument has taken me through the impugned judgment, deposition of PWs and OPWs and other materials on record and then submits that the learned trial judge erred in law in disallowing the pre-emption case on the main ground that the case was hopelessly barred by limitation as the case was filed beyond the stipulated time of 3 years although there is no limitation to file the pre-emption case and, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside. The learned Advocate to fortify his 1st branch of argument has referred to the decisions reported in 36 DLR 351, 1 BLT (AD) 34 and AIR 1973 (Patna) 142. Mr Nurul Amin further submits that the findings of the trial Court below on the point of partition of the suit land is perverse being contrary to the evidence on record inasmuch as admittedly, Md Rejan Nobi as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 174 of 1976 for partition of their ejmali property including the case land and finally the said suit was decreed and, as such, in no way it can be said that the ejmali property of the parties was partitioned or divided by metes and bounds. Mr Nurul Amin further submits that the engaged Advocate in the court below due to his unintentional mistake did not mention the schedule of the land under pre-emption in the preemption petition and the same cannot be a valid ground to reject the case if otherwise the case is maintainable in law. Finally, Mr Nurul Amin submits that the impugned judgment is a product of non application of judicial mind and suffers from patent illegality and, as such, the same is liable to be set-said. 

 8. Mr AKM Golam Mohiuddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-respondents, on the other hand, supports the impugned order and contends that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was perfectly justified in disallowing the pre-emption case on the clear findings that land under pre-emption was not undivided land and the petitioner did not mention the schedule of the case land in the original pre-emption petition and the preemption case was barred by limitation according to the provision under Article 180 of the Limitation Act inasmuch as the case was filed after long lapse of 6/7 years, that is, beyond the stipulated period of 3 years. He further upon referring to the evidence of PW-1 and OPW-1and the certified copy of the sale deeds as well submits that admittedly the preemptor himself transferred a portion of land from his share and, as such, it does not lie in the mouth of the preemptor that he needs more land or land in question belonged to joint or undivided family. Mr Mohiuddin further submits that in spite of getting opportunity to implead the necessary parties such as Taimur Banda, Mozaffar Hossain and others the petitioner deliberately did not implead them in the case and, as such, the case was bad for defect of parties. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the petitioner never approached before the Court with clean hands, who made self contradictory statements as witness in 2 cases namely Title Suit No.174 of 1976 and Miscellaneous (preemption) Case No.43, of 1989 as to the property in question was divided or not and, as such, the appellants as heirs of the pre-emptor petitioner are not entitled to get any relief whatsoever. The learned Advocate to fortify his argument has relied on the decisions reported in 59 DLR (AD) 69, 14 BLC 734, 4 BLC (AD) 98 and 54 DLR 181. 

 9. 1 have heard the learned Advocates from both the sides at length and perused the memo of appeal, deposition of witnesses of both the cases, that is, Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 43 of 1989 and Title Suit No.174 of 1976 and other relevant materials on record. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the parties before this Court it would be convenient for me to decide first of all the question whether the land in question belonged to joint/undivided family or not. 

 11. In this case the pre-emptor, Yamin Nobi himself was examined as PW-1, who in his deposition stated that the case land has not yet been partitioned, the opposite party Nos.2-4 are stranger to the case land. This witness in his cross-examination denied the suggestion of the opposite parties stating that: "১৬-৪-৮৮ ইং তারিখে আকতার বাবু ও আবদুল মুরাদের কাছে জমি বিক্রি করেছি এ কথা সত্য নয়।"আকতার বাবু ও আবদুল মুরাদের কাছে জমি বিক্রয় বিষয় ঠিক একথা সত্য নয়।"This witness was also examined as DW- 1 in Title Suit No.17 4 of 1976, who in his deposition stated that the plaintiff and myself are in possession over the suit land by specific boundary. I have got separate holding No.8 for my portion. The plaintiff's holding number is 8/l. We also pay separate municipal tax. This witness as defendant No.1 filed written statement in Title Suit 174 of 1976 stating inter alia that: 

 14. On a query by me, Mr Nurul Amin, learned Advocate submits that since the instant Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 1989 under section 4 of the Partition Act is related with the original Title Suit No.174 of 1976, the engaged Advocate in the Court below did not mention the schedule of the case land in the original petition of Miscellaneous case for pre-emption. The preemption case under section 4 of the Partition Act is an independent proceeding in which schedule of case land and particulars of the disputed deeds are very much required to be described/made in details otherwise the pre-emption case must fail. Therefore, the trial court below was perfectly justified in holding that since the pre-emptor-petitioner did not mention the schedule of the case land and particulars of the deeds in question in the original pre-emption petition/application, the pre-emption case is incompetent, misconceived and not maintainable. 

 28. On an overall consideration of the facts, circumstances and the materials on record I find that the respondents' basic objection to the maintainability of the pre-emption case mainly on two counts that (i) the land in question is not a part of an undivided family's property and (ii) the original pre-emptor-petitioner neither mentioned the schedule of the land nor has given any particulars. of the disputed deeds in the original pre-emption application which are sound and, I accordingly hold that the pre-emption case itself was not maintainable.

parties:
Ahmed Ali (Md) alias Ataur Rahman and another ------ Petitioners 
Vs
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the Petitioners are full brothers and they have purchased 0.1155 acre of land in Plot Nos. 9094/11422, 9095/11423 appertaining to Khatian Nos. 2951/3, 2951/4 corresponding to Settlement Khatian No. 2951 of Mouza Sylhet Municipality by two registered sale deeds being Nos. 12503 and 12504 dated 17-7-2005 from the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. The petitioners subsequently came to know that the said property was mortgaged by the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 in favour of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation ("HBFC"), Sylhet, who had defaulted in paying the loan money. HBFC filed Artha Rin Suit being No. 51 of 1992 which was decreed in its favour. The said Decree-Holder HBFC for realization of its decretal amount filed Artha Jari Case No. 16 of 2005. Thereafter, the petitioners after getting information about the aforesaid case sent a legal notice to the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 for alleged suppression of fact and to take necessary steps for releasing the property from HBFC. Subsequently the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12 after receipt of the said notice, instead of taking any steps for releasing the property, filed Title Suit No. 185 of 2006 against the petitioners in the 2nd Court of the Joint District Judge, Sylhet, for declaration that the kabalas registered in favour of the petitioners in respect of the aforesaid property are forged and fraudulent and for recovery of khas possession of the said property 

 7. By filing a supplementary affidavit the Petitioners further stated that Toslimunnessa, the Respondent No. 5 and her son Mohiuddin Ahmad, the Respondent No. 12, and daughter Yasmin Akhtar took loan from Uttara Bank, Ambarkhana Branch, Sylhet by mortgaging 0.070 acre of land covered by SA Plot No. 9095/11423, corresponding to BS Plot No. 7108. Out of the said land Toslimunnessa sold 0.035 acre of land by a kabala dated 18-5-2005 to Md. Mostafa Ahmad (Azad), who in turn sold the same to the Petitioners by kabala No. 12503 dated 17-7-2005. Toslimunnessa and her sons and daughters, the Respondents Nos. 5-12 herein, sold .08 acre of land to the Petitioners by kabala No. 12504 dated 17-7-2005 suppressing the fact of earlier mortgage with the Uttara Bank. The Respondents Nos. 5-12 defaulted in payment of loan and the said Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 7 of 2008 in the 2nd Court of the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet. The Suit was decreed, and the decree-holder Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 28 of 2009 for realization of the decretal money through auction sale of the mortgaged property under sections 33(1) and (4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("Act"). Since, there was no bid in response to sale proclamations and notices, on the application of the said Bank the Adalat issued and registered a certificate of title on 01-8-2012 in respect of the aforesaid 0.070 acre of land in favour of the Bank under section 33(7) of the Act declaring the title of the said land vested in the decree-holder Bank. The present Petitioners made representations to Uttara Bank on 7-6-2012 and 27-2-2013 seeking release of 0.035 acre of land, which the Petitioners purchased from Md. Mostafa Ahmad Azad, a transferee from Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar on 17-7-2005, on receipt of the decretal amount from the Petitioners. But instead of responding to the Petitioners, Uttara Bank published auction notice on 28-4-2013 for sale of 0.07 acre of land. The present Petitioners challenged the same by filing Writ Petition No. 4924 of 2013. By an Order dated 15-5-2013 this Court directed the said Bank to dispose of those representations of the Petitioners within a period of one month in accordance with law and further directed that till disposal of those representations the auction process initiated by the Bank be kept in abeyance. 

 8. Uttara Bank, however, remaining in non-compliance of that Order, the present Petitioners, consequentially filed Contempt Petition No. 74 of 2014 wherein a Rule was issued on 15-5-2014 directing the Uttara Bank to show cause as to why a contempt proceeding will not be drawn against it. This led to a positive response from the Bank manifested in its recognition that the Petitioners should pay the whole of the decretal amount and take whole of the land. Ultimately, the Petitioners agreed to the Bank's proposal to secure their property and the said Bank by a kabala executed and registered on 9-6-2014 sold the land in the case plot No. 9095/11423 to the Petitioners who thus acquired title in the said land. 

 9. Evident also is the fact that, Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar took loan of Taka 5,00,000 from the Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. Ambarkhana Branch by mortgaging the self same land by a deed of mortgage dated 21-7-2002 prior to the Petitioners' acquisition of the said land from her. Thereafter, the Petitioners got the property released by paying the loan and then took the kabala No. 12504 dated 17-7-2005 from Toslimunnessa Jaigirdar and her son and daughter. At the time of purchase, the vendors handed over certified copy of their title deed to the Petitioners on the plea that the original had been lost. The Petitioners further asserted that, if the money paid by the Petitioners is adjusted in the account of the judgment-debtors, the Petitioners undertake that they would not demand from HBFC return of the original title deeds of the Borrower-judgment-debtors and will not claim any other right of subrogation. 

 10. HBFC contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying all the material allegations made in the application contending, inter alia, that on an Order of the Adalat the Petitioners deposited the decretal money in their names and not in the names of the Borrower-Judgment-Debtor Respondent Nos. 5-12. Since the higher authority within HBFC refused to accept the said deposit in the names of the Petitioners, HBFC filed a petition in the Adalat on 9-7-2012 to review the Order No. 54 passed by it on 29-2-2012 and the Adalat by Order No. 58 dated 29-7-2012 reversed the earlier Order and directed HBFC to supply draft copy of auction sale by 13-8-2012. It is also contended that HBFC cannot accept the decretal amount from a third party other than judgment-debtors as there is no legal relationship between HBFC and the Petitioners. Rather there is a title dispute between the judgment-debtors and the Petitioners relating to the mortgaged property. So, the Petitioners have no locus standi and, as such, the Writ Petition is not maintainable and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioners submit that the Petitioners as purchasers with a view to save the property from auction filed an application in the Artha Jari Case praying for addition of party as judgment-debtors and accepting the decretal amount from the Petitioners. By Order dated 21-7-2011 the Adalat added the Petitioners as Judgment-Debtor Nos. 2 and 3 in the Artha Jari case. The respondents did not challenge the said Order before the higher court and, as such, the Petitioners have assumed the status of judgment-debtors co-extensive with the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. As judgment-debtors the Petitioners in pursuance of an Order of the Adalat dated 29-12-2012 have deposited entire decretal amount with interest totaling Taka 20,44,000 in the account of HBFC towards adjustment of the loan owed by the Respondent Nos. 5-12. The Adalat passed the said Order with the consent of HBFC and Respondent Nos. 5-12 directing HBFC to adjust the amount in the loan account of the Respondent Nos. 5-12. On an application filed by HBFC the Adalat reversed the Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012 and directed the Decree-Holder to supply draft copy of the auction notice by 13-8-2012 most illegally and arbitrarily. Mr. Maswood further submits that the Artha Rin Adalat cannot review its Order passed earlier which has already taken effect. It is also argued that any person whose interest is involved in the mortgaged property other than a Judgment-Debtor is similarly legally entitled to pay and satisfy the decree with a view to get the property released. Since, therefore, the Petitioners have assumed the role of judgment-debtors in the Artha Jari Case by way of addition, there is no legal impediment in they making the payment of the decretal amount towards adjustment of the loan of the Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. It is argued, therefore, that, the Adalat passed the Order on 29-2-2012 rightly allowing the Petitioners prayer to pay the amount and directing HBFC to adjust the same in the loan account of the loanee. 

 12. The arguments above are predicated on the core submission of Mr. Maswood that person other than the judgment-debtor can satisfy the decretal amount and seek recording of satisfaction of the decree as per provisions of Order XXI, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("Code"). Accordingly, the Petitioners having made payment of the decretal amount to the Decree-holder, the latter is legally bound to adjust the same in the account of the borrower judgment-debtor. But the Decree-Holder HBFC instead of making adjustment of the amount in the account of the loanee with a mala fide intention, Mr Maswood submits, sought review of the Order passed by the Adalat. It is also argued that the intention of the legislature is to recover money from the borrower judgment-debtor and not to sell the property of the mortgagor or their successor. But in the instant case HBFC is more interested to sell the property in auction than to adjust the amount paid by the Petitioners in the account of the Respondent Nos. 5-12 borrowers. Such-attitude and action of the HBFC has got no legal sanction under the Act or under any other laws and, as such, the impugned order passed by the Adalat reversing its earlier Order is palpably illegal and without lawful authority. It is also submitted that the Petitioners shall not claim redemption of the mortgaged property in their favour or insist on the handing over of the original property documents, if the adjustment of the money is made by HBFC in the loan account of the judgment-debtors. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of KS Hussain Peer vs Kadapala Venkata Ramana Reddy reported in AIR 1989 (AP) 62. 

 13. Mr Imam Hossain with Ms Khurshid Jahan, the learned Advocates appearing for the Respondent No. 4 submit that the Petitioners are neither mortgagors nor judgment-debtors as such they are not entitled to make payment of the decretal amount to HBFC which is not legally obliged to accept the payment made by them and to release the mortgage property in favour of any person other than the mortgagors. Mr Imam also submits that there is a dispute between the mortgagor-borrower and the Petitioners regarding validity of the sale deeds alleged to have been executed by the mortgagors. If the payment is received from the Petitioners and the property is released by HBFC, there is the risk of multiplicity of proceedings and anticipating such scenario HBFC refused to accept the payment and adjust the same in the account of the borrower and took step for auction sale as per Order of the Adalat. It is also argued that the Artha Rin Adalat can rectify its own order under section 57 of the Act and there is no illegality in the impugned order. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Md Salim Hossain vs Uttara Bank Ltd. reported in 17 BLC (AD) 154, facts of the present case is different from the case referred to by the Respondent's counsel. 

 16. From a perusal of the above quoted Order of the Adalat, it is found that the direction given by the Adalat to adjust the amount deposited by the Petitioners in the account of the borrower-judgment-debtor without any objection from the decree-holder as well as the judgment-debtors i.e. Respondent Nos. 5 to 12. Thereafter, HBFC by filing an application on 9-4-2012 prayed three months' time to effect adjustment of the amount and for an Order enabling HBFC not to hand over the original documents to the added judgment-debtor-petitioners. The Adalat allowed time as prayed for and fixed 9-7-2012 for further Order. On the date fixed the HBFC filed an application under Order 47, rule 1 of the Code for review of the Order No. 54 dated 29-2-2012. The Court fixed 12-7-2012 and thereafter on 29-7-2012 for hearing the said application. The Adalat heard the application filed by HBFC on 29-7-2012 and upon hearing the parties allowed the application and accordingly reversed its earlier Order dated 29-2-2012 in the terms which runs thus:- 

 22. A cumulative reading of the clauses (a)(b) and (c) of rule 1 coupled with rule 2 of Order XXI of the Code reveals that while judgment-debtors are legally bound to pay the decretal amount to the Decree Holder, there is little indication as who specifically may pay the amount in the manner formulated in clause (b) of Sub-rule 1. This, in this Court's view, sufficiently envisage a scenario where a person who has purchased the property subject to the encumbrances may step into the shoes of the vendor and, though not being the borrower Judgment-Debtor strictly understood, by that reason is entitled to, and not precluded from, pay the decretal amount. Indeed, this can be seen substantiated from another perspective for example, under Section 55(5)(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 which runs thus:- 

 23. This Court finds, therefore that given the above quoted provisions of law, a buyer shall be bound to pay the moneys due on any encumbrances subject to which the property is sold and the interest thereon afterwards accruing due. In the instant case the Petitioners contend to have purchased the case property with the encumbrances and, as such, they suffer from no legal impediment to pay the decretal amount as public charge to the decree-holder to satisfy the decree even given the fact that the fact of mortgage is not disclosed in the sale and notwithstanding the pending of Title Suit No. 185 of 2006. It is understood that the sale in question took place subject to encumbrances. For that reason also the Petitioners can pay and satisfy the decree as alleged purchaser of the property subject to a mortgage. 

 25. To answer the second part of the question earlier raised, this Court, upon visiting the Act in its entirety has found nothing therein that attests .to the fact of the Artha Rin Adalat being empowered to review its own Orders. By that reason, and given the observations herein above, this Court finds that the impugned order on the face of it is illegal and not sustainable in law. Therefore, this Court finds merit in the Rule and is inclined to make the Rule absolute. However, nothing of this judgment shall affect the merit of the Title Suit No. 185 of 2006 filed by the Respondent Nos. 5-12 against the petitioners challenging the validity of the sale deeds in question.

parties:
Rama Kanto Nath others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Md Helal Uddin Chowdhury and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order of remand dated 29-6-1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar in Title Appeal No. 45 of 1991 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The petitioners as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 22 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Baralekha, Moulvibazar praying for a decree for establishment of title, for declaration that Kabala dated 11-6-1988 purported to be executed by the defendant No. 6 in favour of defendant No. 1-3 is void, collusive and without consideration and also for permanent injunction. Subsequently, by order dated 27-7-1989 amendment was allowed to the effect of recovery of possession of .01 decimal of land to the northern part of settlement plot No. 1260. 

 4. The case of the petitioner in short, is that the suit land appertaining to settlement plot No. 1259 area 11 decimals and plot No. 1260 area 19 decimals including other land while was owned and possessed by Arjad Ali and Anjab Ali father of the defendant No.7. Mujahid Ali Chowdhury purchased the suit land including some other land by registered kabala dated 20-12-1951 corresponding to 6th Poush, 1358 BS of which item No.4 of the kabala schedule land attracts the suit land Mujahid Ali Chowdhury died leaving defendant No.7 in whose name the D.P. and final settlement khatian was rightly published and while defendant No.7 was in exclusive possession to sold away by two registered kabala dated 26-6-1978 and 25-10-1978 in favour of Priya Moni Debi, who transferred the same in favour of the plaintiff by deed of gift dated 8-9-1985 and 2-6-1987 and they are in possession of the said land by growing paddy and paying rents to the government. That the defendant Nos.1-3 obtained a collusive and fictitious kabala dated 11-6-1988 from one Sonahar Ali although their vendor or his predecessor had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The plaintiff father came to know that the defendant No.7 during his father life time created a false lease deed dated 23-2-1954 in favour of the predecessor of the defendant Nos.4-6. Asab Ali, when the defendants threatened the petitioners to dispossess them from the peaceful possession in the suit land, they were constrained to file the present suit on 21.02.1989. During pendency of the suit, the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs-petitioners from northern 01 decimal of land of suit plot No. 1260 for which they prayed for recovery of possession of the said land. 

 5. Defendants Nos. 1 and 2-opposite party Nos. I and 3 herein contested the said suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the defendants had no objection about the plaintiff's title in the 0.11 decimal of plot No. 1259 but regarding 0.19 decimals of land of plot No. 1260 the plaintiff case is that the total land of said plot is 0.35 decimals, same was owned by Mujahid Ali Chowdhury who for his financial crisis had leased out entire land of plot No. 1260 including other lands in favour of father of defendants Nos. 4-6 Asab Ali for a period of 10 years. It was stipulated in the leased that in case favour to return the money by the leaser within the specified period of the leased deed would automatically as complete sale and since then Asab Ali had been possessing the total land of plot No. 1260 within the knowledge of all concerned. In the last settlement operation name of Aftab Ali Chowdhury was wrongly inserted in the title column, but in the column of possession the name of Asab Ali was rightly recorded. After death of Asab Ali by amicable partition defendant No.6 Sanar Ali got the land of suit plot No. 1260 in his exclusive possession and sold it to the defendant Nos.1-3 by registered kabala dated 11-6-1988 since then they are in possession. During the war of liberation the original title deeds of the vendors of the answering defendants had been destroyed. With these averments the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit with costs. 

 b. Have the plaintiffs any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land? 

 e. Are the plaintiffs entitled to get the relief as prayed for or entitled to any other relief or reliefs? 

 7. Learned Assistant Judge after considering the evidence and materials on record decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 28-2-1991. Against the said judgment and decree the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 45 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Moulvibazar and on transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar, who by the judgment and order dated 29-6-1997 allowed the appeal and sent the suit on remand to the trial court, on the finding that the local investigation is necessary for ascertaining the identity of the separate .01 decimal of land to entitle them to get a decree for recovery of khas possession of the suit land. 

 14. It appears that the trial judge decreed the suit upon non-consideration of preliminary point and without considering objection raised by the defendant Nos. 1-3 in their written statement at the earliest opportunity for holding local investigation into the suit land and without holding such local investigation the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any decree in the suit as prayed for since the said objection directly hit at the root of the plaintiff's title in the suit. Further, the learned trial court did not consider the factual aspect of the case that no issues was framed whether the dag/plot in item 4 of the registered kabala dated 22-12-1951 attracts the suit schedule land or not. 

 15. It further appears that the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint bearing dag Nos. 1259 and 1260 are unspecified, vague, indefinite and not clearly bounded and even the statements of the plaintiff are taken to be so far one block of the suit land as claimed by the plaintiff, but they failed to point out '01 decimal of land within the original boundary of the plaint from which the plaintiff alleged to have been dispossessed has not been specifically described with specific boundaries as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to get decree upon unspecified suit land without holding local investigation for ascertaining the identity of the suit land. 

 18. Law as in order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the plaintiff to give clear description of the land in suit so that the land in suit is identifiable. In the present case it is seen that the particulars of the land as in schedule of the plaint is vague and unspecified. In that state of the matter it is clear that the plaintiff have sought for declaration of title in respect of unspecified, vague and undivided land. If the land in suit is vague, unspecified and that relief sought is in respect of undivided portion of land of particular plot in that case suit for mere declaration of title is not maintainable.

parties:
Zubair Alam Chowdhury and others ----- Defendant-respondent-Petitioners
Versus
Abdul Motin being dead his legal heirs: I (a) Shafiara Begum and others ----- Plaintiff-appellant-opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1-7 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 26.04.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet in title Appeal No. 90 of 1997 reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.03.1997 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gowainghat, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 80 of 1992 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can he stated thus, the present opposite party nos.l-7 as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 20 of 1986 in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Sylhet for getting partition of the land described in schedule of the plaint and also for permanent injunction against the defendants. The suit was transferred subsequently to the court of learned Assistant Judge, Gowainghat, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No 80 of 1992. The pleadings of the plaintiffs to the suit is such that one Abdus Sattar predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs purchased 07(seven) decimals of land from the original owner the defendant No.2. Thereafter, Abdus Sattar mutated his name and continued possession. The defendant No.2 subsequently executed and registered a deed of rectification in favour of Abdus Sattar inserting plot No. 9093 instead of plot No. 1293. After the demise of Abdus Sattar the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land after getting the land by may of inheritance but the defendants being the co-sharers of the plaintiffs tried to disturb the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs and at the request of the plaintiffs they denied to effect amicable partition in respect of the suit land which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant Nos.1 and 5-7 in short is thus that the defendant no.2 Ayesha Khalilunnessa being the original owner of the suit land transferred I (one) "kedur" land in favour of one Hoshneara Khatun and thereafter transferred 08 decimals of land in favour of the defendant's father Forhad Hossain Chowdhury. The father of the defendants after purchasing the land erected homestead therein and constructed pacca house. After the death of Forhad Hossain Chowdhury the defendants acquired the suit land by way of inheritance and possessed the same after giving boundaries for more than thirty years but the plaintiffs only to harass the defendants creating some forged anti-dated collusive papers filed the suit which is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned trial court after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit in part in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of 05(five) decimals of land instead of 08(eight) decimals. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 90 of 1997 in the court of learned District Judge. Sylhet which was transmitted to the Court of learned Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet and the learned lower appellate court hearing the parties allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree dated 26.04.2003. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned appellate court below in disposing the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and after assessment of evidence rightly arrived at a decision that the plaintiffs are entitled to get 07(seven) decimals of land in plot No.9093 pursuant to their purchase deed and subsequent deed of the rectification. The learned Advocate further submits that the original owner of the land the defendant no.2 despite initially transferred the land in favour of the plaintiff's predecessor from two plots No. 9091 and 9093 but subsequent to that rectified the plot and asserted within the contents of the rectification deed that only from plot No.9093 the land measuring 07(seven) decimals was transferred by him. Therefore, the learned lower appellate court rightly held that the plaintiffs do get 07(seven) decimals which is their claimed land in the original suit from plot no.9093. The learned Advocate also submits that the deed of rectification dated 01.05.1980 has been duly proved which has been marked exhibit-1(ka). The learned Advocate further submits that the title deed of the defendant-petitioners which has been marked as exhibit-Ka( 1 ) go to show that the vendor transferred the area comprising 08(eight) decimals of land from two plots. 9091 and 9093 and this makes it clear that the defendant-respondent-petitioners are stopped from claiming the entire land comprising 08(eight) decimals from one plot 9093 only which has been properly decided by the lower appellate court in the impugned judgment and decree and there is no infirmity or illegality in deciding the merit of the appeal. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned appellate court in passing the impugned judgment and decree properly assessed the evidence on records and there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

 10. On perusal of the case records it transpires that admittedly the defendant no.2 Ayesha Khalilunnessa Chowdhury was the original owner of the disputed property. It is the contention of the plaintiffs that their predecessor-in-interest Abdus Sattar by a kabla deed dated 24.12.1970 purchased 07 (seven) decimals of land from the original owner and possession was delivered in favour of the purchaser Abdus Sattar and the purchaser after mutating his name paid rent. Subsequently, the vendor-defendant no.2 by a deed of rectification dated 29.03.1980 rectified the earlier transfer deed dated 24.12.1970 stating that instead of plot no. 9091 he has transferred the land only from plot No.9093. The further contention of the plaintiffs as it appears from their pleadings is such that they are possessing the land measuring 07(seven) decimals from plot No.9093 but due to difficulty in ejmoli possession with the defendants they claimed partition which was refused and thereafter they instituted the original suit. 

 11. Vis-a-vis; it was asserted by the contesting defendant-respondent-petitioners that the original owner of the property Ayesha Khalilunnessa Chowdhury on 16th Kartik, 1377 B.S. transferred 08(eight) decimals of land in favour of their predecessor-in-interest Forhad Hossain Chowdhury from the suit plots. In fact, possession was delivered from plot No.9093 despite it was written as plot no. 9091 and 9093. The further contention of the petitioners is such that their predecessor was inducted into possession after the transfer on 19.11.1970 marked Exhibit-Ka( I) in respect of the entire transferred land measuring 08 (eight) decimals and thereafter they erected their homestead with boundary wall. 

 12. The learned trial court during deciding the fate of the suit after framing use different issues held that in the original suit there is no defect of party and the suit as framed is maintainable. The plaintiffs are entitled to get an order of partition but the area of the land would he five decimals instead of 7(seven) decimals of land. It was further held by the trial court that exhibit-1(ka) which is prior to the transfer deed in favour of plaintiffs' predecessor was duly effected and the transferor owner of the land delivered possession from suit plot No.9093. The boundary of the transferred property which is cited within the content of the deed has been reflected within the averments of the witnesses as adduced from the sides of the parties. The learned court below in his findings and decision consulting the title documents of the parties arrived at a conclusive decision that the plot No. 9093 from where the defendants are possessing consists of an area 8might) decimals and the total quantum of land of the said plot as it appears from the settlement record that 43 decimals had been owned and possessed by the vendor prior to his transfer. After transfer of 38 decimals and 08(eight) decimals the property left behind cannot be more than 05(five) decimals of land and as such the boundaries which is properly described within the testimony of the witnesses makes it clear that the defendants do possess their purchased land after constructing their dwelling but and boundary wall which is admitted from the plaintiffs witnesses. The observation and findings which is cited within the contents of the judgment in deciding the issue No.3 was not properly addressed by the lower appellate court in the impugned judgment and decree. In this context; the learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners argued that under the purview of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is the mandatory duty of the appellate court to rebut the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records in the case of reversal of the decision but in the instant case apparently the lower appellate court violating the provisions of law in a evasive manner decided the fate of the suit as well as ' appeal which is an apparent error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 this regard; the decision cited from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioners reported in BLD 1983(AD)I26 have got much importance in deciding the fate of the case. Where; there is a conflict between the area of plot mentioned and the area within the boundaries of the land, the area within the boundaries found shall prevail over the area of the plot mentioned. Their Lordships decided this in the case of Md. Akkas Ali aced others Mansur Atoned and others. In this contest; the evidence led from the parties go to show that the plaintiff no.2 who deposed as witness no.1 in the original suit stated that he has instituted the original suit as because he do not possess the entire purchased land. Besides this; he has admitted that the defendant no. 1 do possess the suit land by giving wider" fencing. During cross-examination the plaintiff further admits that in his deed there is a mention `Forbad Hossain Chowdhury' who possess to the western side. The witness no.2 of the plaintiffs in his averment corroborated the boundaries by stating that to the western side the defendants possess and to the eastern side the plaintiffs possess. The other witnesses adduced during trial of the original suit were also discussed by the trial court. But it is apparent from the face of the records that the lower appellate court without evaluating the testimonies of the witnesses rebutting the findings of the trial court decided the merit of the appeal. 

 16. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 26.04.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet in title Appeal No. 90 of 1997 reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.03.1997 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gowainghat, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 30 or 1992 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Aftab Uddin (Md) ------ Appellant
Vs.
Chairman, Court of Settlement and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
4. The case of the respondent before the Court of Settlement was that the lessee, Kulsum Bibi was absent at all material times and she left the house uncared, her whereabouts were not known after emergence of Bangladesh and her whereabouts were also not known on the day, when President's Order (PO) No. 16 of 1972 came in to force. The appellant's contention of death of the lessee on 27-3-1971 leaving only her husband Abdur Rahman as the sole heir, was a story concocted by the appellant to grab the property in question. The property which the appellant was claiming became abandoned property from 28-2- 1972 and vested in the government as abandoned property. The appellant's kabala as regards that property in question having been registered without prior permission of the Ministry of Works is hit by the provision of section 6 of PO 16 of 1972, and the appellant having no right, title and interest in the property in question sought by way of exclusion of the property from the 'Kha' list of the Abandoned Buildings is not available to him and the case so filed is liable to be dis missed. 

 I "Whether the High Court Division was wrong in holding that the High Court Division is not competent in law to disturb the finding of the. court of Settlement particularly, when it is apparent that the Court of Settlement did not take into consideration the evidence on record regarding death of Kulsum Bibi and her husband Abdur Rahman, and the possession of the original documents of title by the appellant and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside; and II. Whether the learned Judge of the High Court Division while upholding the judgment and order of the Court of Settlement did not notice that the property in question could not be listed as abandoned property because Abdur Rahman, the husband of the original lessee Kulsum Bibi, was in possession thereof since her death on 27-2-1971 and on 28-2-1972 he never ceased to possess, manage and control the property which fact has been corroborated by the remarks made by the survey committee and; as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside." 

 9. Mr Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. In addition he submitted that the appellant filed all the original papers relating to the property, which were not discussed, nor properly assessed by the Court of Settlement. Even while reviewing the case, the Court of Settlement simply mentioned that documents were produced and considered, but they were not discussed nor any cogent reason given as to why they were disbelieved, especially since they have been produced from the proper custody of the applicant, who is a subsequent purchaser for value. 

 10. The learned Advocate further submitted that the appellant has been living in the disputed property since his purchase in the year 1977 and his name has been duly mutated by the proper government authority. He submitted that Abdur Rahman was the rightful owner and in possession of the disputed property after the death of his wife and legally sold the same to the appellant, which is supported by the original papers relating to the title of the property. 

 11. It appears that the appellant annexed all original documents to the concerned authority on 6-7-1985 in response to the notice dated 1-7-1985. We also note the comment of the "House to House Report of the Survey Team" who noted in the 'Remarks' column that the house in question may not be abandoned. 

 14. In view of the above facts and circumstances, particularly since the Court of Settlement did not discuss the veracity, value, weight or otherwise of the original documents produced earlier by the appellant, we are of the opinion that the matter be sent on remand to the Court of Settlement to assess the documentary evidence produced in this case and then to come to a decision in accordance with law.

parties:
Inspector of School, Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education, Dhaka and others ------Defendants- Appellants
Versus
Md. Rafiqul Islam ----- Plaintiff-Respondent
full_judgment:
12. The learned Advocate for the appellant again submits that the Plaintiff was asked to deposit defoliated money to School fund as per resolution adopted by Managing Committee the competent authority of the school which was taken in pursuance of Boards Suggestion to reconcile the matter with the plaintiff but that was not complied with by the plaintiff. The learned Advocate for the appellant then submits that the learned Court below misread the deposition of DW. 2, the DW-2 admitted in cross examination that "Abul Quashem is Headmaster in Charge "আবুল কাশেম ভারপ্রাপ্ত প্রধান শিক্ষক” The witness furthermore replied in cross that he did not accompany the plaintiff when he joined and did not see which works was done by him on that day. The learned Advocate for the appellant again submits that having regard to the fact that Managing Committee on 14.6.1999 the respondent No. 1 against suspension filed a writ petition and obtained Rule and stay order but alter hearing the Rule has been discharged, thereafter the managing Committee dismissed the Plaintiff respondent No.1 on various allegation of misconduct/ misappropriation of school fund and sought approval of the Education Board and during pendency of the same he filed a suit which was rejected as premature and not maintainable and on an appeal the High Court Division interfered with the order and directed to hear the suit on merit and as such the suit proceeded but the issue of maintainability was not resolved by the Trial Court and respondent No. 1 got the decree and in that view of the matter the trial Court committed error of law in decreeing the suit. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that the trial Court committed error of law in decreeing the suit giving emphasis of the order of injunction regard to the fact that the order of injunction was stayed by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in C.P. No.1753 of 2002 and the Appellate Division granted leave by order dated 29.1.2003 and the appellant riled C.A. I89 of 2003 and the Appellate Division extended the stay order till disposal of the said Appeal which is still pending and in such view of the matter the trial Court misconceived in coming to the finding and decision that the plaintiff/respondent is functioning at the strength of injunction granted by the High Court. The learned Advocate for the appellant lastly submits that the learned trial Court gave emphasis on the order of the High Court but failed to consider that the Hon'ble Appellate Division granted leave on the ground that the High Court Division erred in law in not following the judicial principles in respect of granting temporary injunction illegally acted on some fake and forged papers in making the Rule absolute and that resolution dated 24.12.2000 of dismissal adopted by the managing committee was sent to the Board for approval but the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Board keeping the matter in abeyance for long time directed to compromise which is without jurisdiction and the respondent No. 1 upon misleading the Court obtained the order of injunction in as much as from the date of his suspension on 14.6.99 an acting headmaster is functioning as headmaster in charge of the said school and the respondent No.1 is not entitled to have an order of injunction in as much as he has no prima-facie arguable case nor he is holding the office of the headmaster since 14.6.99 nor the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in his favour. 

 16. In the result the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 decree signed on 20.02.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court Tangail is hereby set aside and the original Title Suit No. 10 of 2002 is hereby dismissed with cost.

parties:
In the matter of: An application under Article 102 (1)(2)(a)(ii)of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh.
And
In the matter of: Government of Bangladesh ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
The Chairman, First Court of Settlement and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
The petitioner as opposite party before the Court of Settlement contested the case and claimed that one Md. Solaiman Khan was the original allottee of the case property and his whereabouts were not known and that he had left this country after independence of Bangladesh keeping the case property uncared for. The Government had taken over possession of the case property found it uncared for and had been possessing it through demand note (D. N.) holder, and the inclusion of the case property in the abandoned list was correct and legal. 

 The respondent No. 2 testified before the Court of Settlement and produced all of the original deeds and documents in support of his case by way of firisty before the Court of Settlement. The Court of Settlement on consideration of the material evidence on records allowed the case of respondent No. 2 by its judgment and order dated 06. 08. 1995. The Settlement Court allowed the case of the respondent No. 2 mainly finding that the case property had not fallen within the meaning of abandoned property as defined in Article 2(1) of P.O. 16 of 1972. 

 Mr. Fida M. Kamal, the learned Advocate submits further that the respondent No. 2 filed the case before the Court of Settlement claiming himself as Md. Solaiman Khan as the original allottee by creating some false and forged documents, whose whereabouts were not known to the Government and the Government found the case property uncared for listed it in the list of the abandoned property under Ordinance LIV of 1985 within the meaning of Article 2(1) of P.O. 16 of 1972 and handed over possession of the case property to the predecessor of respondent Nos. 3-6 as a tenant of the petitioner. 

 Mr. Abdul Salam Mondal, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing with Mr. Sukumer Biswas, the learned Assistant Attorney General on behalf of the petitioner upon referring a decision reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 submits that the Court of Settlement ought to have compared the signature of the alleged claimant (Respondent No.2) with the admitted signature of original allottee Md. Solaiman Khan available on the original lease deed and allotment latter through hand writing expert. But the Court of Settlement itself compared the signature of the alleged claimant with the signature available on the original deed which should not be taken into consideration as a mode of proof and the High Court Division can interfere with those perverted findings of the Court of Settlement in writ jurisdiction. 

 Mr. Mondol, the learned D.A.G submits further that when the original allottee Md. Soliman Khan left this country keeping the case property uncared for and when his whereabouts were not known to the Government and he had ceased to occupy, supervise and manage the case property in person at the very relevant time i.e. on 28.2.1972 the Government had rightly declared the case property as abandoned property within the mischief of the Article 2(1) of P.O No.16 of 1972 and listing of the case property in the abandoned list is conclusive proof of facts. 

 Mr. Mondal, the learned D.A.G submits further that mere keeping the original allotment latter and lease deed do not prove that the allottee was present in Bangladesh at the very relevant point when P.O. 16 of 1972 came into operation and that he used to occupy and supervise the case property in person or through his agents Mr. Mondol, the learned D.A.G finally submits that the respondent No.2 is none but a fake and fictitious person and filed the case only to grab the abandoned property claiming him as the original allottee but the Court of Settlement failed to consider those aspects and hence the judgment of the Court of Settlement should be declared to be illegal, without lawful authority, and is of no legal effect. 

 On the other hand Mr. Joynul Abedin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent No.2 submits that the Court of Settlement having considered the original title deeds and other documents of this respondent came to a conclusion that the case property had not fallen within the mischief of Article 2(1) of P.O 16 of 72 and as such nothing to interfere with the judgment of the Court of Settlement invoking writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution, unless judgment of the Court of Settlement suffers from any illegality or without jurisdiction. 

 Mr. Abedin, the learned Advocate submits further that the Court of Settlement compared the signature of the respondent No.2 (claimant) with the available signature in the admitted documents and came to a conclusion that the signature of the respondent No.2 is genuine and also found that the respondent No.2 Md. Soliman Khan is the original allottee of the case property and as such nothing to interfere with the judgment of the Court of Settlement. 

 The Court of Settlement allowed the case of the respondent No.2 mainly finding that the claimant of the case property is the original allottee who has been able to prove his case by producing the original deeds and documents himself. The Settlement Court also in its own initiative compared the signature of the claimant with the admitted signature available on the original lease deed and the case petition. 

 In the instant case the Court of Settlement upon proper consideration of the materials on record found that the original allottee is present in this country and the petitioner-Government did not make any attempt to controvert this fact. As such, there cannot be any reason to say that the whereabouts of the respondent No.2 is not known for the purpose of treating the case property as abandoned. Moreover, property of a Bangladeshi National cannot be treated as abandoned property without any proof of taking active part against the liberation war or he helped military operation against the state and the Government of Bangladesh in 1971.Therefore, the property in question under no circumstances falls within the purview of P.O. 16 of 1972 read with the Ordinance LIV of 1985 and hence nothing to interfere with the judgment of the Court of Settlement.

caseno: First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 with Civil Revision Nos. 2755, 4769 of 2010.
parties:
Agrani Bank Ltd. ----- Appellant
Vs.
Samsad Asif and two others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 arises out of Title Suit No.280 of 1994 which was instituted on 30-11-1994 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka by Agrani Bank Ltd. as plaintiff impleading Shamsad Asif, Nowshad Asif and Ershad Asif as main defendant Nos. 1-3 respectively, while Abidur Rahman, Al-Baraka Bank Ltd. Rajdhani Unnoyun Katripaka, M/s Goldhil Tobaco Complex Ltd. M/s Nippon Traders Ltd. and M/s Nippon Motors Ltd. as pro-defendant Nos.4-10 respectively. The aforesaid defendant Nos. 8-10 were represented by their Managing Director Abidur Rahman who has also been impleaded as defendant No. 4 in the suit. The subject matter involved in the suit is being described as under:- 

 5. The defendant No.5 Al-Baraka Bank upon filing a separate written statement on 17-6-1997 denied the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit land was leased out to one Mr Tashfin I Huq for 99 years by Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) on 6-12-1965 at a consideration of Taka 12,107 and got possession; thereafter said Mr Tashfim I Huq gifted away the property in question in favour of his wife Ms Shahana Huq and the donee got her name recorded with the DIT in respect of the suit land and also constructed a double storied building thereon; in 1973 Ms Shahana Huq transferred the suit property in favour of defendant Nos. 1-3 at a consideration of Taka 2 (two) lacs with prior approval of DIT by a registered deed dated 30-11-1973 and the purchasers got possession and they had also mutated their names in the office of the DLR as leasee thereof; in 1989 one Mr Masudur Rahman proprietor of Masud Enterprise applied for Bai-Muajjal facility of Taka 1.50 crore to defendant Nos. 5 and the facility was sanctioned by defendant No. 5 against collateral security of legal and equitable mortgage of the suit property recorded in the name of the defendant Nos. 1-3; the guarantors of the loan as per rules of DIT and terms of the lease deed (the defendant Nos. 1-3) applied for permission to create legal and equitable mortgage in favour of Al-Baraka Bank (BD) Ltd. and the same was approved by DIT vide Memo dated 7-2-1989; the defendant 1-3 also submitted non encumbrance certificate to defendant No. 5 thereafter registered deed of mortgage dated 2-6-1990 and equitable mortgage by deposing all registered documents with the defendant No. 5 was created; the defendant Nos. 1-3 also executed a registered irrevocable general power of attorney dated 2-5-1990 in favour of defendant No. 5 in respect of the suit land; the defendant after inquiry of the DIT records and title deed, created a mortgage deed of the suit property as security of the loan which was repayable within one year. 

 6. Similarly one Anwarul Huq, proprietor of M/s Anwar Trading Co. applied for Muajjal facility of one crore to the defendant No. 5 which was sanctioned on 30-12-1989 against collateral security of equitable mortgage of the suit property of defendant Nos. 1-3 i.e. guarantor of the loan; those loan was also repayable within one year; after sometimes defendant Nos. 1 -3 created equitable and legal mortgage of the suit property in favour of the defendant No. 5 and also executed a registered irrevocable general power of attorney in favour of this defendant No. 5; that the suit property therefore legally and bonafide stands as security of the facilities granted by the defendant No. 5 on the above account; the defendant No. 5 also acted bonafide in creating mortgage of the suit land and being satisfied and after inspecting the title deed and the records of DIT accepted the security as aforesaid and completed all legal formalities: the borrowers, Masud Enterprise and Anwar Trading Co failed to adjust the dues of the answering defendant and for these reasons this defendant filed two separate Mortgage Suits being Title Suit No. 80 of 1992 and 81 of 1992 respectively in the Court of 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka and the court decreed both the suits in preliminary form and thereafter final decree was drawn directing sale of the suit property; this defendant has also filed execution case for sale of the schedule property as per mortgage deed which were pending for disposal; it was also disclosed in the written statement by the defendant No. 5 that the plaintiff has no charge whatsoever over the suit land nor defendant Nos.1-3 executed any mortgage in favour of the plaintiff; it was also disclosed in the writ-ten statement that the attachment order of the court in Money Execution Case filed in 1993 having created no right in favour of the plaintiff as against prior mortgage in favour of answering defendant No. 5; the plaintiff cannot claim first charge on the basis of subsequent attachment against the earlier mortgage charge, therefore, the defendant No. 5 prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 8. It may be mentioned that the original Title Suit No.280 of 1994 was eventually re-numbered as Title Suit 35 of 2001 on transfer before the learned Joint District Judge and 1st Additional Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka. During pendency of the appeal, on 6-8-2010 one Aminul Huq son of late Lutfor Rahman got himself impleaded as respondent No. 3(a) of this appeal and subsequently on 18-8-2010 Sonali Bank Ltd. got itself added as respondent 3(b) in this appeal. 

 9. Civil Revision No. 2755 of 2010 has been brought by Agrani Bank as decree holder petitioner impleading M/s Goldhill Fibers Ltd.; Abidur Rahman as judgment debtor opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, Sonali Bank as 3rd party opposite party No. 3 and Aminul Hoq auction purchaser as opposite party No.4, against order No. 121 dated 20-6-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 in Artha Jari Case No. 79 of 2010 (re-numbered) staying writ of delivery of possession to be given to the petitioner bank, stating inter alia in the said revisional application as under:- that the petitioner bank as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 16 of 1985 on 24-6-1985 before the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj for recovery of Taka 31,33,664 against the opposite party Nos.1 and 2; the said suit was decreed ex parte on 5-6-1986; the said decree was put into execution in Money Execution Case No. 71 of 1988 on 9-4-1988 before the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj; thereafter said decree was sent to the court of District Judge, Dhaka for execution on the basis of no objection certificate; accordingly Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 was started on 14-8-1988 before the Sub-ordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka (at present Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka) for recovery of decretal dues amounting to Taka 45,65,182 as on 6-4-1988; the property measuring 14 khatas 15 chataks situated at House No. 33, Block CEN(H) Road No. 114, Gulshan Model Town belonging to the judgment debtor No. 2 Mr Abidur Rahman was included in the schedule of the execution case; after obtaining a contested decree for benami declaration dated 21-4-2002 against three sons of judgment debtor (benamder) in Title Suit No. 190 of 1999 before the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka; the revisional application also contains similar averments as made in the plaint of the Title Suit out of which the instant First Appeal is pending, therefore, skipped over to avoid repetition, it was also stated in the said revisional application that the decree holder petitioner bank on 15-9-2009 filed an application for issuance of writ of delivery of possession of the attached property to the decree holder Agrani Bank since the aforesaid property had already been attached in the execution case brought by the petitioner bank; the said application was allowed by the executing court on 17-11-2009 issued writ of delivery of possession for giving possession to the decree holder fixing 14-1-2010 for service return; thereafter Sonali Bank opposite party No. 3 filed an application on 25-11-2009 for recalling the writ of delivery of possession whereupon the executing court allowed the prayer exparte vide order No. 107 dated 25-11-2009; accordingly writ was recalled; thereafter the petitioner bank as decree holder filed written objection stating inter alia that the property in question could not be sold in auction because of shockingly low price quoted by the bidders, therefore, on the prayer of the decree holder bank a certificate of enjoyment and possession and sale under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 was issued in favour of the decree holder petitioner bank; eventually the writ of delivery of possession was also given in favour of the petitioner bank; thereafter Sonali Bank filed an application for recalling of the delivery of possession which after hearing both sides was allowed by the impugned order maintaining the previous order dated 25-11-2009, therefore, the instant Civil Revision has been brought challenging the said order No. 121 dated 20-6-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka. 

 11. Civil Revision No. 4762 of 2010 has been brought by Sonali Bank as petitioner impleading Al-Baraka Bank Ltd as decree holder opposite party No. 1, M/s Gold hill Fibers Ltd and Abidur Rahman as judgment debtor opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 Md Aminul Huq auction purchaser as opposite party No. 4 challenging order No. 133 dated 14-10-2010 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka refusing to cancel the certificate issued earlier in favour of decree holder opposite party No. 1 under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in Artha Jari Case No. 79 of 2010 (previously Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988); the said revisional application by Sonali Bank has been brought stating inter alia that the Sonali Bank allowed loan in favour of opposite party No. 3 Abidur Rahman from London Branch of the Bank but he defaulted in payment of the loan; the Queen's Bench Division of UK decreed the suit in 1984 against him for an amount of 4,14,323.79 sterling/ pound; there was no appeal against the said decree of the Queen's Bench Division. Therefore, it was put to execution as money execution suit No. 23 of 1987 in the 1st Commercial Court, Dhaka since that was a foreign decree; thereafter on a direction from the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 7238 of 1989 execution case was filed before the District Judge, Dhaka; accordingly it was transferred to the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka and was renumbered as Money Execution Case No.2 of 1989; thereafter on 15-10-1990 the said property was attached by the learned District Judge in the said execution case; the judgment debtor Abidur Rahman challenged the order No. 24 dated 15-10-1990 before the High Court Division in Civil Revision which was rejected in Civil Order No.2276 of 1990; the said order was also upheld by the Appellate Division by its judgment and order dated 23-5-1991 passed in Civil Petition No.386 of 1990; thereafter one of the three sons of Abidur Rahman namely, Nowshad Asif filed an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1992; but after hearing said Miscellaneous Case was rejected on 27-3-1995; against the said order Civil Revision No. 2279 of 1995 was preferred and rule was issued but after hearing the said rule was also discharged on 7-8-1996; the executing court found the decree holder, Abidur Rahman as the owner of the attached property and his three sons are his benamders; the said finding of the executing court was also affirmed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2279 of 1995 against which Nowshad Asif did not prefer any appeal; thereafter Samsad Asif, another son of Abidur Rahman preferred Civil Revision No. 1084 of 1999 challenging an order of the executing court rejecting his prayer for stay of all further proceedings in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 on the plea of pendency of Writ Petition No. 2795 of 1998 and 2796 of 1998 till disposal of execution case No. 58-60 of 1995 arising out of Title Suit Nos. 80 and 81 of 1992 and Title Suit No. 223 of 1998 but after hearing the said rule was eventually discharged by judgment arid order dated 10-3-2002 passed by this Court in Civil Revision No. 1084 of 1999; after discharge of the aforesaid rule the execution case proceeded and the attached property was sold in auction on 10-7-2006 to the auction purchaser Md Aminul Huq, the opposite party No. 4, who purchased the same at Taka 3,11,00,000; he also paid taxes and fees in this connection to the tune of Taka 3,12,000. 

 13. In Civil Revision No.3982 of 2009 arising out of Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2009 filed by Agrani Bank Ltd. High Court Division when making the rule absolute on 24-3-2010 directed the executing court to hear the Miscellaneous Case No.3 of 2009 within two weeks on the point of limitation which has been complied by the executing court within time; eventually by its order dated 4-5-2010 dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2009 filed by Agrani Bank on the ground of limitation; against the said order dated 4-5-2010 Agrani Bank preferred FMAT No. 379 of 2010 before this court which was also dismissed by the judgment and order dated 26-7-2010 passed by a Division Bench of this Court; in the meantime the opposite party No. 1, Agrani Bank obtained a money decree against the opposite party Nos.2 and 3 in Money Suit No. 16 of 1985 and eventually brought Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 before the 1st Commercial Court, Dhaka; said execution case was renumbered as Artha Jari Case No.79 of 2010 which has been pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka; in the said Money Execution Case, the land of Tejkunipara mouza was included in the schedule of the case but, subsequently, Agrani Bank Ltd. upon an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure included the attached land of Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 in Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 on 12-9-2002; thereafter Agrani Bank obtained certificate under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 in respect of the said attached land on 13-11-2004; thereafter on 27-11-2005 Money Execution Case No. 177 of 1988 was finally disposed of; thereafter Samsad Asif son of judgment debtor, Abidur Rahman preferred writ petition No. 448 of 2005 before this Court against order dated 27-11-2005 and two other orders claiming himself as co-owner of the said property; but after hearing of the said writ petition rule was discharged holding that Samsad Asif is not the co-owner of the said property and affirmed the certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 in favour of Agrani Bank; Agrani Bank had knowledge about the attachment of the said property in execution case No.2 of 1989 from 23-6-2002 but knowing about the said attachment of the property they obtained the order of attachment of the said land in Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 on 23-9-2002 and on the basis of such illegal attachment they obtained certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003; Agrani Bank obtained order of delivery of possession of the said property in their favour in Money Execution Case No. 79 of 2010 and the petitioner filed an application for recalling the said order of delivery of possession with a prayer for releasing the property from attachment and for deleting the schedule land from the plaint of the execution case whereupon executing court after hearing the parties by his order dated 20-6-2010 recalled the order of delivery of possession but rejected the prayer for releasing the property from attachment upon holding that since the certificate under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 has been issued the property is not in attachment, therefore, the same cannot be attached; there-after the petitioner on 30-6-2010 filed another application for cancellation of the said certificate obtained by Agrani Bank stating all the material facts upon filing all necessary papers; the Agrani Bank filed a written objection against the said application dated 20-6-2010 but they did not deny the facts that they brought Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 2002 for setting aside the exparte decree in Title Suit No.297 of 2001; thereafter the learned Joint District Judge after hearing the parties rejected the said application by his impugned order dated 14-2-2010 which has been challenged in the instant rule. 

 14. The opposite party No. 1 Agrani Bank entered appearance upon filing a counter affidavit denying the material allegations made in the petition stating inter alia that Agrani Bank allowed loan in favour of opposite party No.2 M/s Goldhill Fibers Ltd. of which the Managing Director was opposite party No. 3 Abidur Rahman; he defaulted in repayment of the loan as such the opposite party No.1 Agrani Bank Limited brought Title Suit No. 16 of 1985 against them for realization of the said loan and eventually suit was decreed against the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 as such Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 was brought by the opposite party No. 1 which was renumbered as Artha Jari Case No. 79 of 2010 which has been pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka; the said land was included in the schedule of Money Execution Case which was attached thereafter Agrani Bank obtained Certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 on 30-11-2004; on 27-11-2005 the said Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 was disposed of; thereafter one son of Abidur Rahman the judgment debtor namely Samsad Asif preferred Writ Petition No. 448 of 2005 challenging the said order dated 27-1-2005 which after hearing the rule was discharged affirming the certificate issued under section 33(5) in favour of Agrani Bank and subsequently, the opposite-party No. 1 obtained order of delivery of possession of the said property in their favour in Money Execution Case No.79 of 2010; it was also asserted on oath in the said counter affidavit that Sonali Bank Ltd. practiced fraud upon the court beyond the knowledge of opposite party No. 1 and attached the said property in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 filed by the petitioner and was sold in auction on 10-7-2006 to the auction purchaser Md Aminul Huq the opposite party No. 4; thereafter the petitioner filed application for cancellation of the said certificate in favour of the opposite party No. 1 and after hearing the learned Joint District Judge rejected the said application by his order dated 24-10-2010 which has been impugned in the instant rule. 

 19. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5, that the ingredients of the Benami transaction as laid down by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 61 DLR (AD) 133 the factum of intention to create benami, possession of property, possession of title deeds having not been raised or decided by the executing court earlier the question of res judicata is not applicable in Title Suit No. 35 of 2001. 

 20. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5 that the execution having no jurisdiction to decide the issue of title to property or the question of Benami transaction in a proceeding under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure the principle of res judicata is not applicable to Title Suit No. 35 of 2001 filed by Agrani Bank against which the instant appeal has been brought. 

 28. Mr Islam, further submits that a proceeding under Order XXI, rule 58 is not a summary proceeding it should be treated a regular suit. All questions including the question of title and right of the claimants have to be adjudicated, separate suit for decision on title or right is barred. 

 37. In this connection it may be pointed out that the said property was mortgaged in favour of Al-Baraka Bank on 2-6-1990 by defendant Nos. 1-3 (sons of Abidur Rahman) and Sonali Bank got the same land attached in its execution cases on 15-10-1990 while Agrani Bank also got the same land attached in execution of its case on 12-1-2001 and in view of the position as above, we find that the registered mortgage deed obtained by Al-Baraka Bank in respect of the self same land took place earliest in point of time and attachment of the Sonali Bank comes in the 2nd position and the attachment made by Agrani Bank falls in the 3rd position. We have also noticed that Al-Baraka Bank obtained the deed of mortgage in respect of the said property from the ostensible owners thereof as guarantor to the loan granted in favour of two companies both by legal mortgage and by equitable mortgage upon depositing all original deeds in respect of the property to the custody of the said bank. We have also noticed that Al-Baraka Bank has taken all reasonable care and caution to ascertain that the defendant Nos. 1-3 had power to make the mortgage as such Al-Baraka had acted in good faith therefore the mortgage in favour of Al-Baraka Bank by defendant Nos. 1-3 is no doubt protected by section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act. We are of the opinion that the question posed as above, lost its efficacy particularly in view of the fact that the judgment of the said two civil revisions namely Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 and Civil Revision No. 2755 of 2010 passed by the High Court Division complying the principle of res judicata were set aside by their lordships in the Appellate Division in their aforesaid judgment and in the context aforesaid Al-Baraka Bank cannot but be treated as a secured creditor. 

 47.
