Turning to the merit of the First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 and the connected two Civil Revisions namely CR No. 2755 of 2010 and Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 it may be pointed out further that we have gone through the impugned judgment and on perusal of the judgment passed in Title Suit No.35 of 2001 we find that it is a well reasoned judgment passed on consideration of the evidence and materials placed before the learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Court No. 1, Dhaka and the learned Judge meticulously considered the evidence both oral and documentary upon arriving at a positive finding to substantiate the impugned judgment and consequent decree, therefore, it call for no interference by this court. Hence we find no merit in this appeal.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1928 of 2010
parties:
Md. Bande Ali Miah being dead his heirs: 1(a) Payesy Begum and others ------- Petitioners
VS
The Chief Engineer, Housing and Settlement, Directorate of Housing and Settlement, Segun Bagicha, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, as plaintiff, filed Title Suit No. 61 of 1999 against the respondents for perpetual injunction. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that Zayor Bibi was the original owner of the "Ka" schedule land mentioned in the plaint. In 1959-60 vide L.A. Case No. 13 the defendants acquired the said land for rehabilitation of the refugees migrated from India. That the Government assured Zayor Bibi that she would be given proper compensation and alternative land and she would not be evicted till doing so. But the said land was never used for the purpose for which it was acquired and as such Zayor Bibi applied for de-requisition of the said land for several times. But no step was taken by the Government for de-requisition of the same. Zayor Bibi, however, had been possessing the said lands excepting the land which was used for construction of a road. That after independence Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms vide Memo No.  L.A.29/72/46736 dated 23.07.1972 ordered that all arrears of acquired land should be paid by 31.08.1972, otherwise all acquisitions should be deemed to be cancelled. That since the compensation money of the suit land was not paid within 31.08.1972 the acquisition of the same land was cancelled. Then on 27.04.1979 Zayor Bibi sold out 30 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff by a registered deed and the plaintiff was also inducted into the possession of that land and since then the plaintiff had been residing in that land by paying holding tax regularly. In 1979 and lastly on 19.03.1991 the defendants threatened the plaintiff with dispossession and thus the plaintiff was compelled to file the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 3, 5 and 6 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and there was no cause of action for the suit. The case of the defendants, in short, was that the suit land was acquired in 1960 which was published in the gazette on 18.12.1980. That the original owner of the suit land had been allotted a plot on 20.07.1979 and compensation also was given to the original owner. That a 120 feet wide road has been constructed on the suit land and the plaintiffs are not residing in the suit land. 

 5. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties, decreed the suit holding that since before completion of the process of acquisition the plaintiff purchased the suit land from the original owner he acquired right and title in the suit land and that the plaintiff had been the possessing suit land also. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial court the Chief Engineer, Housing and Settlement, Directorate of Housing and Settlement filed Title Appeal No. 99 of 2000 in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka, which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Subordinate Judge and Artharin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka. 

 7. The appellate court affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court holding the same view that since the plaintiff purchased the suit land from the original owner before acquisition of the same by the Government the plaintiff acquired right and title in the suit land and he had also been possessing the same. Against this judgment of the appellate court the appellant filed the above mentioned Civil Revision No. 1606 of 2001 and obtained the Rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, on hearing the learned Advocate for the appellant-petitioner and considering the facts and circumstances and relevant laws, made the Rule absolute making, observations to the effect that the suit land was admittedly acquired by the Government by gazette notification and holding that "once a property is acquired and Gazette Notification is published under Section 5(7) of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, the right, title and interest, if any, of the owners are extinguished". 

 11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and considered the matter. Admittedly, 94 decimals of land including the claimed lands of the plaintiffs of plot No. 63 of mouza Bisily under P.S. Mirpur, District-Dhaka along with other lands were acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No. 13 of 1959-60 for the purpose of rehabilitation of the refugee migrated from India and this acquisition, was published by Gazette Notification. The plaintiffs case that the suit land was not used for the purpose for which it was acquired and as such the plaintiffs are entitled to get return of the suit land is not acceptable at all After acquisition of any land by the Government as per provision of law the Government becomes the absolute owner of that land and all right, title and interest of the original owners in the acquired land are extinguished. In the present case the plaintiff though, before the trial court and the appellate court, pleaded a case to the effect that their predecessor-in-interest purchased the suit land from the original owner Zayor Bibi before completion of acquisition process and as such their predecessor-in-interest acquired valid right, title and possession in the suit land but before this Division the learned Advocate for the petitioners did not press any such case. Mr. M. G. Bhuiya, the learned Advocate for the petitioners has submitted before as to the effect that subsequently, in the year 2002, the Government has made order releasing 30 decimals of land of the plaintiff and has also ordered for Gazette Notification of the said release of the land from acquisition and in this circumstance the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree as prayed. To substantiate this submission of the learned Advocate photocopies of some orders allegedly issued from the Land Ministry only have been filed with an additional paper book, but the petitioners could not file any Gazette Notification showing that actually their claimed 30 decimals of land have been released or returned to them by the Government. 

 13. However, we find that the High Court Division was very much correct in holding that after acquisition of the suit land by the Government in accordance with law and handing over the same to the requiring authority namely, Directorate of Housing; and Settlement, Dhaka, no legal or vested right can accrue in favour of the original owner or the plaintiff the alleged purchaser from the original owner by mere Inter Ministerial Communications. The revisional court rightly found also that the alleged possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land was illegal and the plaintiff being mere trespasser in the suit land cannot get any protection of law to retain his illegal possession, if any, in the suit land.

full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in-short, are that the present appellants as plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 23 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal imp leading the defendants for declaration of title on the averments that one Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was owner of the suit land appertaining to CS Dag Nos.1194 and 1195 of Mouza Charvaduria measuring about 17.33 acres of land, who took settlement by executing a registered kabuliyat in favour of the then Government on 7-11-21. At the time of taking settlement of the suit land Abdul Kader Mia was a seasonal but collector of khash mohal; that Abdul Kader Mia died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs while he was in service; that Abdul Kader Mia in connection with his service posted different station in which he assigned his full brother defendant No. 2 to look after the suit property; that the defendant No.  2 with ill motive got the suit land recorded in the name of the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia in equal share, that is, 3 arenas 4 gandas share; that the preparation of RS Khatian in the name of defendant Nos. 1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia was collusive and without any legal basis; that on the basis of wrong RS Khatian, the SA Khatian has also been pre-pared wrongly in the name of the defendants and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land in which the defendant Nos. 1-4, in-fact, have no right, title or legal interest whatsoever; that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was the exclusive owner of the suit land, who used to possess the suit land through different bargadars on the basis of barga Kabuliyats and after the death of Abdul Kader Mia, the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land through different bargadars on payment of rent to the Government; that the plaintiffs demanded Nadabinama or Multiparty in respect of the suit land in which the defendants Nos.1-4 have not tile or interest whatsoever but the defendant Nos.1-4 refused to execute any Nadabi  Muktipatra in their favour in respect of the suit land on 27th poush, 1384 BS; that the preparation of the wrong record of rights have cast a cloud upon the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence, the suit for declaration of title. 

 3. The defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint con-tending, inter alia, that Abdul Latif, the father of defendant Nos. 1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his eldest son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs; that Abdul Latif, the predecessor of the defendants got the suit land recorded during the time of PS operation of the year 1925 in Khatian No. 34 in the name of Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs to maintain benami character; that Abdul Latif Mia was a forester under Khas Mohal, when he took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his minor son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs; that Abdul Latif Mia during his life time was in possession of the suit property on payment of rent to the Government; that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a minor school going student during the RS operation of the years, 1925 and was in joint mess with his father Abdul Latif in the year 1925; that Abdul Kader Mia had no source of income to take settlement of the suit land and he never possessed the suit land before the death of his father Abdul Latif Mia; that the kabulyat dated 7-11-21 was executed and registered in the name of Abdul Kader Mia by false percolation; that Abdul Latif Mia died before RS operation and Abdul Kader Mia the predecessor of the plaintiffs used to look after the property of his father; that Abdul Kader Mia got the suit land recorded in the name of his 5(five) brothers. The daughters of Abdul Latif Mia relinquished their claim in the suit land and thereupon, the suit land was recorded in the name of 5(five) brothers including Abdul Kader Mia in equal share in which they are in possession; that the SA operation has also been made correctly in the name of the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia in equal share; that the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs are in possession in the suit property in equal share on payment of rent to the Government; that the RS and SA khatian have been correctly prepared in the name of defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in equal share; that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit property relating to the shares of defendant Nos.1-4 and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. The learned trial Judge on consideration of the materials on record by his judgment and decree dated 29-8-1980 (decree signed on 4-9-1980) dismissed the suit mainly on 3 (three) counts: (1) that the suit is hopelessly barred by law of limitation. (2) that Abdul Kader Mia took settlement of the suit land in the became of his eldest son Kader Mia, who was a minor as per his service book (Exhibit 9) and the evidence of PW 1. (3) that the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land. 

 8. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellants in the course of his argument has taken us through the impugned judgment and decree, deposition of witnesses, exhibits and other materials on record and then submits that the findings of the trial Court below that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs had no source of income at the time of execution of kabuliyat dated 7-11-21 (Exhibit l) while he was a school going boy, his father Abdul Latif Mia took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his eldest son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs is perverse being contrary to the material evidence on record. He next submits that the trial Court below having failed to consider the vital aspects of the case that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land from the then government on 7-11-21 and he executed and registered Kabuliyat in favour of landlord on 7-11-1921 and to prove the case the original Kabulyat was called for from the collector ate on 11-8-1979 vide order No. 27, Kabulyat was exhibited as Exhibit 1 and the settlement was acted upon vide Exhibit Nos. 1A-1G that is the chronological registered barga kabulyat which were given by abraders in favour of Abdul Kader Mia and in those deeds including Exhibit 1 the occupation of Abdul Kader has been consistently stated as service holder. He further submits that the trial Court without assigning any sound reason most illegally ignored all registered documents (exhibits "1 and 1A-1G series") which were produced from the custody of the plaintiffs and those documents are more than 30 years old documents and have strong presumptive value as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act. 

 9. Mr Md Nurul Amin, further submits that the finding of the trial Court on the point of limitation is totally perverse inasmuch as the plaintiff's suit is for simple declaration of title and the proposition of law is well settled that the limitation will start not from the date of publication of record of right, so long any dispute as to title and possession is not raised there is no reason to institute a suit and in the present case it is apparent from the record that the title of the plaintiffs was threatened in the year 1977 and the suit was filed in the year 1978 and therefore, the suit is not barred by limitation. He adds that the wrong record of right by itself does not constitute a ground of limitation, when the title is threatened or evasion only then the cause of action would arise but the trial Court below failed to appreciate this simple point of law. 

 10. Mr Nurul Amin, further submits that the findings of the trial Court on the point of possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land is not only against the weight of evidence on record also contrary to the well settled principle of law inasmuch. as admittedly in the present case the SA and RS record was prepared in the name of the defendants along with the name of the plaintiffs but the defendants never paid any rent to the Government, on the other hand, the PW 1, Hanif Miah used to pay rent to the Government regularly vide exhibit 2A-2F starting from 1954 to 1975 and those rent receipts are evidence of possession and the same should be used as collateral evidence of title. He further points out that the plaintiff-appellants by adducing sufficient evidence both oral and documentary have been successfully proved their right, title and possession over the suit land and on the other hand, the defendant could not show any scrap of paper in support of their title and possession in the suit land but the trial Court below without considering the vital and ancient documents namely exhibit 1 and 2 series mechanically dismissed the suit which resulted in the failure of justice. 

 12. Mr Md Nurul Amin, finally relying on the decision reported in 1 XP (AD) 73 submits that the original title deed is in the name of, Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiff-appellants and on the basis of that registered kabuliyat PS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Kader Mia but subsequently SA and RS record was prepared in the name of the defendants and in such situation the conflicting between kabala and khatian the earlier registered kabuliyat prevails over the subsequent record of rights in RS khatian and SA khatian. 

 13. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate on the other hand, appearing for the defendant respondents in the course of argument after placing the impugned judgment and decree submits that the trial Court below after discussion of the evidence on record rightly arrived at a finding that Abdul Latif Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants settled the suit property in the name of his minor son Abdul Kader Mia because he was govt. servant and it was possessed by Abdul Latif Mia during his life time and later on, his five sons possessed equally and accordingly RS and SA khatian was prepared in the name of five brothers at the instance of Abdul Kader Mia himself and all of them used to pay rent jointly. Mr Abdul Quayum, next submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, Barisal after discussion of the evidence on record rightly dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29-8-1980 on the findings that the suit is barred by limitation and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a minor as per statement of PW 1 admitted is his evidence that his father was a student of Class X in 1925 in BM School as well as the service book of Abdul Kader Mia (Exhibit 9) shows his date of birth in 1904 and the suit is barred under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiffs do not have exclusive possession over the suit land. Mr Abdul Quayum, further submits that the plaintiffs tried to establish that the kabulyat dated 7-11-1921 is a registered document and the original was called for vide order No. 27 dated 11-8-1979 but there is no order or arrival of such record and there is nothing on record to show that registered kabulyat was produced before the Court below rather the kabulyat marked as "Exhibit 1" is an unregistered kabulyat and it was not proved by any manner as provided in the Evidence Act whatsoever. 

 14. He further upon placing the written objection filed by the only contesting defendant No.  2 and the evidence of DWs submits that the contesting defendant No. 2 pleaded that their father Abdul Latif Mia was a Government servant so he took settlement in the benami of his minor son from his own fund and possessed the same and after his death his 5 sons used to possess it and accordingly it has been recorded in RS and SA khatian and in that view of the matter the intention, motive and source of money, possession dealing with, preparation of RoR all the ingredients of benami transaction has been proved by the defendants by adducing evidence both oral and documentary. 

 16. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides at length and perused the evidence and materials on record including the impugned judgment and deposition of witnesses. Now, in order to resolve the disputes, let us examine first how far the learned Subordinate Judge was justified to dismiss the suit on the findings that Abdul Kader, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a benamder and the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land. 

 23. In view of the above evidence both oral and documentary there is nothing on record to suggest that the plaintiffs are not in possession. Rather, the exhibited rent receipts and registered deeds in respect of the suit land demonstrate that the possession of plaintiff-appellants in the suit land. 

 24. In consideration of this material evidence on record and facts, our view is there-fore, that the reasons given by the trial Court below for passing the impugned judgment on the point that Abdul Kuader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a benamder and the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land are not sustainable either in law or on facts. Furthermore, in his connection it may be mentioned that a kabuliyat (Exhibit 1) executed and registered in 1921 creates a presumption that the registration authority under the then British Government was satisfied that the executants Abdul Kader Mia was squarely a valid citizen to execute the kabuliyat (Exhibit 1). 

 26. We have already indicated that in view of the evidence both oral and documentary on the point of possession there is nothing on record to suggest that the plaintiffs are not in possession. PW 1, Hanif Miah used to pay rent to the Government regularly vide exhibit 2A to 2F starting from 1954-1975 and those rent receipts are evidence of possession. On examination of the rent receipts vide exhibit 2A to 2F together with the evidence of PWs and DWs. We are unable to agree with the finding of the trial Court that the suit was barred by law of limitation as well as barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession in the suit land within 12 years from before the date of filing of the suit. This finding of the trial Court below appears to be perverse and the same does not deserve to be sustained. 

 27. The proposition of law is well settled that the limitation will start not from the date of publication of record of right, so long any dispute as to title and possession is not raised and in the present case it is found from the record that the title of the plaintiffs was threatened in the year 1977 and the suit has been filed in 1978 and thus, the suit is not barred by limitation. Mr Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate in the facts and circumstance of the case rightly pointed out that the wrong record of right by itself does not constitute a ground of limitation, when the title is threatened or evasion only then the cause of action would arise but the trial Court below having failed to appreciate this simple point of law. We are inclined to agree with Mr Nurul Amin. 

 29. To meet the last branch of argument of Mr Abdul Quayum, we have carefully examined the entire evidence on record and it appears that at the trial both the parties admitted in their respective testimony that Exhibit 1, kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921 executed and registered by Abdul Kader Mia. It also appears that out of 4 defendants only defendant No.  2 (DW 2) Rafiqul Alam alias Rafiqul Islam contested the suit by filing written statement, who in his written statement as well as evidence admitted about the registration of the kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921. 

 30. Upon a scrutiny of the evidence on record, it appears that the Exhibit 1, kabulyat dated 7-11-1921 is admittedly a registered document of 1921, the defendants also claimed their title by virtue of the same kabuliyat (exhibit-1). No dispute was raised in the trial Court as to its registration nor nay finding on this point in the judgment of the Subordinate Judge, Barisal. The records shows that the trial Court called for the original kabuliyat from the Collectoriate. Therefore, we do not find any substance in the last branch of argument of Mr. Abdul Quayum that the kabuliyat (Exhibit 1) is an unregistered document particularly when the same is nobody's case. 

 32. Be that as it may, the records of rights of the Government which at best are evidence of possession at the time when such records are prepared and not an evidence of title. This is a well-established principle of law. A registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights, until and unless such kabala/kabuliyat is cancelled on a specific allegation of fraud by any civil court in an appropriate civil suit. 

 35. On an overall consideration of the facts, circumstances and the materials on record, we are of the opinion that the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court below suffers from illegalities in many folds, it cannot be sustained in law and is liable to be set-aside. 

 Let a copy of the judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

lawyer:
MA Azim Khair; Advocate -----For the Appellant (in FA No. 48 of 1999) 
Mohiuddin Ahmed. Advocate -----For the Appellant (in FA No. 330 of 1999) 
Probir Halder, Advocate -----For the Appellant (In FA No. 203 of 1999)

parties:
Shamsul Hossain ----- Appellant
Vs.
Anwar Hossain and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: These three appeals, First Appeal No. 48 of 1999 by Samsul Hasan alias Md Hasan Samsuzzaman, defendant No.5, auction purchaser, FA No. 203 of 1999 by Anowarand others plaintiffs and FA No. 330 of 1999 by Government of Bangladesh, represented by Secretary, Ministry of Jute Corporation directed against a single Judgment passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, first Court, Narayangonj decreeing Title Suit No.10 of 1997 in part as:- 

 2. The plaint case, in short, is that "Ka" schedule land was originally belonged to Sree Laksmi Narayan Thakur who got permanent settlement and while in possession; his name was finally published in CS khatian. Thereafter, he transferred the suit land to M/s Rally Brothers famous Jute Company under which hundreds of day labourers were working for carrying jute from the jute dealers bepary) boat to the mill. Day laborers used to get their remuneration from the beparies. For staying the day laborers, in 1324 BS on the land of Rally Brothers some temporary huts were constructed with bamboo and tiles. Rally Brothers did not take any rents from the laborers and also the laborers did not pay any rents to the Rally Brothers for staying in the temporary huts. In the cyclone of 1326 BS the temporary huts were totally blown away and in 1328BS the day laborers, despite obstruction raised by Rally Brothers, erected some kacha structures for their living. Rally Brothers tried to evict them but fail. In this way, the predecessors of the plaintiffs acquired title by adverse possession. On 17-9-1996 defendant No.6 invite tender in Daily Janakantha for selling 'ka' schedule land to the highest bidder. This tendered as not noticed by the plaintiffs. Defendant No.5 and others participated in the tender and defendant No.6 accepted the tender of defendant No.5. Defendant No.5 after purchase of 'ka' schedule land as aforesaid, now tried to dispossess the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs are in possession on the suit land for more than 70 years and acquired title by adverse possession, as such, defendant No.6 has no authority to sell the suit land. It has been prayed in the suit that:- 

 3. The case of defendant Nos. 1 to 3, 6 and 7 is that, Rally Brothers was an old and famous jute company and the suit property is coolie shade of Rally Brothers. Rally Brothers proposes to sell the suit property to the Government of Bangladesh. On 23-2-1977 agreement was arrived and pursuant to the said agreement, Rally Brothers delivered possession of the suit property to the Government. In 1965, under ordinance No. 30, the suit property vested under Ministry of Jute and Textile Corporation as acquired property Cell (Rally) Special Property (jute) along with other properties. After installation of Bangladesh Jute Corporation, the schedule property was posted under the Jute Corporation. Jute Corporation took up management and control of the property and obtained decree against Rally Brothers and execution of the decree got kabala registered through Court. Governments by ordinance No. 24 of 1993 dismantle/abolish the Jute Corporation and all properties were vested under the Jute Ministry. For selling the suit property earlier three tender were called for but the price having not been up to the mark, it was put for further tender on 30-9-1996 and it was sold to the highest bidder defendant No.5 at Taka 21,74,544. The defendant No.5 paid the entire money on 1-2-1996. On 4-2-1997 and 16-2-1997 the suit land was handed over to the defendant No.5. As per SA record, Rally Brothers were recorded as land lord in Dag No. 257. The entire land was recorded in the name of Rally Brothers'. Jute office staff quarters, collie shade and some of the staffs living in the staff quarters possession were delivered to defendant No.5. The persons living there are on permission from defendant No.5. Plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in of the suit and the plaintiffs acquired no title by adverse possession. 

 4. The case of defendant No.4 is that the suit land was originally belonged to Rally Brothers' in whose name the SA khatian and RS khatian No. 290 were prepared and was finally published. The plaintiffs, 71 in numbers, most of them are false and imaginary and failed to mention how the predecessors of them was living in the suit land specifically in the plaint nor they described in the plaint as to whose heirs are they. It is admitted fact that the suit land belonged to Rally Brothers' and Rally Brothers proposed to sell the suit land to the Government on 23-2-1977 and there was an agreement for sell and thereafter the possession of the suit land was delivered to Government of Bangladesh and Government of Bangladesh filed the suit praying for decree against the Rally Brothers and suit was decreed and pursuant to the decree Government of Bangladesh through Court got possession and become the absolute owner/holder of the suit property. Government of Bangladesh after selling the suit land to defendant No.5, delivered possession of the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The case of defendant No.5, is that the suit land was acquired property from Rally Brothers' and Government after taking control and management of the suit property and pursuant to the agreement dated 23-2-1977, obtained decree from Court and thereafter, in Ordinance No. 30 of 1985 the suit land was put under the control of the Ministry of Jute and Textile of the Government of Bangladesh as acquired property cell (Rally) and Special property cell (jute). After abolishing of the industrial units and converted into Bangladesh Jute Corporation, the properties of Rally Brothers was placed under the Ministry of Jute and thereafter, it was put into auction. Government of Bangladesh on 15-7-1996 registered the kabala through Court. By Ordinance No. 24 of 1993 after abolishing the jute corporation, the property of Jute Corporation was taken under the control of Ministry of Jute and Ministry of Jute through tender sell the suit land to this defendant as highest bidder at Taka 21, 74,544 and this defendant paid entire tendered money on 1- 12-1996. The suit property was handed over to the defendant No.5 on 4-2-1997 and 16-2-1997. The some of the staffs of Rally Brothers-living to the suit property on permission while the possession of the property was delivered in favour of the defendant No.5. Plaintiffs have no right, title or permission in the suit property. 

 6. Learned Judge framed six issues, i.e. whether the suit is maintainable in its present form, whether the suit is' barred by limitation, whether the plaintiffs acquired title by possession over the suit land, whether the tender notice is illegal, what the other relief or relives plaintiffs are entitled and whether plaintiffs entitled to get the decree. 

 7. Learned Judge dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs holding that the plaintiffs did not acquire any title by adverse possession. Against this finding plaintiffs filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 203 of 1999. 

 8. Learned Judge after dismissing the suit directed for selling the suit land to the plaintiffs. Against this finding defendant No.5, filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 48 of 1999. 

 9. Learned Judge also found some irregularities in the tender. Against which defendant No.4 filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 330 of 1999. 

 11. Mr Probir Halder, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants of Appeal No. 203 of 1999, submits that, the plaintiffs having been proved that they are in the suit land from 1326 BS, the Rally Brothers tried to dispossess the plaintiffs but failed to dispossess the plaintiffs, as such the possession of the plaintiffs against original owner of the suit property running notoriously adversely and hastily thereby the plaintiffs acquired a good title against the original owner, Rally Brothers, by adverse possession, as such, the learned Judge committed illegality in not decreeing the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiffs being poor illiterate, as such, they have no knowledge of the auction purchase pursuant to the notification dated 17-9-1996 published in The Daily Janakantha and by this purchase, defendant No.5 acquired no title over the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that, the plaintiffs being in possession, the suit property ought to have been hand over to the plaintiffs and the learned Judge having found possession of the plaintiffs against the original owner Rally Brothers running more than statutory period of limitation committed no illegality in directing for selling the suit property to the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate submits that on the fact of the given case this portion of the judgment should not be set-aside. 

 12. Mr MA Azim Khair, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant of First Appeal No. 48 of 1999, submits that, learned judge having been found the plaintiffs did not acquire any title by adverse possession acted illegally in passing a decree directing the Government to sell the suit property to the plaintiffs there by vested right of this defendant as auction purchaser has illegally been taken away, as such the judgment and order to the effect the direction to the Government to sell the suit land to the plaintiffs should be set-aside. 

 13. Mr Md Mohiuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant of First Appeal No. 330 of 1999, submits that, the suit land after vesting in the Government pursuant to the decree obtained by the Government against its original owner Rally Brothers, and thereafter, the suit land was vested in the Ministry of Jute pursuant to the ordinance of 1983 and since then suit land being totally managed and controlled by this defendant No.4 and the suit land having been sold in auction under notification dated 17-9-1996, there being no objection from anyone and after it put into auction for three times, as such, this portion of the judgment directed the Government to sell the suit property to the plaintiffs was passed illegally and not sustainable in law. 

 14. Although learned Judge' dismissed the claimed of the plaintiffs as to acquire of title by adverse possession but since the learned Judge directed the Government to sell the property to the plaintiffs as the plaintiffs are in possession, as such, the possession of the plaintiffs is to be considered first. It is the case of the plaintiffs that their predecessors went into possession at first on permission from Rally Brothers. Thereafter, a storm blown away their cutcha strictures and they by their own money again constructed shed/hut for their living on the suit land. From the own averments of the plaintiffs it appears that excepting permissive possession, there is nothing in their favour to hold that their possession is of their own. A person may be in possession for more than statutory period of limitation but if it is permissive possession none accrued any title excepting his possession under the original owner and, as such, permissive possession in no way give any benefit and such possession of a person is in fact actual possession of the owner of the suit land in which he is in possession. The land lord has every right to thrown him out of possession any time either with or without notice. Moreover, we find that none of the khatian prepared in the name of plaintiffs. CS porch was prepared in the name of Rally Brothers. It is their case that they has become more dangerous to the plaintiffs when it is found are not in employment of the Rally Brothers, but they were under the employment of "bepary' or merchant who brought Jute to Rally Brothers and the plaintiffs only carried the jute from the boat to the mill and they have been paid by the "bepari" that is boat men not by Rally Brothers, as such, they have acquired no right against the purchased not against the Rally Brothers. On a reference to the depositions of PWs 1,2, 3, 4 and 5 it appears that none of them could say from which date they are in possession of the suit land. 

 "By adverse possession I understand to the meant possession by a person holding the land on his own behalf (or on behalf) of some person other than the true owner, the true owner having a right to immediate possession. If by this adverse possession the statute is set funning, and it continues to run for twelve years, then the title of the true owner is extinguished and the person in possession becomes the owner." 

 17. It has been held by all the Courts of this Sub-Continent that to get title by adverse possession, the possession not only open but it is hastily notoriously runs against its true owner beyond statutory period of limitation. It is held in the case of Hazera Begum vs Rowshan Ara Begum, 39 DLR (AD) 22 that apparent show of adverse possession not sufficient to defeat the title of real owner. Moreover, whatever claim made by the plaintiffs on adverse possession is against Rally Brothers not against Government. After purchase by the Government of the suit land, plaintiffs become unauthorized possessor from the date of acquiring title by the Government and Title by adverse possession can be acquired when possession runs adversely within notice of the land lord. To acquire title by unauthorized possession against Government it requires 60 years which start from 1993 not before that. We find learned Judge perfectly and rightly dismissed the suit.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 922 of 2003
parties:
Bijoy Kumar Sarbabidya ---- Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Judgment Bangladesh & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Bijoy Kumar Sarbabidya, the predecessor   of the petitioners, filed the above-suit for declaration of title in the suit land on the averments, inter alia, that Surendra Chandra Ghosal, father of the defendant No.3 and Dijendra Chandra Ghosal proforma defendant No.4, on 30.8.1947, entered into an agreement for sale of the suit land to him for a consideration of Tk.1,00,000/- and he having paid a sum of Tk. 95,000/-, on that very date as part performance of contract the vacant possession of the suit land along with title documents, khatians etc. were delivered to the plaintiff and since then the plaintiff, by constructing his residence and godown in the suit land, had been possessing the same adversely to the exclusion of all for more than the statutory period of limitation; further the plaintiffs having paid all rents and taxes also acquired indefeasible right, title and interest in the suit land; even though Surendra and Dijendra received the balance consideration of Tk. 5000/- they did not execute and register the sale deed in his favour; further the defendant No. 2 created certain papers and documents which clouded his title and hence the suit. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit and filed written statement contending, inter alia, that the alleged agreement for sale dated 30.8.1947 is forged and fabricated; the original owners Surendra and Dijendra having left for India in the year 1965 the suit land, at first, became enemy property and subsequently became vested property and government had been possessing the suit land by leasing out the same to different persons. During the pendency of the suit on 30.5.1999 the respondent Nos. 7 to 9, prayed for being added as defendants stating they took lease of the suit land from the government and had been possessing the suit land by constructing structures and also running their business thereon and on 25.5.2000, two others also prayed or being added as defendants on the ground that they also are the lessees under the government and are in possession of the suit land and their prayer being also allowed, they were added as defendants. 

 4. On appeal the High Court Division, after hearing allowed the appeal holding that the suit for declaration of title under section 53A of Transfer of Property Act as made by (plaintiff) is not maintainable and no case has also be made out for the claim of title on the basis of adverse possession. 

 6. As it appears the High Court Division found that no title deed being executed by the original owners or by any one on their behalf in favour of the plaintiff, no title passed to the plaintiff; though in paragraph 4 of the plaint the plaintiff made an averment about adverse possession but ended by asserting that he has acquired indefeasible right, title and interest in the suit property under section 53-A of the Transfer of the Property Act; none of the P.Ws. made any statement that the plaintiff had been possessing the suit land adversely against the original owners and no prayer was also made for declaration of title on the basis of adverse possession and the plaintiff in the plaint merely prayer for passing a decree declaring the title of the plaintiff in the suit land as its absolute owner though in order to make out a case of adverse possession it must be pleaded that adverse possession commenced and continued against the rightful owner but in the plant no such case of adverse possession was at all pleaded not to speak of proving such adverse possession; in the instant case there is also no evidence as to when the plaintiff started to possess adversely against real owners and when such possession became hostile; P.W.1 in her deposition admitted that even after the full payment no attempt was made to get any document from the original owners and no demand was also made for executants of any documents; the evidence on record shows that the plaintiff claimed to have entered into possession in the suit land on the basis of the agreement and as such the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land is permissive and if possession is found to be permissive at its inception the possessor cannot claim adversely to the grantor of the possession and the question of adverse possession does not arise where there has been no refusal on the part of the proposed vendor to execute the sale-deed and the possession of the vendee may be permissive even if the vendor has received the entire consideration money; the principle laid down in the cases of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), petitioner in C.R No. 372 of 1999 and Abdur Rashim vs. Md. Rezauddin Pk and others in reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 on which the learned Advocate of the petitioner relied in support of his contention that exhibit-23 has a presumption of correctness, is not applicable in the instant case as the very execution of exhibit-23 having not been proved by sufficient and competent evidence the provisions of section 90 of the Evidence Act regarding presumption of genuineness of document which is 30 years old, has no manner of application in the instant case; the case of Md. Ashraf Ali and another-vs. Fatiq Chandra Saha and others reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 315 and the case of Santipada Datta & others-vs. Satish Chandra Das and others reported in 54 DLR(AD) 173 relied on by the learned advocate for the petitioner to substantiate his contention that the plaintiff can maintain the suit for declaration of his title on the basis of adverse possession, is not also applicable in the instant case since no case of adverse possession has been made out in the plaint in that regard and in the plaint no prayer was sought for declaration of title on the basis of adverse possession and further the trial court did not decree the suit on the basis of adverse possession but under section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act though the provisions of section 53-A does not create any title in the property but only protects the right of the transferee in part performance of contract; the plaintiff though adduced certain evidence of possession but could not prove any paper in support of payment of rent to the municipality immediately after the agreement though in the plaint it was stated that the title deeds and khatians were handed over by the original owners to the plaintiff at the time of execution of the agreement of sale and delivery of possession but no such document or khatian of the original owner have been proved in this case and the papers produced have no nexus with the delivery of possession on 30.8.1947; the plaintiff also failed to make out a case of their very entry in the suit land; the contents of exhibit-A show that the added respondents are the lessees under the government; further in the plaint the area of suit land was originally shown as 6 acres but subsequently by amendments one after another the area was ultimately reduced to only .79 acres; moreover the description of the suit being vague and indefinite no decree could be passed in the absence of any local investigation; the suit as framed is not maintainable as neither exhibit-1 nor exhibit-23 have been proved by sufficient evidence.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Government of Bangladesh represented by the DC and others ----- Defendants-Respondents-Petitioners 
Vs. 
Anjum Nahar Khatun ----- Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-10-97 and 21-10-97 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Satkhira, in Title Appeal No. 188 of 1995 allowing the appeal and decreeing the suit and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 29-10-95 and 6-11-95 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Satkhira Sadar, in Title Suit No. 415 of 1990 dismissing the suit should not be set aside. 

 2. The brief fact of the case is that the opposite party as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 415 of 1990 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Satkhira against the present petitioner and others for declaration of title of the suit lands and for further declaration that the vested property list relating to suit lands is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff, which was dismissed on contest. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff-appellant-opposite party, in short, is that, the suit land along with other lands appertaining to CS plot No. 247 originally belonged to Murali Dhar Chattapadhya who settled the land by postdated 11-8-39 in favour of Ashalata Das and others who sold the same by the registered kabala dated 26-4-47 to Hari Sadhan and this Hari Sakhan sold 1.87 acres of land including the suit land to plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 2-9-70 and delivered the possession. 

 7. The further case of the petitioner is that plaintiff has no title and possession over the suit land but filed the instant false suit by creating a forged and fabricated kabala which is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 9. The plaintiff-appellant-opposite party being aggrieved by the judgment and decree preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Satkhira being Title Appeal No. 188 of 1995. 

 14. Abdul Haque Dhali, the husband of the plaintiff Anjum Nahar Khatun, was examined as PW 2 who stated in his evidence that the suit property was purchased by his wife Anjum Nahar Khatun by a registered kabala dated 2-9-70 from one Hari Sadhan and produced the certified copy of the purchase deed which was exhibited as Exhibit 4. He further stated in his evidence that as the original deed was lost he could not produce the original deed. 

 15. Mostab Ali Halder, a permanent Moharar of Sub-Registry office was examined as PW 1 who brought the volume from Sub-Registry office to prove the genuineness of the certified copy of the purchase deed. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the plaintiff claims her right and title over the suit land on the basis of the title deed. Next he submits that mere producing a certified copy of a deed and calling for the volume from Sub-Registry office does not necessarily mean to prove the execution of a deed. The PW 2 stated in his evidence that Hari Sadhan is still living in Bangladesh and they are living in the same village and the distance of the house of Hari Sadhan and the plaintiff is about 10/12 cubit hands, as such, to prove the genuineness of the document, the plaintiff ought to have produced Hari Sadhan as witness but plaintiff failed to produce Hari Sadhan to prove the execution of the deed. The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submits that as a matter of fact Hari Sadhan left for India long before, as such, his property was treated as enemy property and subsequently, vested property by operation of law. In support of his contention the learned Counsel relying on the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian Vested Property, Chandpur, reported in 39 DLR (AD) 223 wherein it has been held that : 

 16. The learned Counsel next submits that it is the duty of the plaintiff to prove his case beyond all reasonable doubt. The initial onus lies on the plaintiff to prove his title according to his claim over the suit land. In this connection, the learned Counsel cited another decision in the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian, Vested Property, Sandspur reported in 39 DLR (AD) 224 wherein it is stated that: 

 "The plaintiff is claiming his title to the suit land on the basis of a deed of gift. I have got no doubt in my mind that the initial onus was on him to prove his title. The observation made in 32 DLR (AD) 29 would be of no avail to the appellant, as he failed to discharge his initial onus by proving his document of title. Had he succeeded to do so then the onus would have shifted on the enemy property authority to prove that the executants of the plaintiff's document, the sons of Surendra Mohan Saha, were residing in an enemy country at the relevant time." 

 17. The learned Counsel further submits that the plaintiff has got no title and possession over the suit land and the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his title and also possession. Although the plaintiff claims that she is in possession of the suit land and produced two rent receipts, one of 1986 and another of 1990, that is not the proof of his possession. Next he submits although the plaintiff claims that he has mutated his name by Mutation Case No. 1060/74 but the plaintiff could not produce any certified copy of mutated khatian or any rough paper of mutated khatian. Finally, the learned Counsel submits that the Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) (Repeal) Act, 1974 which is known as Act No. XLV of 1974 wherein section 3 savings-(1) reads as follows : 

 20. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr Md Asadullah, appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent-opposite party submits that the suit property is not an enemy property, because the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 2-9-70 purchased the suit property from Hari Sadhan, the original owner of the suit property. The plaintiff since the purchase was owning and possessing the suit property but abruptly the vested property authority treated the said property in the list of vested property vide VP Case No. 1 600 (Kali)/ 8081. The learned Counsel next submits that the plaintiff has mutated his name vide Mutation case No. 1060/74 and paid rent upto 1387 BS. Hari Sadhan, the vendor of the plaintiff, is a permanent citizen of Bangladesh who never went to India and is still living in Bangladesh, as such, his property cannot be treated as vested property in the year 1980. The plaintiff thereafter submitted a prayer before the ADC (Revenue) for releasing the property from the list of the vested property. On the prayer of the plaintiff, the ADC (Revenue) after perusing the record and connected papers recommended to the Ministry of Land that the property does not come within the purview of vested property list, as such, the suit property may be released from the list of the vested property. The learned Counsel further submits that after the repeal of Ordinance No. 1 of 1969 no property could be declared as enemy or vested property. This suit property was declared as vested property in the year 1980 which is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction and ultra virus to the Enemy Property Repeal Act of 1974. The learned Counsel in support of his contention cited the case of Saju Hosein and others vs Bangladesh and another reported in 58 DLR (AD) 177 wherein it has been held that: 

 22. On a meticulous examination of the evidence on record, certified copy of the registered deed, the judgments of both the courts below and other connected papers, it transpires that the learned trial Court in his judgment discussed the evidence and also perused the certified copy of the registered deed produced by the plaintiff and made his clear observation that the certified copy of the registered deed by the plaintiff dated 2-9-70 which was exhibited as Exhibit 1 (ka) was not the original deed. The PW 2, the husband of the plaintiff, stated in his evidence that the original deed by which the plaintiff purchased the suit land from Hari Sadhan was lost, as such, the certified copy of the original deed as secondary evidence was produced and exhibited as Exhibit 1 (ka). 

 23. The plaintiff examined as many as 6 witnesses in this case to prove the case. Shahamat Ali Karikar was examined as PW 3 who was said to be an attesting witness. The learned trial Court observed that since the original deed was not produced his signature could not be compared with original deed. PW 2 stated in his evidence that the vendor of the plaintiff Hari Sadhan never went to India and still he is living in Bangladesh and Hari Sadhan has been living in the same village of the plaintiff and in that case the plaintiff ought to have examined Hari Sadhan to prove the genuineness of the registered kabala dated 2-9-70. The recommendation made by the ADC (Revenue) to release the property from the list of the vested property has got no basis because although the plaintiff claimed that she was possessing the suit land by mutating her name by Mutation Case No. 1060/74 but the plaintiff could not produce any certified copy of the mutation khatian or any rough mutation khatian. The plaintiff produced 2 rent receipts, one of 1986 and another of 1990, but the claim of the plaintiff is that he purchased the land in the year 1970 but no rent receipt except in 1986 and 1990 could be produced by the plaintiff. The trial Court rightly observed that the plaintiff had no continuous possession over the suit land. The plaintiff's case has got two phases: first phase of the plaintiff's case is that the plaintiff purchased the suit land from Hari Sadhan by a registered kabala dated 2-9-70 and the second phase is to treat the property as vested property. Thereafter, while the plaintiff was enjoying the property, abruptly in the year 1980 the vested property authority treated this property as vested property and enlisted the property in the vested property list and thereafter, leased out the suit property to one Nur Mohammad vide VP Case No. 600 (kali)/ 8081. Now the question is, whether the plaintiff has been able to prove his title over the suit property by the certified copy of the kabala dated 2-9-70. In this connection, I like to rely on the case of Sova Rani Guha alias Sova Rani Gupta vs Abdul Awal Miah and others reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 257 wherein it has been held that section 63—Secondary evidence —"The production of the certified copy of a sale deed does not by itself warrant the presumption of due execution of the original document A party producing the Secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution of the original. Even in a case where a document has been exhibited without objection the court is to be satisfied as to the execution of the document." In the instant case, to prove the genuineness of the document onus is upon the plaintiff to produce Hari Sadhan who executed the deed in absence of the original one but the plaintiff could not produce Hari Sadhan before the court as witness. The lower appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial Court ought to have assigned in his judgment justifying the reason in reversing the judgment of the trial Court, particularly in respect of the title deed. But the lower appellate Court in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court did not assign any cogent reason and also did not consider the evidence on record, particularly the evidence of PW 2 affecting the merit of the case. In this connection, I like to rely on the decision in the case of Most Mohsina Khatun vs Ms Habib Knitting Mills reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 47 wherein it is stated that while reversing the judgment of the trial Court the appellate Court is required to reverse the material findings of the trial Court with reference to evidence on record. The judgment of the trial Court transpires that in arriving at its finding the said Court carefully considered the material facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, both oral and documentary, and the certified copy of the original title deed of the plaintiff. The learned trial Court did not commit any error of law and illegality in arriving at its finding because the plaintiff could not be able to prove his case. The lower appellant Court without considering the evidence on record and without proper assessment of the evidence and also without considering the title deed was not proved and came to an erroneous finding which is liable to be interfered by this Court. In this connection, I rely on the decision in the case of Hasan Ahmed Chowdhury vs Md Nurul Amin and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162 wherein it has been held that— 

 25. From the discussion made above and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal position, the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-10-97 and 21-10-97 respectively passed by learned District Judge, Satkhira, in Title Appeal No. 188 of 1995 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is hereby set aside and the Judgment and decree of the trial Court is affirmed.

Vs
Bangladesh and others  ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
3. Plaint case, in short, is that one Tamej Sheikh was owner in possession of 3 decimals of land including the suit land, which was accordingly record in his name in CS Khatian No. 315. Tamej Sheikh transferred said land to Nandalal Das and Bateswar Das, sons of Mohan Das and delivered possession. SA record of rights was separately prepared in their names. By a registered deed of sale dated 24-12-69 Nandalal Das then transferred the suit land to Md Chan Miah. Md Chan Miah by registered sale deed dated 22-12-76 transferred said land to Alimul Hyder and handed over possession. When Alimul Hyder was thus owner in possession, he by two separate deeds of sale dated 27-6-81 and 15-11-82 transferred the suit land to the plaintiff and delivered her possession. The plaintiff got her name mutated and possessed on payments of rents. 

 4. The suit land was then recorded first in the name of Chan Miah in RS Khatian and then as khas in the name of the government. Defendant No. 2 Additional Divisional Commissioner (Revenue) served a notice dated 30-12-90 upon the husband of the plaintiff asking him to vacate the land by 30-1-91 otherwise he would be evicted therefrom by removal of unauthorised structures. Such notice cast a doubt over the title of the plaintiff who was accordingly, constrained to institute the suit. 

 5. Defendant No. 2 alone contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case, in short, is that the suit land was within Ramchandrapur hat of the erstwhile 'Zaminder.' With the wholesale acquisition of land receiving interest under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land vested in the government. RS record of rights accordingly recorded the suit land as khas of the government. The suit land was situated at the periphery of Ramchandrapur Bazaar. By purchase from persons who had no title the plaintiff acquired no right title or interest in the suit land. Husband of the plaintiff got the suit land mutated in collusion with corrupt 'Tahshilder' and such mutation had no legal effect. 

 10. Mr Md Haroon-ar Rashid, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the plaintiff proved her title and possession in the suit land by both oral and documentary evidence while the defendant failed to prove that the suit land vested in the government and the trial Court correctly decreed the suit but the appellate Court set aside said decree without considering the evidence on record. 

 12. The plaint case is that the suit land originally belonged to one Tamej Sheikh and CS record of rights was accordingly, prepared in his name. CS Khatian No. 315, Exhibit 1 recorded the suit land comprising of CS plot No. 828 as 'Nal'. Nature of tenancy was recorded as 'Borga Korfa' under land receiver Durga Sundari Basu and others. The appellant Court took the view that such tenancy held as 'Barga Korfa' had no 'raiyati' right, had no right to transfer before the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 came into force. He however, did not mention any law or authority in support of his view. 

 15. When the nature of tenancy was recorded as 'Barga Korfa' the intention was very clear that it was not a simple interest of 'Barga' as we popularly understand. Such tenancy was definitely heritable and transferable. 

 16. But in the absence of any material on record the appellate Court held that such tenancy 

 17. It must also be noted that the land was recorded as a 'Nal' land. Immediate superior rent receiver was Durga Sundari Basu and others, not Ramchandrapur Zamindars. 

 19. Plaintiff adduced original title deeds of Chand Miah and Alimul Hyder, Exhibits 3 and 4. She also adduced SA Khatian No. 787 which recorded the suit land in SA plot No. 2859 as 'Chandina' in the names of Nandalal and Bateswar, Exhibit 2. 

 22. Recording of the suit land as 'Chandina' in SA record of rights might have created all problems for the appellate Court. Such record was prepared sometime in 1964. With the wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest, all land "in a hat or bazaar" vested in the government with effect from 2 April, 1956. But under sub-section 3 of section 44  of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 such land would stand finally acquired and vested in the government with effect from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of a notification in the official Gazette declaring that the Compensation Assessment-roll was finally published. 

 23. During the CS survey, the land was recorded as 'Nal'. With the passage of time when the bazaar in question expanded up to near the suit land, the recorded tenant might have made shops thereon for some quick bucks. With further extension of the bazaar, the shops might be now in the periphery of Ramchandrapur bazaar as claimed by defendant No.2. Land in the periphery cannot be deemed to be 'in the hat or bazaar' within the meaning of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Such land was therefore never intended by the legislature to vest in the government under section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The defendant therefore, failed to produce any notification of final Compensation Assessment-roll vesting the suit land in the government. 

 26. Send down the record at once.

Al Baraka Bank Bangladesh Ltd ------ Appellant
Vs
Rina Alam and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Defendant No. 1 Al Baraka Bank presented the appeal against the decree dated 26-11-2001 passed by the Joint District Judge and First Commercial Court at Dhaka in Title Suit No.197 of 2001, which decreed the suit. 

 2. Respondent No.1 as plaintiff on 14-7-97 instituted Title Suit No. 208 of 97 against the appellant bank and another for a decree of declaration that the plaintiff owed no amount to said bank on account of any loan and that the plaintiff had no liability with the bank; and that so-called memorandum or deposit of title deeds dated 17-3-88 was manufactured, forged and inoperative and that the plaintiff was entitled to get back her title deed No. 788 as described in the schedule to the plaint; and also for direction for return of said title deed and for compensation of Taka 75,00,000 as damages. The suit was ultimately, renumbered as aforesaid Title Suit No. 197 of 2001. 

 5. Said bank instituted a suit in the court of Artha Rin Adalat showing said property of the plaintiff mortgaged for the loan advanced to the Coast Marine Line Ltd. It was a public limited company and one AB Siddique was the managing director of the company, The bank fraudulently created a memorandum of deposit of title deeds dated 17-3-88 and an agreement for creating further charge dated 9-3-89 behind 'the back of the plaintiff. The plaintiff never executed any such memorandum of deposit of title deeds and/or the agreement. Neither the plaintiff nor her husband was a director or a share holder of the company. She had no interest in the company. Neither the plaintiff nor her husband was connected in any way with the company. 

 7. Denying the plaint case defendant No. 1 bank contested the suit by filing a written statement. Main defence case is that on 29-2-88 one AB Siddique Ludu applied for Bai-Muajjal facility to the bank for purchase of two ships and also for adjustment of the loan of Taka 99,50,000 and offered to mortgage the property of the plaintiff which was given in mortgage against the loans of Shawkat Ali. Defendant bank sanctioned Bai-Muajjal facility and in terms of the facility the plaintiff on 17-3-88 executed a memorandum of deposit of title deeds and deposited the original lease deed dated 28-10-66 and original deed of sale dated 22-2-73 in the bank. On 17-3-88 Mr AB Siddique Ludu also executed other charge documents. Thereafter, the plaintiff executed the agreement to create further charge on 9-3-89. The Coast Marine Line Ltd having failed to adjust the loan of Taka 1,33,70,592 the bank instituted Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 then renumbered as Title Suit No. 113 of 2000 in the 4th Court of Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka. The plaintiff could not get back the schedule deed before adjustment of the loan of Coast Marine Line Ltd. 

 5. What relief the plaintiff was entitled to? 

 11.	Defendant No. 2 was the son of her husband's elder brother. She gave the deed to said defendant No. 2 in trust in connection with his business. But he obtained some loan facility keeping deposit of said deed in the bank. He told her that he obtained loan in connection with his business of Gold Star Lines, and Trans Bangla Shipping Line. He was the sole proprietor of those firms. The Bank obtained a general power of attorney in respect of the loans from her and she executed and registered said power of attorney on 22-6-87 through commission. The power was given in respect of said Gold Star Lines and Trans Bangla Shipping Co only. Besides that document she did not execute any other document. Defendant No. 2 already paid off entire loan with interest to the bank. The Bank informed her by issuing two non liability certificates dated 13-7-92 Exhibit 1 and 1(ka). Defendant No. 2 gave her the certificates saying he already adjusted the loans and assured her to return the original deed. Her property was never mortgaged in respect of any other loan. 

 13.	In cross examination, she stated she was impleaded as defendant No.4 in Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 brought by defendant No. 1 bank in the Artha Rin Adalat. After receipt of summons, she came to know about the suit. Before receipt of the summons, she had no knowledge about Coast Marine Lines Ltd. She did not mortgage any of her property against any loan of said company. There was no question to know as she had no knowledge whether the company obtained loan from the bank. She did not execute so-called memorandum of deposit of title deeds. Defendant bank had no claim or loan against her. The bank never informed her about why the bank kept her document in its custody. She did not lodge any 'Ijhar' for not returning by the bank of the deed. 

 16. PW 2 Serajul Alam, husband of the plaintiff, deposed that the plaintiff deposited her title deed in question against the loans of Gold Star Lines and Trans Bangla Shipping Co. Shawkat Ali was the proprietor of both' firms. Shawkat Ali already paid off the loans on 17-11-88. Property was mortgaged in 1987. Defendant then issued certificates of non-liabilities in favour of Shawkat Ali on 13-7-88. Then he thought to purchase a company like Pan Asia Lines. He obtained a deed of agreement for loan against the proposed company but ultimately, did not obtain any facility. Proposed loan was also not disbursed since Pan Asia Lines ultimately was not brought into existence. He on behalf of his wife demanded return of the deed. On 17-12-92 she demanded in writing return of the deed. But the bank did not reply. 

 17. He stated that the property of his wife was not mortgaged in connection with the loan of Coast Marine Line Ltd. His wife was made unnecessary party because she had no connection with Coast Marine Line Ltd. He saw the signature on the Memorandum of deposit of title deed and that was not the signature of his wife. That was created by the bank. The bank withheld the deed illegally. They suffered heavy loss for want of the deed. He could not do business nor develop the land. Signature on said memorandum of deposit of title deeds did not tally with any of the signatures of his wife in the papers of the bank filed. 

 18. In cross-examination, he stated that they were 4 brothers alive. AB Siddique Ludu was his brother. Coast Marine Line Ltd obtained loan of Taka 99,50,000 from the defendant bank. Then he said he had no knowledge. He denied that the property of his wife was mortgaged to secure said loan of Taka 99,50,000. He had no knowledge of Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 of the 4th Court of Artha Rin Adalat. Then he said he heard that there was a suit and his wife along with others submitted written statement. 

 20. Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 against Coast Marine Line Ltd was pending in the 4th Court of Artha Rin Adalat. Property of the suit was shown mortgaged there. The plaintiff was impleaded as defendant. In the written statement it was stated that the property remained mortgaged up to 17-11-88. He denied that he was the real owner of the firms of Shawkat Ali and that he got the suit instituted through the plaintiff. On 29-2-88 he applied for loan and in the application security were mentioned, that was not executed. To the question of court he replied that he proposed to mortgage one concrete built house valued at Taka 1 (one) crore and thereby nothing mentioned, his house or any particular house. 

 22. In cross-examination, he stated that he was working in the defendant bank since 1990, after the questioned transactions. He deposed in Title Suit No. 113 of 2000 of the Fourth Court of Artha Rin Adalat. The suit property was once mortgaged. He saw the charge document of March, 1988 executed by Rina Alam. He could not say whether the property was still mortgaged on 17-11-88. 

 26. On the evidence, oral and documentary, learned Joint District Judge by impugned judgment and decree decreed the suit in part and declared that loans taken on behalf of Ms Gold Star Lines and M/S Trans Bangla Shipping Lines were adjusted on 17-11-88 and further declared that memorandum of deposit of title deed dated 17-3-88 was created, forged, fraudulent and ineffective; and directed defendant No.1 bank to return schedule title deed No. 788 along with other documents to the plaintiff. 

 27. Mr Sayyid Shahid Hussain, learned Advocate for the appellant bank, submitted that learned Joint District Judge failed to consider the loan application Exhibit 6, sanction advice exhibit-C, original deeds of title of Rina Alam filed by the bank Exhibits H, I, and J to J(7), memorandum of deposit of title deed Exhibit E, deed to create further charge Exhibit L and oral evidence which conclusively and clearly proved that the plaintiff mortgaged the suit property to the bank again and thereby, erred in law in decreeing the suit. 

 31. In view of the conflicting submissions, the questions as to (a) whether the plaintiff further mortgaged her property by deposit of her title deeds and (b) whether the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat dated 24-5-2001 would act and/or operate as res judicata for the present suit are the moot issues facing us. 

 33.	As stated above, the plaintiff deposited her title deed No. 788 creating mortgage to secure the loans of Gold Star Lines and Trans Bangla Shipping Lines. Said loans were admittedly liquidated on 17-11-88. Said deed was also offered as a security against a proposed project of Pan Asia Lines. But the project did not ultimately materialise. On 13-7- 92 the bank issued two certificates stating that the loans were fully adjusted on 17-11-88, Exhibits 1 and 1(K). Then, the plaintiff on 17-12-92 wrote a letter addressed to the bank for return of her title documents, which the bank received on 19-12-92. 

 34. The case of the bank is that, during the continuance of the mortgage the plaintiff further mortgaged the property to secure Bai-muajjal facility for an amount of Taka 99,50,000 sanctioned to the Coast Marine Line Ltd by executing a memorandum of deposit of title deed on 17-3-88, Exhibit E. She further executed a deed of agreement for creating further charges dated 9-3-89, Exhibit L. 

 36. Clause (f) of section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act defines mortgage by deposit of title-deeds as follows, 

 "Where a person delivers to a creditor or his agent documents of title to immovable property, with intent to create a security thereon, the transaction is called a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds." 

 37. In order to create a mortgage by deposit of title deeds, 

 39. Defendant bank examined one of its officers who joined the bank in 1990. He had no knowledge about the execution of the memorandum of deposit of title deeds and the agreement for creating further charge. He said that he deposed on the basis of the record. So, there is practically no evidence on record to prove execution by the plaintiff of either the memorandum of deposit of title deeds or the agreement for creating further charges, exhibit E and L respectively. 

 44. Mr Shahid submitted strenuously that if the plaintiff had not created further charge on the deeds why she did not take any step for return of the deeds. He also claimed that the copy of the letter dated 19-12-92 was created by her. In the facts and circumstances of the case, such wild suggestion is not at all accepted. It is on record that after adjustment of the loans of Gold Star Lines and Trans Bangla Shipping Lines, another project of Pan Asia Lines for purchase of two vessels from London was submitted by Serajul Alam and others and property of the plaintiff was offered as collateral. As project did not materialise, the plaintiff demanded return of her title deeds by letter dated 17-12-92 which the bank received by putting the round seal of the bank. The balk did never deny the seal. Nor any step was taken to prove the seal forged. 

 45. The plaintiff deposited her original deeds in trust with the bank. The bank was required to take utmost care in dealing with such security, particularly in making further charge on the deeds. Admittedly, the bank never approached the plaintiff nor obtained any consent oral or written of the plaintiff for making further charge on the document. Such conduct is not becoming with the banking ethics, customs and practice. What disturbed us most how a bank could have created without any consent of the plaintiff further security on the deed already deposited in the bank in connection with and continuance of another loan. 

 46. In the circumstances, we find no reason to differ with the views of the learned Joint District Judge that the plaintiff did not execute the memorandum of deposit of title deed dated 17-3-88 Exhibit E or the agreement for further charge dated 9-3-89 Exhibit Land that she did not further mortgage her property to secure the loan of Ms Coast Marine Lines Ltd. " 

 "No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such court." 

 50. On 30-10-92 the bank instituted Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 before the Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka and on 14-7-97 the plaintiff instituted her Title Suit No. 208 of 1997 before the Fifth Court of Subordinate Judge at Dhaka. After five years, the suit of the plaintiff was instituted. Cause of action for the suit of the plaintiff arose only when the bank refused to return the deed in question and therefore, not same as that of the suit of the bank. Relief sought for in the suits is not the same. Both suits continued side by side before two forums for a pretty good time. No step was taken by the bank either before the civil Court or Artha Rin Adalat to stay further proceedings of the subsequent suit. Reason is obvious. Neither the suit before the civil Court could be stayed pending decision of the suit before the Artha Rin Adalat nor the other way round, the suit before the Artha Rin Adalat could be stayed for the suit of the civil Court. 

 53. In the plaint of Artha Rin Suit, the bank just claimed that defendant No. 4, the plaintiff herein, on 17-3-88 created equitable mortgage by deposit of the title deeds of schedule property as suety. The bank did not claim that on 17-3-88 the plaintiff executed a memorandum of deposit of title deed or on 9-3-89 executed the agreement for creating further charge on the deeds in question. The defendants including the plaintiff jointly denied the claim of mortgage. The bank did not suggest any issue on such mortgage and, as such, no issue was framed by the Artha Rin Adalat. The parties, particularly the plaintiff, did not adduce all the evidence that was adduced in the present suit.
